findings.description: workspaceLaunchPayload() (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:3875-3887) builds the new launch payload as {projectId, mode: "from", baseRef?, branch?} with no `strategy`/multi-root marker, inferred solely from the one reported Zod error text. Per docs/playbot-agent-integration.md:423, the `mode` (open/from/copy) vocabulary and `baseRef` field name were previously only used by Playbot's `quick` strategy, documented there as explicit "single-root provisioning" — distinct from the `project` strategy this tool has always relied on for "every project root gets a worktree" (docs/playbot-lanes.md:58). There is no new test exercising a multi-root project against the new schema, and engineReadiness's only root-coverage guard (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:3764) is gated to engine-dependent dispatch on exactly Playbot 0.117.0, so a multi-root project on another version calling create_workspace (or an engineDependent:false dispatch) with the new schema would silently get back a workspace covering only one root if the new schema is in fact single-root, with no error raised.
findings.user_instructions: Firstmate decision for review-1: FIX. Preserve the accepted behavior that every project root gets a worktree, and refuse rather than guess. Installed Playbot 0.124.0 source evidence: /tmp/.mount_PlaybooLajdl/resources/app.asar, .vite/build/main.js. The strict Vj launch workspace schema at byte offset 655551 includes projectId, optional projectRootId, baseRef, branch, mode, and rootOverrides; it has no strategy or name. In async function _D at byte offset 986448, Playbot reads all project roots with se(e.id), maps every root with n.map(...), and defaults non-selected roots to mode "from" while carrying the requested branch. In function MD at byte offset 990518, provisioning passes projectRoots: r into Moe; async function _oe at byte offset 991750 maps every root as well. Cite these packaged source locations and the confirmed multi-root behavior in the PR. Regardless of Playbot version, after create_workspace and dispatch with newWorkspace, verify through the existing bounded root-settle re-read that the created workspace covers every project root exactly once. If it does not, refuse by name and name the created workspace; do not rely on the 0.117-gated engine-readiness check. Add a multi-root new-schema test proving full coverage and refusal. Apply only the selected review-1 finding in this fix round.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The fix is well-evidenced, narrowly scoped, and thoroughly tested for the reported failure and legacy paths, but it ships an unverified assumption about multi-root worktree coverage under Playbot's new schema plus stale documentation, so it's safe to merge to unblock Playbot usage while those two points get confirmed/fixed as follow-ups.

findings.description: The fix round added verifyCreatedWorkspaceRootCoverage() only inside createWorkspace() (lines 3975, 3991 — reached by the create_workspace tool, and by createChat()'s legacy openThread branch), and dispatch already had its own equivalent check via createdWorkspaceFreshness()->workspaceFreshness() at line 6567. But createChat()'s 'launch' branch (lines 4011-4030, used when chatCreationApi() === 'launch', i.e. exactly the new mode-based schema this PR is about) builds the new workspace directly via threads:launch/workspaceLaunchPayload and returns publicThread(resolveThread(...)) with no coverage check at all. This branch is reached directly by the create_chat MCP tool (handler at lines 6496-6499 returns createChat()'s result with no follow-up verification), which is documented at line 6302 as explicitly supporting 'Can create the workspace first via newWorkspace.' Concretely: calling create_chat with newWorkspace on a multi-root project, on a Playbot build using the mode schema, where that schema only provisions one root, returns a successful thread/workspace with silently incomplete root coverage — no error, exactly the failure review-1 was raised to prevent, just reachable through create_chat instead of create_workspace/dispatch. The new tests in this round (tests/fm-playbot-lanes.test.sh single-root fixture) only exercise create_workspace, not create_chat. The earliest shared boundary that would close this is inside createChat()'s 'launch' branch itself (call verifyCreatedWorkspaceRootCoverage when newWorkspace !== undefined, before returning `created`), since both create_chat and dispatch route through createChat().
findings.user_instructions: Firstmate decision for review-3: FIX. This completes the review-1 decision at one missed call site. In createChat()'s launch branch, call verifyCreatedWorkspaceRootCoverage when newWorkspace is set, before returning, so create_chat and dispatch share that boundary. On incomplete coverage, refuse by name and include the created workspace and chat ids. Add a create_chat with newWorkspace case to the single-root test fixture covering both full coverage and the refusal. Do not add other new machinery. Apply only review-3 in this fix round.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The fix round correctly resolves the reported failure (dispatch with newWorkspace erroring on the new mode schema) and adds coverage verification for create_workspace and dispatch, but the same multi-root-coverage protection was not extended to the create_chat tool's own 'launch'-schema branch, leaving one documented, directly-callable entry point able to silently return an incomplete workspace without error.

findings.description: The new kind=lane branch-resolution logic (bin/fm-merge-local.sh:97-103) is unreachable for every real lane task, because the pre-existing gate at bin/fm-merge-local.sh:79 (`[ "$MODE" = local-only ] || exit 1`, reading `mode=` from the task's .meta) runs first and the only production writer of kind=lane records, ensureTerminalLaneIdentity in bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs (~line 5471-5481), never writes a mode= field. I reproduced this directly: building a meta file with exactly the fields that writer produces (kind=lane, spawn_gen, playbot_project/workspace/thread, playbot_desktop/harness_home, project=, worktree=, landing_branch=, and no mode=) and running bin/fm-merge-local.sh against it fails at line 79 with 'error: task ... is mode=, not local-only', before ever reaching the new lane logic. laneMeta() in fm-playbot-lanes.mjs (which enumerates the identity fields a lane record carries) also never mentions mode, confirming this isn't an omission in one call site. The new tests in tests/fm-merge-local.test.sh don't catch this because their shared write_meta helper (lines 36-43) unconditionally injects mode=local-only for every fixture, including the new lane cases, which doesn't reflect how real lane identities are created. As written, this change cannot actually land any Playbot-lane ship task automatically - the stated goal of the PR - because every such task is refused before the lane-specific code runs. Fixing this requires a design decision (e.g. have fm-merge-local.sh treat kind=lane as satisfying/bypassing the mode=local-only requirement, since lane dispatch has no shell-spawn mode step to draw it from; or have the lane identity writer in fm-playbot-lanes.mjs record mode=local-only for local-only lanes) rather than a mechanical patch, so it needs the author's input.
findings.user_instructions: Do not make kind=lane bypass the mode=local-only gate: lanes can also be no-mistakes or direct-PR. Fix upstream in bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs: thread an explicit mode parameter through dispatch into ensureTerminalLaneIdentity exactly as landingBranch is threaded, and persist mode=<value> as a required .meta field. Fail dispatch/identity creation closed when mode is absent; do not default it. Update laneMeta() and the MCP dispatch tool's accepted parameters to include mode. Update tests/fm-merge-local.test.sh write_meta so mode is added only when a fixture explicitly passes it; add a case proving dispatch persists the given mode. Add one line to docs/playbot-lanes.md saying lane dispatch must pass mode for local-only landing. Keep no-mistakes and direct-PR lane behavior unchanged.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The change is mechanically safe (fails closed, well-tested for the scenarios its own fixtures cover) but, based on tracing the only real producer of kind=lane records, the new lane-landing path appears to be dead code in production due to an untouched mode=local-only precondition - meaning the change likely does not accomplish its stated purpose and needs author input before merging.

findings.description: User intent states: "Playbot has updated to 0.128.0 ... Confirm whether 0.128.0 can be trusted the same way, and if so, extend the check so engine-dependent validation can proceed again." The diff instead adds 0.129.0 to every verified-version list/string (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:49-50, 3792, 3800, 3808; docs/playbot-lanes.md:276), and the new tests explicitly assert the opposite of what was requested: tests/fm-playbot-lanes.test.sh:8724-8735 feeds version 0.128.0 and asserts the verdict is 'unconfirmed' and that engine IPC is NOT reached ('unverified 0.128.0 reached engine IPC' / 'fails closed'), with a comment stating 'the earlier reported version remains unverified because this fixture cannot establish its live contract'. So 0.128.0 — the version the Frogpile bug fixes are actually stuck on per the intent — is still rejected after this change; only 0.129.0 gained trust. There is no evidence in the repo (commit message, docs, or code comments) of an investigation establishing that Playbot has since moved to 0.129.0, superseding the 0.128.0 report, or that 0.128.0's IPC contract was checked and found untrustworthy. This is a direct contradiction of the stated required behavior and needs the author to confirm whether this is a deliberate version correction (Playbot actually shipped 0.129.0 by the time of the fix) or a transposition bug (128 typed as 129), since as written the change does not unblock the reported problem.
findings.user_instructions: Firstmate confirms Playbot auto-updated from 0.128.0 to 0.129.0 during this investigation, so 0.129.0 was the live version verified and trusted; 0.128.0 remains unverified. Add one plain line to the commit message stating this provenance and, if natural, to the doc comment. Do not change code or tests.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The change appears to miss its own stated goal: it verifies Playbot 0.129.0 instead of the 0.128.0 version the intent says is blocking tonight's Frogpile bug fixes, and new tests explicitly lock in 0.128.0 remaining unconfirmed/fail-closed, so merging as-is would not resolve the reported incident unless there's an undocumented reason Playbot moved to 0.129.0.

findings.description: The 'already owns duplicates' guard reads only the backlink in `.duplicates`. dedupe writes the duplicate record first and the canonical backlink second. If a run is interrupted between those writes, A is a duplicate of B but B.duplicates is still empty. A later `dedupe B --into C` then passes the guard and creates the A→B→C chain this change is meant to prevent. The window is narrow. The existing interruption test suggests it is a known failure mode, and none of the new tests cover it. Consider also refusing when any record has a duplicate disposition whose reference is this candidate, or repair the missing backlink before the check.
findings.user_instructions: Before the canonical-owns-duplicates guard, scan for any record whose duplicate disposition references the candidate being deduped; treat that as owning duplicates (refuse, naming the members), and if the canonical's backlink list is missing such a member, repair the backlink under the same lock before refusing. Add a regression test that simulates the interrupted first-write state (A marked duplicate of B, B.duplicates empty) and proves dedupe B --into C is refused and the backlink is repaired.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The change adds two narrow guards that refuse chained dedupes, with tests for the chain, retry-after-chain and pre-existing multi-hop cases. The only gap is an interrupted-write window where the backlink is missing.

findings.description: The refusal is opt-in per brief. fm-spawn.sh only runs the open-question check when the brief already contains an `Open-question register:` line, and that line only exists if firstmate passed `--open-questions` to fm-brief.sh. The intent requires that a ship brief for a project with a register must name every dependent question and be refused while any is open. Nothing ties the register to the project, so a brief scaffolded without the flag, or with the section deleted, dispatches unchecked. That is the original incident path: a brief that never mentioned the register. AGENTS.md says to pass the flag 'when the project keeps a register', which leaves detection to firstmate's memory. Consider a project-level register declaration, for example in project metadata, that makes fm-spawn require the section. Otherwise confirm that firstmate-discipline enforcement is the intended scope.
findings.user_instructions:
review-1 (decision from firstmate): make the guarantee project-level. Add one optional project-level register declaration owned by the existing project registry path: data/projects.md parsed by bin/fm-project-mode.sh (its header owns the registry line format). Add one optional field naming the register file relative to the project root (for example an `open-questions <relative path>` clause in the entry's description, parsed the same way the existing "at /path" clause is, with a query mode such as `fm-project-mode.sh --open-questions <project>` that prints the declared path or nothing; missing/duplicate/ambiguous entries behave as that script already defines). bin/fm-brief.sh must emit the `# Open-question dependencies` section automatically for a ship brief whose project declares a register (keep --open-questions as an explicit override or remove it, but a declared project must never get a brief without the section; a conflicting explicit value should be refused). bin/fm-spawn.sh must refuse fresh ship dispatch for a declared project when the brief's section is missing, names a different register, or is unfilled; an explicit `Open questions: none` is allowed. Resolve the declaring project in fm-spawn by matching the registry entries' registered clone path (fm-project-mode.sh --path) against the spawned project directory, since a registry name can differ from the clone basename (prototype-game lives inside the ProjectWhite clone); if more than one declared entry maps to the same clone, require the brief's register to be one of them rather than guessing. Projects without a declaration behave exactly as today. Update the owning headers (fm-project-mode.sh, fm-brief.sh, fm-spawn.sh, fm-open-questions-lib.sh), the AGENTS.md section 7 sentence (keep it one sentence), the project-management skill if it owns registry syntax, docs/scripts.md, and add behavior tests (registry declaration -> automatic section; declared project + brief without section -> refused; undeclared project unchanged) in the existing colocated test files.
review-2: restrict fm_oq_brief_check to lines inside the `# Open-question dependencies` section (from that heading to the next top-level heading outside fenced blocks), so lines in the task text or captain's intent are never counted; add a test where the captain's intent contains an `Open question X: open` line that does not affect the check.

findings.description: `fm_oq_brief_check` scans every line of the whole brief, not just the `# Open-question dependencies` section. A line in the task text or captain's intent that begins with `Open question X: ...` or `Open questions: none` is counted as a dependency line. It can trigger a false refusal, a duplicate-id error, or a `none`/deps conflict. Restricting the scan to the section would remove that ambiguity.

findings.description: In `--declared-registers`, a candidate whose `--path` lookup fails (duplicate or ambiguous entry) skips the clone-path comparison and is still counted as declaring for the target. If that entry's register is valid, it is attributed to every project. If it is invalid, `exit 1` makes every ship dispatch and brief scaffold fail repo-wide, not just that project's. Fix: when `--path` fails, `continue` for non-matching targets or fall back to the `FM_HOME/projects/<name>` path, and report the invalid entry only when it maps to the target.
findings.user_instructions:
review-1: in --declared-registers, never attribute a candidate's register to a target it does not provably map to: when the candidate's --path lookup fails, fall back to the FM_HOME/projects/<name> default path for the comparison (or skip it), and report an invalid or unresolvable declaration only when that entry maps to the target, so one bad registry line never breaks dispatch or scaffolding for other projects. Add a test with a broken unrelated declaration that leaves another project's dispatch unaffected.
review-2: anchor the declaration so prose cannot trigger it: only recognize `open-questions` immediately followed by a backtick-quoted relative path (for example open-questions `prototype-game/docs/wiki/open-questions.md`); any other occurrence of the word is ordinary prose and declares nothing. Update the registry-format header and docs accordingly and add a test that a description containing plain prose such as "no open-questions yet" or "surfaces open questions" declares no register.

findings.description: The declaration clause ` open-questions <word>` is matched anywhere in a registry description. Anchoring the clause more tightly, for example requiring a path-like token or backticks, would remove the ambiguity.

findings.description: status_current_phase puts `working:`/`resolved:` back on the last reported phase. That phase never resets after a `done:` line. Example: a ship worker writes `phase: ready-to-merge - <PR>`, then `done: PR ready`, then gets review feedback and writes `working: addressing review comments` without a new `phase:` line. The board keeps showing "Ready to merge" (ready group) while the worker is back to fixing. Possible fixes: clear the remembered phase on `done`, or let a `working` line after `done` show as plain `working`. This is a product-semantics choice for the author.
findings.user_instructions: Clear the remembered phase when a done or failed line arrives, so a later working line without a new phase line shows as plain working; add a regression test for phase ready-to-merge then done then working.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The feature meets the intent (workers report their own phases, the board updates live, firstmate reads the same rows through `show`, and pointing at a row reaches it as a durable wake), but it changes the watcher's wake triage and the latest-event scan, and the phase fold can show a stale ready-to-merge label.

findings.description: A second `done:` line after `phase: ready-to-merge` + `done: PR ready` keeps the row on "Ready to merge". The done branch only switches to `done` when phase != ready-to-merge, and phase still holds ready-to-merge after the first done. Example: `phase: ready-to-merge`, then `done: PR ready`, then `done: merged` still shows Ready to merge. Only the first done right after a ready-to-merge phase should confirm it; set a flag, or compare against `worker` before clearing it.
findings.user_instructions: Only the first done line right after a ready-to-merge phase confirms Ready to merge; clear the remembered phase once that done is consumed so a later done shows as done. Add a regression test for phase ready-to-merge then done then done, and keep the existing ready-to-merge then done then working test passing.

findings.description: In normal mode, any unbound lowercase letter (a, b, c, d, e, n, p, w, x, ...) switches into note input with that letter pre-filled. For a vim user, a mistyped key (e.g. 'x', 'w', 'n', or 'd' meant as Ctrl-d) followed by Enter sends that text, plus the selected item, to firstmate's inbox and wakes it. This conflicts with keeping the board a safe vim-style navigator. Please confirm that type-to-note is intended; if not, keep note entry behind i/: only.
findings.user_instructions: In normal mode, enter note input only via i or :; unbound letters are ignored and never prefill or send a note. Add a test that a stray letter followed by Enter sends nothing to the inbox.

findings.description: The new EXIT trap in `command_tui` replaces the `trap "rm -rf -- '$work'" EXIT` that `command_refresh` installed earlier in the same shell (`command_refresh >/dev/null` runs in-process at line 185; the base version had no second trap). On the default `tui`/`open`/`firstmate` path the staging directory `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-crew-board.XXXXXX` created at line 119 is therefore never removed and leaks on every board launch, holding snapshot.json, previous.json, mtimes.json, panels.json (phone serials, captain questions, quota detail) and the previous board payload. The leak is invisible to the test suite because the PTY harness sets `FM_CREW_BOARD_ALLOWANCE_DISABLE=1`, and it does not reproduce on the standalone `refresh` path where the original trap survives. Keep both cleanups: either `rm -rf -- "$work"` at the end of `command_refresh` (or chain the previous trap text into the new one) instead of overwriting it.

findings.description: The new EXIT trap signals `$FM_CREW_BOARD_ALLOWANCE_PID` without checking that the pid still belongs to the sampler. The sampler can end on its own during a session: `refresh_allowance`'s handler calls `QUOTA_ERROR.touch()` outside any guard (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:282), so an OSError there (state directory removed by teardown, unwritable state) escapes `refresh_allowance`, ends the `--allowance-loop` process, and is invisible because the sampler's stderr is redirected to /dev/null (bin/fm-crew-board.sh:190). findings.description: The row hit test accepts every Y from rect.y+3 through rect.y+rect.height-1, but the focused panel only draws `innerHeight = height-5` view rows (view.go:335), and its box ends one row above the rect bottom: `Height(max(1, height-2))` (view.go:387) cannot pad the height-3-line content (strip + title + viewport) up to lipgloss' height-4 target, so the panel is height-1 rows tall while the rect claims height. Concrete: focus WORKERS at 120x24 (rect.y=4, rect.height=16 -> 11 visible lines, indices offset..offset+10). Clicking the panel's bottom border (Y=rect.y+14) computes line = offset+11, one past the last visible line, and clicking the blank row below the panel (Y=rect.y+15) computes offset+12, so a click on dead space silently moves the selection to a row that was never on screen and re-scrolls the panel. Bound the accepted range to the rendered rows (rect.y+3 .. rect.y+3+innerHeight-1) or reuse the viewport's visible window when computing `line`.

findings.description: The new phone-alert block keys both the promotion predicate (line 425) and the reason line (429) off the *merged* status, while `phone_entries` overlays a matched cache entry onto the device row and keeps the adb fact only in `row["adb"]` (`row.update(status=entry["status"] or row["status"], ...)`), so a cache match can mask or mislabel the state this fix round was asked to surface. Concrete 1 (wrong label, reproduced by running the projection with a stub adb): cache `{"id":"serial-two","title":"Galaxy S22","status":"locked","detail":"held by worker"}` + `adb devices -l` -> `serial-two unauthorized` yields a row with `status` "locked" and `adb` "unauthorized", and the alert reads `Phone serial-two locked` / detail `adb reports locked, so the phone cannot take tests` - contradicting the `adb` value stored in the very same row. A locked phone whose cable/daemon drops is exactly this case. Concrete 2 (missing alert, also reproduced): the same cache entry with `status` "busy" + `serial-two offline` fails the tuple check at line 425, so the offline device adds no ALERTS row at all (only the watcher row was emitted) even though the row carries `alert=true` and therefore already badges the page and the PHONES sub-tab; docs/configuration.md:630 states the intended contract ("unauthorized, offline, locked, and unavailable phones each add an ALERTS row"). The earliest shared boundary that makes the invariant hold is the adb state itself: append the adb-driven alert from `phone.get("adb")` (title/status/reason all from the adb state) alongside the existing status-driven branch, so a cache overlay can neither relabel nor suppress it. One case in `test_phone_connection_states` with a cache entry that also matches the unauthorized serial would pin both paths.
findings.user_instructions: Use the adb state itself for unauthorized/offline alert title, status, and reason even when a cache overlay changes the phone row status. findings.description: `local_phones` keeps only lines whose second field is exactly `device`, `unauthorized`, or `offline`, so a real attached phone that adb reports in any other state is dropped and the panel falls back to `No phones connected` (view.go:341) — the exact symptom of the reported bug, from a different cause. Concrete: on a Linux host without udev rules `adb devices -l` prints `R58M12345            no permissions (user in plugdev group; are your udev rules wrong?); see [http://developer.android.com/tools/device.html]`; `fields[1]` is `no`, so the row is skipped and a phone the captain has plugged in is invisible again. `recovery`, `sideload`, and `bootloader` states are dropped the same way. Since the durable fix for this bug is exactly "show what `adb devices -l` lists", dropping unknown states keeps the authorized failure reachable. Earliest shared boundary: treat every device line as a row — recognise the two-word `no permissions` state, and for any other second field report it with `alert=true` (e.g. `item(model, serial, state, alert=True)` with `row["adb"] = state`), instead of filtering by an allowlist.

findings.description: The new adb-keyed alert branch narrows which phones reach ALERTS: promotion now requires either `phone.get("adb")` to be `unauthorized`/`offline` (only attached rows have an `adb` key) or a merged status of `locked`/`unavailable`. A cache-supplied phone row that no attached device matches (`phone_entries` returns `rows + cached`, and `cached` rows have no `adb`) with `"status":"offline"` or `"status":"unauthorized"` therefore produces no ALERTS row at all, where the previous round's projection promoted all four statuses regardless of attachment. docs/configuration.md:630 still states "unauthorized, offline, locked, and unavailable phones each add their own ALERTS row", so the code and the documented contract diverge for that row shape. Naively re-adding `unauthorized`/`offline` to the status check would double-alert attached phones (their merged status is adb-derived), so the safe form is `if phone.get("adb") is None and phone["status"] in ("unauthorized", "offline"): alerts.append(item(f"Phone {phone['title']} {phone['status']}", phone["detail"], phone["status"], alert=True))`. Whether a cache-only row in those states should alert at all is a contract decision: if not, drop them from the doc line instead.

findings.description: An `exhausted_now` scope is still silently dropped whenever the same provider has another scope with a numeric percent, so the requirement this round was written to satisfy ("treat exhausted_now as an alert") holds only for the two shapes it enumerated. `exhausted` (line 337) is consulted only under `if not scoped:` (line 350), so the flag is discarded as soon as one sibling scope appended a row. The mixed shape is produced by the real path, not just by hand-written fixtures: bin/fm-quota-choose.sh's TOON→JSON branch (`group_by(.provider)` over `$rows + $attention_entries`) merges a provider's `quota[]` rows with its `attention[]` rows, and `attention_availability` maps kind=headroom_unknown + detail `exhausted_now limited by …` to `{status:"unknown", runway:{status:"exhausted_now"}}`; bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:61-88 accepts that under `quotaSemantics.status` known (all scopes known or unknown) and partial. Concrete input: `{"provider":"claude","quotaSemantics":{"status":"known","effectiveAvailability":[{"scope":"all_models","status":"known","effectivePercentRemaining":70,"runway":{"status":"through_reset"}},{"scope":"model:fable","status":"unknown","runway":{"status":"exhausted_now"}}]}}` traces to: scope 1 appends `claude` / `70% left` with alert=false and scoped=1; scope 2 sets exhausted=True and `continue`s; `if not scoped:` is false, so scope 2 yields no row and no alert on any surface (the AI ALLOWANCE sub-tab badge, its red border, and the PLANNING tab count all stay off) while a scope reads exhausted_now — the same severity inversion the prior finding reported, in its remaining reachable form. Make the invariant hold at the earliest shared boundary, the per-scope loop, rather than at the provider-level fallback: for a scope without a numeric percent whose runway is `exhausted_now`, append the exhausted row there (title `name` for `all_models`, else `name / <scope>`, status `exhausted now`, alert=True) so no scope can vanish because a sibling is scoped. Pin it with a test in tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh using the mixed input above.

findings.description: The PHONES panel's new source still only resolves `adb` by bare name, so in the environment the bug was reported from it returns no devices and the reported symptom survives the fix. Sequence: `local_phones()` (line 213) runs `subprocess.run(["adb", "devices", "-l"], ...)`; when adb is not resolvable that raises FileNotFoundError, which the handler on lines 215-216 (`except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired): return []`) converts into an empty list, never into an error. `phone_entries` then merges that empty list with `entries(cache, "phones")`, and this home has no `data/crew-board-cache.json` at all, so `panels.phones` is `[]` and bin/fm-crew-board-tui/view.go:340 renders the literal `No phones connected`; the TESTING summary card reads `0 connected`. Evidence that the precondition does not hold where the bug came from (this machine is the captain's home, /var/home/sanchith/LILA/firstmate): `command -v adb` fails, the binary exists only at `$HOME/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb`, no startup file (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .zshrc, /etc/profile.d, ~/.config/environment.d) adds platform-tools to PATH, the shell history only ever invokes it as `$HOME/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb -s <serial> ...`, firstmate's own `data/learnings.md:234` records "needs the Android SDK on PATH; plain adb exits 127", and the board payload this change replaces already has `panels.phones == []`. `tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:187` passes only because it installs a stub `adb` on a fabricated PATH (line 176: `PATH="$stub:/usr/bin:/bin"`), so the fix's precondition was never exercised against the real environment. The earliest shared boundary that makes the required invariant hold is one adb resolution behind the query, matching how this repo already handles a tool a non-login shell cannot find (`bin/fm-inbox.sh:68` prepends `$HOME/.toolbox/bin` for exactly this reason) and how the project's device harness accepts either (frogpile `scripts/device_test_lib/android.py` reports "adb not found on PATH — install Android platform-tools, or set ANDROID_HOME"): PATH first, then `$ANDROID_HOME`/`$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/platform-tools/adb`, then `$HOME/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb`. The same boundary should also stop rendering an unanswered query as `No phones connected` — a timeout (2 s on line 214) or a missing adb currently produce the identical empty panel a healthy `adb devices` produces when nothing is attached, so "adb could not be queried" is indistinguishable from "no phones attached"; that is the ambiguity that made this bug reportable in the first place. Which fallbacks this home should support, and what an unqueryable adb should read on the board, is the author's/captain's call.

findings.description: `quota_entries()` returns `[]` the moment `state/crew-board-quota.json` is missing or unreadable (line 338) and `allowance_entries()` (line 407-411) then falls back to cache rows only, so the failure marker the sampler writes on every failed attempt (`QUOTA_ERROR.touch()`, line 275-281) is never read in exactly the state a permanently broken sampler lives in. Concrete trace: on this home `quota-axi` resolves only from `/var/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin` (npm global under the Linuxbrew prefix; `command -v quota-axi` fails in any shell that did not source brew's shellenv), so `refresh_allowance()` raises OSError on `subprocess.run(["quota-axi", ...])`, touches `state/.crew-board-quota-error`, and never writes `crew-board-quota.json`; `quota_entries()` then hits the `except OSError` at line 337 and returns `[]`, this home has no `data/crew-board-cache.json`, so `panels.allowance == []`. Surfaces: the PLANNING page's `renderFocused` shows the generic `No items to show` (bin/fm-crew-board-tui/view.go:298-299), the AI ALLOWANCE summary card reads `AI ALLOWANCE  none` (view.go:56-57), `alertCount(2)` and `subTab` see no row with `alert`, and the ALERTS panel gets nothing - a home with a broken sampler looks identical to a home with no providers, and the doc sentence this behaviour was written against only covers the pre-first-snapshot case ("shows only its cached rows until the sampler records its first good snapshot"), not a sampler that has failed every time. The earliest shared boundary that makes the invariant hold is the same one this file already uses for the two sibling failure paths: `tasks_axi_list` returns None so `backlog.source` reads `unavailable` on the board, and `local_phones()` returns a single `Phone check` alert row carrying the reason (line 269-274). One row on the `allowance_entries`/`quota_entries` boundary when `QUOTA` is absent and `QUOTA_ERROR` is present (mirroring `Phone check`) would make a failed sampler visible without touching the sampler itself; what that row should say, and whether the card should read `unavailable` as the phones card does, is the captain's call, so this is recorded rather than assumed. Not a merge blocker: no wrong value is printed, only an ambiguity.

For contrast, only a patch above 128 KiB splits: commit b20ec58 (3252 lines, 142414 bytes) plans as 2 chunks. Confirm whether enabling chunked mode is the intended outcome for the board fix, or whether that change must be split (or the fork's per-chunk budget used) so its review actually runs as bounded independent turns. docs/configuration.md:234 ('splits the review of a diff larger than that many changed lines into bounded chunks') overstates the guarantee in the same way.

findings.description: `daily_routines()` derives a routine's hourly gate by regexing the routine's own check script and passes the captured number straight into `dt.time(hour)`, which raises `ValueError` for any hour outside 0..23, and no caller catches it. Concrete path: a hand-written `state/<name>-daily.check.sh` containing `[ "$hour" -lt 24 ]` (or such a line inside a comment, since the regex matches anywhere in the file) makes `project()` raise, so `bin/fm-crew-board.sh refresh` aborts with `cannot compose local crew board panels`; the TUI then keeps its last payload and shows the error in the notice bar — every panel stops updating, not just DAILY ROUTINES. Not triggered today (this home's three scripts gate on 18 and 10), but one authored bound fixes the blast radius cheaply: clamp or ignore out-of-range matches, e.g. `hour = min(23, int(hour.group(1))) if hour else 0`, or keep the whole routine row inside a try/except and emit the row with `hour = 0`.

findings.description: `playbot_workers()` spawns bare `node` and returns `[]` for every failure (non-zero exit, the 1.5s timeout, OSError) with nothing recorded anywhere, so all Playbot lanes disappear from WORKERS with no row, badge, or ALERTS entry explaining it. Concrete path: `bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs` imports `node:sqlite` at its top (line 82) and its header states it requires Node 22.5+ (line 74), so on a PATH whose `node` is older than 22.5 the module dies at import, `run.returncode` is 1, and no lane is ever listed for that whole session; the same empty result comes from node being absent, or from the 1.5s bound being exceeded on a loaded machine. This repo already treats ambient `node` as untrustworthy — `tests/lib.sh`'s `fm_test_find_node`/`fm_test_require_node` (lines 139/182, FM_TEST_NODE_MIN=22.5) search PATH then the known install roots for that reason, and this change hardened the lane test to gate on that resolver — but the production read kept the bare `node`, while docs/configuration.md:628 promises unconditionally that a live Playbot lane appears. The captain's stated requirement is that Playbot work is never skipped. Earliest shared boundary that would make that hold: resolve the runtime the way the suite already does (at least FM_TEST_NODE_MIN, else the fm_test_find_node roots) and/or emit the read's own reason as a row when the bounded read cannot answer.

findings.description: test_phone_adb_fallbacks (lines 295, 298, 301, 304) and test_phone_check_unavailable (line 316) run the board with PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" and rely on that PATH holding no `adb`. bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:239-249 shows why PATH wins: `adb_binary()` calls `shutil.which("adb")` first and only then tries ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, ~/Android/Sdk and Linuxbrew, so any ambient adb on that PATH pre-empts the probe. Concrete: on a host with the distro package (Debian/Ubuntu `android-tools-adb` installs /usr/bin/adb), the first block of test_phone_check_unavailable resolves that binary, `local_phones()` returns its output or the "no device list" failure instead of the intended "adb was not found", and the assertions 'Phone check'/'adb was not found' fail against a correct implementation; the four fallback blocks likewise read the host binary (or jq yields null ids) instead of serial-android-home/serial-android-sdk-root/serial-home-sdk/serial-brew. The round-1 fix neutralized ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, HOME and HOMEBREW_PREFIX in these blocks but left PATH, which is the one path the resolver consults first. Run these blocks with a PATH that provably has the tools the board needs (sh, python3, jq, perl, mktemp, date) and no adb - a fixture directory of symlinks, or the neighbouring tests' stub-PATH pattern - so binary resolution is controlled rather than ambient.

findings.description: `panelSummary` derives every collapsed card's number from `len(rows)` plus a fixed noun, but for two panels the rows are not one per named item. (a) AI ALLOWANCE: `quota_entries()` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:957-966) appends aggregate bucket rows (`2 providers unavailable`, `1 provider unmeasured`) alongside the per-provider rows, so with four providers of which two report a broken state the card renders `AI ALLOWANCE  3 providers` (the aggregate row counts as a provider). This is the captain's own requested surface (`Also where is the cost thing you promised to show me`) and the exact complaint the labelled card was added for (`The bare number has no label`), so a number that does not match what it names reproduces the reported problem. Reachable input: the repo's own fixture in tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:483-490 feeds a `cursor` provider with `state.status` `auth_required`, which produces one bucket row next to every healthy provider. (b) TEST QUEUE: `nouns["test_queue"] = "queued"` while `test_queue()` rows are one per resource group member, including each group's `RUNNING: <task>` row (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:713-719), so a suite that is running with two waiters reads `TEST QUEUE  3 queued`. findings.description: `allowance_failure()` reports only the failure's age, and `refresh_allowance()` (line 909-933) throws the cause away: a non-zero exit, an unparseable payload, and a missing binary all collapse into the literal `quota-axi failed` / `quota-axi was not found...`, and the marker is written with `QUOTA_ERROR.touch()` so `state/.crew-board-quota-error` carries no content. A captain whose AI ALLOWANCE panel reads `Allowance check: no quota snapshot is recorded; the last quota-axi attempt failed 0m ago` therefore cannot tell an unauthenticated provider from a network outage from a missing quota-axi, while the two sibling checks rendered by the same panel do surface their concrete reason (`Phone check: adb was not found on PATH, under ANDROID_HOME...`, and `Playbot check unavailable: <binary> board-lanes exited N`). The marker is only tested for existence (tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:451) and read by nothing else, so writing the cause into it (e.g. the `run.stderr` tail or the exception text) and including it in the message is safe; otherwise state the actionable half only, since the age alone is not actionable.

findings.description: After a refresh, `refreshedMsg` only drops a selection whose index is now out of range, and `selectReadable()` returns early whenever an in-range index exists. It never checks whether the row at that index is now a section heading. Concrete path: the captain replies to the last question under 'Your decisions'. Firstmate deletes that entry (AGENTS.md:514), so on the next 2s refresh the same index points at the 'For Tarun' heading. `selectedQuestion()` then returns nil, `readingQuestion` is never true because headings take the `continue` branch in panelLines, and no row is highlighted. Moving a stale index onto the nearest selectable row (`selectableFrom(index, 1)`, falling back to `selectableFrom(index, -1)`) in the refresh path, or in selectReadable itself, would keep the invariant 'a selection never sits on a heading' that the keyboard paths already enforce.

findings.description: The docs say the lane read adds the unavailable alert when the runtime 'does not answer within 1.5 seconds'. The code applies that 1.5s bound only to `board-lanes` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:427). findings.description: crew_cwd_reconcile runs each relaunch one after another, in the foreground, inside the bootstrap child. fm-session-start.sh collects that child's output in BOOT_OUT=$(...) and runs it under the whole-digest bound (FM_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT, default 120s). Each `fm-control.sh relaunch` can wait up to EXIT_WAIT (30s) for the old agent to stop, plus settle time, plus LAUNCH_WAIT (90s) for the replacement to come up. That makes one worker's worst case longer than the whole budget. With the reported scenario of three misplaced workers, slow but normal launches (about 30-40s each) can also use up the budget. When the bound is hit, the process group is killed and two things go wrong. First, the buffered BOOT_OUT is lost, so the CREW_CWD lines already produced never reach firstmate and the digest only shows STARTUP TRUNCATED. Second, an fm-control transaction can be killed partway, after the old agent was stopped but before the replacement is confirmed; its EXIT-trap rollback does not run on SIGKILL. Suggested fix: move the relaunches out of the bounded local digest, either into a detached or deferred stage with its own deadline (as the network sweeps do) or with a per-relaunch time limit, and keep only the detection and reporting in the digest.

findings.description: The detached relaunch worker only gets its own session when `setsid` exists. On macOS, which this repo supports and which has no `setsid` by default, it falls back to `nohup`, and nohup does not change the process group. fm-session-start runs the whole digest under fm_run_timed (timeout, gtimeout, or perl setpgrp), and when the bound expires it kills the entire process group (`kill -KILL -- -$runner_pid`). The nohup'd worker is still in that group. So if any later stage (wake-drain, fleet-state, network harvest) pushes the digest past FM_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT while a relaunch is running (the relaunch can take 30-120s), the worker is SIGKILLed partway through `fm-control.sh relaunch`. That skips fm-control's EXIT-trap rollback and queues no outcome wake, which is exactly the failure this fix round was meant to remove. Fix: in the fallback, also give the worker a new process group or session, for example `perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV'` (perl is already a fallback in fm-timeout-lib.sh) or a `set -m` background job, so the bound's group kill cannot reach it.
findings.user_instructions:
For crew-cwd-nohup-fallback-same-pgroup: where setsid is absent, start the detached relaunch worker in a new session portably, for example with perl -e 'use POSIX qw(setsid); setsid(); exec @ARGV' (perl is already relied on by fm_run_timed's fallback), and only fall back to nohup when neither exists. Apply the same session detachment to the crew_slot_hold holder so both detached processes behave alike. Keep the existing tests passing.
For crew-cwd-duplicate-background-relaunch: avoid the false failure wake without new machinery. Before queuing a failure wake, the worker re-reads the agent's location with fm_backend_agent_process; if the agent is now inside its recorded local copy, it reports nothing (or a success) instead of a failure. Also have bootstrap skip starting a background relaunch for a task whose fm-control relaunch is already in progress, using fm-control's existing per-task lock or relaunch journal as the evidence, printing a CREW_CWD line that a relaunch is already under way. Cover the re-read suppression with a test.

findings.description: Detection does not know about relaunches that are already running in the background. If the digest truncates, the banner tells firstmate to rerun bin/fm-session-start.sh. The rerun's bootstrap can then see the same worker still in the primary checkout while the first background relaunch is still in progress, and it starts a second detached worker for the same task. fm-control's per-task CONTROL_LOCK try-acquire refuses that second relaunch, so it queues a 'check: crew-cwd: ... the automatic relaunch failed: ...; relaunch it into that copy with ...' wake. Meanwhile the first relaunch succeeds. Firstmate receives contradictory wakes, and the failure wake tells it to run a manual relaunch on a worker that was just moved. A small marker such as state/.crew-cwd-relaunch-<id> (written by the sweep, removed by the worker), or skipping ids whose control lock is held, would prevent this.

findings.description: The detached worker never checks where the agent is before it relaunches. It re-reads the location only after a failure. The busy check in bootstrap protects only the one task whose fm-control lock is held at that moment; tasks still waiting in an earlier worker's list are not protected. Example: three workers A, B and C are found in the primary checkout. Run 1 starts worker W1, which is relaunching A while B and C wait in its list. The digest truncates and firstmate reruns session start. Run 2 sees A as busy, but B and C hold no lock, so it starts a second worker W2 for B and C. There are two bad outcomes. (a) W2 relaunches B successfully, and later W1 reaches B, takes the now-free lock, and relaunches B again. That throws away the replacement that just started, with a note that wrongly says the worker was found in the primary checkout, and it queues a second success wake. (b) W1 is in the middle of B's relaunch when W2 hits the lock refusal. The re-read finds the old agent stopped or the replacement not yet visible, so the read fails and W2 queues a false 'automatic relaunch failed' wake that tells firstmate to relaunch by hand. Fix: before each relaunch, have the worker re-read the location with fm_backend_agent_process and skip the task if the agent is already inside its copy. Treat fm-control's 'another lifecycle action is already running' refusal (or a held control lock or an active relaunch journal) as 'under way', not as a failure.
findings.user_instructions: For crew-cwd-worker-no-precheck-before-relaunch: make the detached worker re-read each task's agent location with fm_backend_agent_process immediately before relaunching it, and skip (report nothing) any task whose agent is already inside its recorded local copy or is no longer readable as being in the primary checkout. Also serialize crew-cwd workers per home with the existing lock helper in bin/fm-lock-lib.sh (a lock under this home's state directory), so a second worker waits for the first to finish and then re-checks rather than racing it; bound the wait and, if it times out, exit without relaunching or queuing a failure for tasks it did not attempt. Keep it minimal, keep the existing tests passing, and add a test that a worker skips a task whose agent is already back in its copy before relaunch.

findings.description: Sharded suite runs are counted as several full suites. Current FrogPile (tests/run_suite.sh with SUITE_SHARDS=2|4, through tests/run_sharded_suite.py) starts 2 or 4 `godot ... -s tests/run_tests.gd -- --selection-file res://tests/.suite-selection.json` processes, one per `<run_dir>/project-N` copy. The exclusion list does not include `--selection-file`, so each shard becomes its own RUNNING row. Their cwd is outside any task worktree, so process_owner falls back to labels like `project-0`. One sharded suite then shows as `EDITOR: 4 running`, and none of the rows names the owning task. The same happens to a service request that shards: every shard is matched and shown as its own row. Fix: treat `--selection-file` processes as shards and group them under their parent process (the run_sharded_suite.py PID, resolved to its worktree), counting them as one run. Simply excluding them would drop the run entirely whenever the holder fallback does not apply.

findings.description: Every request permanently leaves three copies on disk. `submit` makes a full `git clone --no-local` under `repos/<id>`. `execute` makes a working checkout under `runs/<id>`, which the FrogPile `prepare` step fills with a Godot import cache. `retest_moved` makes a scratch copy under `rebase/<id>`. None of these is deleted after the request finishes; the only `rmtree` calls run before a re-run of the same id or on a failed submit. On this PC (four parallel FrogPile requests, each ship task submitting, plus retests) the state directory grows by roughly one full repository plus one imported checkout per request until the disk fills. Then every later clone fails and the service can no longer test anything. Fix: delete `runs/<id>` (and the `rebase/<id>` scratch copy) once the request finishes, keeping logs and results. Delete `repos/<id>` once a request is finished and not set to retest on move, or has been cancelled.

findings.description: `retest_moved` has no stopping point once the submitted commit has landed. After the worker's commit is merged, `original_sha` is an ancestor of the new landing tip. `merge-base` then returns `original_sha`, the rebase produces the landing tip itself, and the service queues a full suite and phone run of that tip. This repeats on every later landing-branch move, for every `--retest-on-move` request that was ever submitted and not cancelled. With N such landed requests, each push to `proto/godot/frog-pile` queues N identical runs of the same tip, filling FrogPile's four slots and the shared suite and phone queues ahead of real worker requests. findings.description: In fast board mode the cache key covers meta and status checksums, so any new status line from a worker throws away that worker's last live observation. Until the background observer finishes a full cycle (about 12 s+ with 19 workers), the worker shows `{state:"unknown",source:"none"}`. Two board behaviours depend on that live state. First, fm-crew-board-panels.py:1422 lists a PR as ready to merge only when `current.state == "done"`, so a merge-ready PR drops out of the ready list whenever its worker appends a status line. Second, task_json_one clears lifecycle-superseded open decisions only for a working run-step or pane source; with source `none`, stale decisions come back. Because notify.go drops the seen record when a cause clears, a returning decision can show up as a new alert. This can briefly reproduce the symptoms in the intent: the merge call is missing and an old question is shown. Options: keep the previous observation with a 'stale' marker, or observe changed and uncached tasks synchronously, which is cheap when only a few changed.
findings.user_instructions: For review-1, keep the previous observation, marked stale with its age, until the background observer replaces it. Do not fall back to unknown and do not add synchronous live reads on the refresh path. A merge-ready PR must stay in the ready list and a cleared decision must stay cleared across a new status line; add a behavioural test for both. Apply review-2, review-3, and review-4 as described.

In fast mode, a task relaunched mid-snapshot can therefore pair new-generation status with old captured metadata. Fix: on generation mismatch, remove the captures and write the same 'generation changed' observation as the slow path.

findings.description: A red receipt on the bottom car can stall the queue with no wake to firstmate. This happens when the receipt names a failure that is not in the landing tip's landing-health baseline, or when the tip is red and no baseline has been recorded yet. In both cases the car is quietly set back to `needs-final` while its receipt stays recorded, and no ready or failed wake is emitted. The brief tells workers to rerun the full suite on `needs-final`, so the worker reruns, gets the same red result, resubmits, and gets `needs-final` again, forever. Firstmate never learns that it needs `fm-merge-local.sh --base-receipt` or that the car has a new regression. Concrete case: tip T is red with failure X and has no landing-health receipt; car A submits a receipt with failures=1 and failure=X; status returns needs-final, the wake count stays 0, and the loop repeats. Suggested fix: report a distinct status such as `red-receipt` / `needs-baseline`, or treat the car as failed, and emit a deduplicated wake so firstmate can record the baseline or the worker can report `failed:`.

findings.description: `refresh` checks whether a car's branch still exists before it checks whether the car has landed. If firstmate fast-forwards car A with fm-merge-local and then tears it down (fm-teardown.sh deletes the branch with `branch -D`) before any queue call runs, the next `status` from any worker marks A as `failed`. That emits a spurious 'landing-queue failed ... reason=local branch missing' wake, and A's own status reports `failed` instead of `landed`, which can lead A's worker to report `failed:`. Suggested fix: when the branch no longer resolves, check whether the recorded head is an ancestor of TIP (`git merge-base --is-ancestor "${heads[i]}" "$TIP"`) and mark the car `landed` if so, `failed` otherwise.

findings.description: A failed car's reason is kept only in memory for the invocation that failed it. The queue snapshot has no reason column, and every loaded row resets `reasons[i]=-` (line 150). Both the brief and the landing-queue skill depend on that reason reaching the worker, so this breaks the handoff. In the needs-baseline flow, the skill has firstmate run `fm-landing-queue.sh fail <id> --reason <those failures>` and says the worker reports `failed:` from its own status. The worker's brief says "At `failed`, report `failed:` with the status `reason`". The worker's next `status` call loads the row fresh and prints `reason=-`, so the failures firstmate identified never reach the worker or its `failed:` line. The same loss happens for 'local branch missing' on any call after the one that detected it. Concrete case: firstmate runs `fail a --reason 'new-red'`, then worker a runs `status a`, which prints status=failed and reason=-. Fix: persist the failure reason in the queue row (add a sanitized column to the format, which is not yet released) and print it for failed cars. Add a test asserting that a later `status` call by a different invocation still returns the recorded reason.

findings.description: A car whose receipt has failures beyond the tip's baseline is handled two different ways depending on whether a baseline happens to be recorded. If one is recorded, the queue reports `red-receipt`, and the worker can fix the failures on a new head and finalize again under the same task id. If none is recorded, the queue reports `needs-baseline`. Firstmate then gets a tip receipt, finds the extra failures, and the skill tells it to run `fm-landing-queue.sh fail <id>`. That makes the car terminal: it cannot rejoin, and the work has to restart under a new task id. The cause is that firstmate has no way to record the tip baseline without also landing, because only fm-merge-local calls fm_health_store, so it cannot turn this case into `red-receipt`. Please confirm that the stricter outcome is intended. If it is not, one option is to let firstmate record the tip baseline (for example via a queue or landing-health command), after which the queue would naturally report `red-receipt` and leave the fix with the worker.
findings.user_instructions: Firstmate decision: the stricter outcome is not intended. A car with failures beyond the tip baseline must stay recoverable by its own worker in both cases. Add a queue command that lets firstmate record the tip baseline from a tip receipt without landing anything, so the missing-baseline case resolves to red-receipt and the worker fixes and finalizes again under the same task id; fail stays for a car that genuinely cannot continue. Update the skill text and add a behavioural test for the missing-baseline path. Also fix empty-car-reported-landed by refusing ready admission for a head already included in the landing tip, with executable behavioral coverage. Preserve merge authority; neither baseline recording nor the queue may merge or push.

findings.description: `refresh` marks any active car as `landed` when its live head is an ancestor of the landing tip. A worker that runs `ready` with a head that adds no commits beyond the tip passes admission, because refresh runs before the join. On the next `status` call the car becomes `landed`, and the brief then tells the worker to append `done: landed {branch} at {head}`, even though firstmate never merged anything. Suggested fix: in `ready`, reject a head that is already an ancestor of TIP (for example, die with 'nothing to land').

findings.description: The new ownership check in the skill compares the raw directory from `fm_backend_agent_process` with the raw `worktree=` value from the record, and it never says to resolve symlinks first. `fm_agent_process_cwd` reads `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, which is always the fully resolved path. The recorded worktree can be written through a symlink. This host has exactly that case: `/home -> var/home`, and paths show up in both spellings. So an agent that follows the skill literally would see `/var/home/.../wt` against `worktree=/home/.../wt`, call a correctly owned pane foreign, refuse the steer, report the task blocked or failed, and relaunch it, losing its conversation. `crew_cwd_reconcile` already avoids this by passing both sides through `fm_slot_canonical_dir` (`pwd -P`) before comparing. Fix: have the snippet print the resolved worktree too, e.g. `cd "$(fm_meta_get <meta> worktree)" && pwd -P`, or tell the reader to compare the `pwd -P` forms of both paths.

Old rows have no `home`/`state_dir`, so they fall back to the service HOME. Live workers whose results were already consumed, or were already pinged by the session stopgap loop (different body, so idempotent dedupe will not collapse it), get woken for stale requests. Each wake costs a full-context turn, which is the cost this change exists to cut. Consider limiting the replay to requests with no outbox row that finished after the table was created (for example, record a migration marker/timestamp, or mark pre-existing terminal rows as already 'skipped' when the table is first created), so only true crash gaps are replayed.

findings.description: The brief still tells workers at `ready-to-land` or `needs-baseline` to "keep checking queue status every 30 seconds". Each check is a full-context worker turn. Nothing steers the worker when its car becomes `landed`: the only steering message the queue sends is the front steer, and the merge-local reconcile steers only the next car. `needs-baseline` waits on a firstmate decision and can last a long time. This leaves a polling loop in place, against the intent ("Why is the worker waiting. Can we not use hooks?" … "with no polling"). Consider having reconcile send the landed car's worker one durable steer, using the same front-marker pattern, and changing the brief so these states post `paused:` and end the turn.
findings.user_instructions:
Firstmate decision 004 authorizes action fix for ready-to-land-polling. When reconcile observes a car become landed, and when a needs-baseline car becomes ready-to-land or red-receipt, send that car one durable fm-send steer exactly once per transition with the same persisted/idempotent marker pattern as the front steer. Change the generated brief so ready-to-land and needs-baseline append paused: and end the turn instead of polling. Add executable regressions including duplicate reconciliation, baseline resolution, and the landed worker (not just the next front worker). Cover a baseline resolving to needs-gate too, and a paused ready car becoming stale/returning work after its head or target moves, so the no-poll flow cannot leave required worker work asleep. Do not suppress landed/baseline continuation merely because the affected car equals the command task-id argument: firstmate calls reconcile/baseline using that same id. Preserve all exact-head, target, fast-forward, project gate, known-red, and v1 record compatibility properties.
Also repair the current auto-fix escalation-retry-unbounded: persist escalation retry backoff with a bounded cadence, and close the already-reported wake publication/acknowledgement replay gap. A durable publication receipt must survive loss of the SQLite final marker even after the firstmate queue row has been acknowledged, so replay/restart does not publish a second wake. Keep shared wake helpers as the queue-format owner, and test the consumed-row/lost-final-marker replay case, not only a duplicate while the first row remains queued.

The failed CI job has been rerun once on the unchanged e64ea70e head; if it fails again, firstmate wants a decision with both run URLs rather than any test modification.
Apply every authorized repair together. Keep max_concurrent, FrogPile project files, and phone-gate detachment unchanged. Follow firstmate-coding-guidelines. findings.description: The new floor check warns on most fresh dispatches, not just prepaid ones. Subscription providers like claude and codex have no `credits` object in the quota-axi snapshot (see the fixture in tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:437), so every Claude or Codex dispatch prints 'warning: claude credit balance absent or unreadable; prepaid credit floor was not checked'. It also warns when quota-axi isn't installed. When no provider is resolved it prints 'warning:  credit balance unreadable (provider-unresolved)' with an empty provider name. These warnings make it look like a prepaid check was skipped on providers that aren't prepaid, which weakens the signal when an OpenRouter balance really can't be read. Suggested fix: only warn when the provider's snapshot row has a `credits` object that can't be read (wrong unit or a non-number `remaining`), or when the provider is known to be prepaid. Stay quiet for providers that report no credits at all. This changes the documented 'absent balance warns' behavior, so it needs the author's decision.
findings.user_instructions: Fix through the pipeline. Warn only when the provider is prepaid: its quota-axi row carries a credits object, or it is a known prepaid provider (openrouter), and its balance is absent or unreadable. Stay silent for subscription providers without credits, when quota-axi is unavailable for a non-prepaid provider, and when no provider resolves. Update the docs line and add a behavioral test proving a Codex dispatch prints no credit warning. Preserve the below-floor refusal on routing-rule and routing-reason.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The change gates every fresh dispatch, including `--routing-reason` routes, on the prepaid USD floor, as the intent requires, and it reuses the snapshot already recorded in task metadata; the main concern is a warning that fires on every non-prepaid dispatch, not a correctness bug.

fix_summary: Warn on unreadable credits only for prepaid providers

findings.description: The credit floor applies only when the caller passes `--routing-provider openrouter`. `--routing-provider` is optional, and `fm_quota_single_provider_for_harness` in bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:96 has no `pi` entry. So a Pi DeepSeek dispatch like `--harness pi --model deepseek/deepseek-chat --routing-reason '...'` with no `--routing-provider` gets an empty ROUTING_PROVIDER and takes the `provider-unresolved` path. The floor is never checked, and after this fix round no warning is printed either. Before, it at least printed a 'provider-unresolved' warning. The user intent says the hand-written routing-reason path is the gap to close: "DeepSeek dispatches that use a hand-written routing reason skip the profile-array quota gate entirely. The ask: make the dispatch path itself refuse a dispatch on a prepaid-credit provider whose remaining balance is below a floor". Every test passes `--routing-provider openrouter` explicitly, so this path is untested. The silence matches the user's round-1 instruction ('stay silent ... when no provider resolves'), but it leaves the original failure reachable whenever firstmate omits the provider flag. Options: map pi to openrouter when the model is a DeepSeek or OpenRouter model, require `--routing-provider` with `--routing-reason` on harnesses whose provider can't be inferred, or keep the warning for an unresolved provider on pi.
findings.user_instructions: When --routing-provider is absent, infer openrouter for a Pi dispatch whose model id starts with openrouter/; DeepSeek ids use openrouter/deepseek/.... Apply the prepaid floor even on --routing-reason. Keep silence for genuinely non-prepaid or unresolvable cases. Add a behavioral test: pi model openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, --routing-reason and no --routing-provider, below floor, refuses. Also honor the later product-owner rule: do not use OpenRouter for Codex or Claude models, and make a floor refusal point to a native Codex or Claude profile, never an OpenRouter GPT or Claude model id.

user_findings.risk_rationale: The fix round correctly limits the warning to prepaid providers, and its new test checks the real behavior and would have failed before the fix. However, a Pi DeepSeek dispatch with a hand-written routing reason and no --routing-provider still skips the floor, now without any warning.

fix_summary: Infer OpenRouter for Pi openrouter models in credit floor

The diff has none of this. It contains no round cap, no escalation, no review scoped to the delta and no switch to Sonnet. The only changes are the worker context block, a price row and a teardown reorder. The intent names review as the largest single cost: $18.42 of $37.04, from 20 Opus invocations over 5 rounds. For handoff-file-commit-risk: use an ignored task scratch path in the worktree for the handoff, such as a path under an existing ignored directory, and verify it is ignored without changing a project's tracked .gitignore. Preserve the relaunch note-file path and keep the handoff through relaunch.

findings.description: Workers are told to append `working: phase handoff ready ...` and end the turn, on the promise that "Firstmate relaunches this task into a fresh session". Nothing on the firstmate side acts on that line. `working:` is not in FM_CLASSIFY_CAPTAIN_RE_DEFAULT (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:78), so the line never wakes firstmate. AGENTS.md, docs/agent-control.md and the stuck-crewmate-recovery skill never mention phase handoffs. The only reference is a row in the harness-adapter tables. Failing sequence: the worker writes phase-handoff.md, appends the working line and goes idle. The watcher absorbs the nonterminal line until the stale-wedge threshold (~240s), then escalates it as a possible wedge. Firstmate, with no instruction, treats it as a stuck worker or nudges it to continue in the same conversation. The context is never reset, so cut (1) gives no saving. Each phase boundary also adds a spurious stale wake, which inflates the stale_wake_count this same change records in the routing ledger. Fix: have the classifier and firstmate's instructions own a phase-handoff signal that triggers `fm-control.sh relaunch --note-file`. Alternatively, have the worker use a verb that wakes firstmate.

findings.description: phase-handoff.md is written to the worktree root and is not gitignored. A worker that runs `git add -A` or commits at the end of a phase (often the same moment it writes the handoff) can commit the note into the PR branch. 'Remove the note before final delivery' only helps if the worker remembers, and by then the note may already be in history. Write it under an ignored path such as .git/ or a gitignored scratch directory, or add it to the worktree's exclude file at spawn time.

findings.description: Workers now append `blocked: phase handoff ready <path>` at every phase boundary. bin/fm-routing-ledger.py:59 computes `blocked_count` as every status line starting with `blocked:`, and this change makes teardown preserve that count for the routing review. As a result, each routine handoff on a Codex or Claude task adds 1 to blocked_count. Example: a task with 3 phase handoffs and no real blocker records blocked_count=3. Next week's before/after review uses these ledger counts, so it will read the rise as more blockers and will not match last week's baseline. Fix: exclude the `blocked: phase handoff ready` form from blocked_count in the ledger and record it as a separate phase_handoff_count. That keeps the blocker metric comparable and also gives a measurement hook for cut (1).

findings.description: The new handoff guidance (bin/fm-dod-lib.sh:138-142) tells the worker to write `$DATA/<id>/phase-handoff.md`. That is firstmate's data directory, outside the task worktree. The same ship brief's rule 2 says "Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it except a private learning candidate". The scout brief's rule 2 at bin/fm-brief.sh:652 likewise lists only the report, the status file and a learning candidate as allowed outside writes. A worker following rule 2 must either skip the handoff or write the note at another path. In both cases `fm-control.sh relaunch --note-file <path>` fails with 'is not a readable file', or firstmate never gets a usable note, so cut (1) does nothing. The authorized fix asked for an ignored scratch path *in the worktree*. The fix chose the data dir instead. That still avoids the commit risk, but nobody added the matching exception to rule 2. Fix: add the phase-handoff note path to both rule-2 exception lists, next to the status file.

After this pass, info or warning findings may be approved; error findings require escalation.

description: workspaceLaunchPayload() (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:3875-3887) builds the new launch payload as {projectId, mode: "from", baseRef?, branch?} with no `strategy`/multi-root marker, inferred solely from the one reported Zod error text. Per docs/playbot-agent-integration.md:423, the `mode` (open/from/copy) vocabulary and `baseRef` field name were previously only used by Playbot's `quick` strategy, documented there as explicit "single-root provisioning" — distinct from the `project` strategy this tool has always relied on for "every project root gets a worktree" (docs/playbot-lanes.md:58). There is no new test exercising a multi-root project against the new schema, and engineReadiness's only root-coverage guard (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:3764) is gated to engine-dependent dispatch on exactly Playbot 0.117.0, so a multi-root project on another version calling create_workspace (or an engineDependent:false dispatch) with the new schema would silently get back a workspace covering only one root if the new schema is in fact single-root, with no error raised.

docs/playbot-lanes.md was not updated to match the new behavior. Line 48-52 ("Chat-creation API detection") still describes only the pre-0.94/0.94.0 split, omitting the new second-level mode-vs-strategy schema detection this diff adds. Line 58 still asserts create_workspace always uses "Playbot's project strategy," which is no longer true for Playbot builds on the new mode schema. Line 64 still states create_chat/dispatch's newWorkspace accepts "the same name, baseBranch, and branch fields," but workspaceLaunchPayload (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:3878-3880) now throws when name is set under the new schema — a caller following the docs would hit a runtime error the docs don't describe.

The fix round added verifyCreatedWorkspaceRootCoverage() only inside createWorkspace() (lines 3975, 3991 — reached by the create_workspace tool, and by createChat()'s legacy openThread branch), and dispatch already had its own equivalent check via createdWorkspaceFreshness()->workspaceFreshness() at line 6567. But createChat()'s 'launch' branch (lines 4011-4030, used when chatCreationApi() === 'launch', i.e. exactly the new mode-based schema this PR is about) builds the new workspace directly via threads:launch/workspaceLaunchPayload and returns publicThread(resolveThread(...)) with no coverage check at all. This branch is reached directly by the create_chat MCP tool (handler at lines 6496-6499 returns createChat()'s result with no follow-up verification), which is documented at line 6302 as explicitly supporting 'Can create the workspace first via newWorkspace.' Concretely: calling create_chat with newWorkspace on a multi-root project, on a Playbot build using the mode schema, where that schema only provisions one root, returns a successful thread/workspace with silently incomplete root coverage — no error, exactly the failure review-1 was raised to prevent, just reachable through create_chat instead of create_workspace/dispatch. The new tests in this round (tests/fm-playbot-lanes.test.sh single-root fixture) only exercise create_workspace, not create_chat. The earliest shared boundary that would close this is inside createChat()'s 'launch' branch itself (call verifyCreatedWorkspaceRootCoverage when newWorkspace !== undefined, before returning `created`), since both create_chat and dispatch route through createChat().

The new kind=lane branch-resolution logic (bin/fm-merge-local.sh:97-103) is unreachable for every real lane task, because the pre-existing gate at bin/fm-merge-local.sh:79 (`[ "$MODE" = local-only ] || exit 1`, reading `mode=` from the task's .meta) runs first and the only production writer of kind=lane records, ensureTerminalLaneIdentity in bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs (~line 5471-5481), never writes a mode= field. I reproduced this directly: building a meta file with exactly the fields that writer produces (kind=lane, spawn_gen, playbot_project/workspace/thread, playbot_desktop/harness_home, project=, worktree=, landing_branch=, and no mode=) and running bin/fm-merge-local.sh against it fails at line 79 with 'error: task ... is mode=, not local-only', before ever reaching the new lane logic. laneMeta() in fm-playbot-lanes.mjs (which enumerates the identity fields a lane record carries) also never mentions mode, confirming this isn't an omission in one call site. The new tests in tests/fm-merge-local.test.sh don't catch this because their shared write_meta helper (lines 36-43) unconditionally injects mode=local-only for every fixture, including the new lane cases, which doesn't reflect how real lane identities are created. As written, this change cannot actually land any Playbot-lane ship task automatically - the stated goal of the PR - because every such task is refused before the lane-specific code runs. Fixing this requires a design decision (e.g. have fm-merge-local.sh treat kind=lane as satisfying/bypassing the mode=local-only requirement, since lane dispatch has no shell-spawn mode step to draw it from; or have the lane identity writer in fm-playbot-lanes.mjs record mode=local-only for local-only lanes) rather than a mechanical patch, so it needs the author's input.

When the lane worktree path recorded in META is missing entirely (removed, never created, or a typo), `git -C "$WORKTREE" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD` fails the same way it does for a detached HEAD (empty BRANCH via `|| true`), so the refusal message at line 102 says 'has no checked-out branch', which is misleading when the real problem is that the worktree directory doesn't exist. Not a correctness issue (it still refuses safely), just a diagnostic-clarity gap worth a follow-up.

The commit's stated purpose ('Land retired Playbot lanes from recorded branch') is unreachable in production: the new `grep -q '^lane_branch=' "$META"` branch at bin/fm-merge-local.sh:101-103 can only ever be taken if something writes a `lane_branch=` line into a lane task's state/<id>.meta, but no production code does. The only writer of that .meta file is ensureTerminalLaneIdentity (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:5474-5509), whose `fields` object (kind, spawn_gen, playbot_*, project, worktree, landing_branch, mode) never includes lane_branch, and laneMeta()'s identity-key list (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:5401) doesn't mention it either. A grep across the whole repo (bin/, tests/, docs/) turns up `lane_branch=` only in bin/fm-merge-local.sh itself and in tests that fabricate it directly via `printf ... >> "$case_dir/state/task-x1.meta"` (tests/fm-merge-local.test.sh:211,236) — the fixtures manufacture the exact precondition no real caller produces, the same pattern already identified and fixed for the earlier mode= gate. Worse, even the specific 'merge after Playbot retires the worktree' scenario these tests simulate can't occur through the system's one guarded deletion path: retire_workspace refuses with a `live-task-record` blocker (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:2721-2729) whenever any state/*.meta still names the workspace, and fm-teardown.sh only removes that lane .meta record after the workspace is already verified idle and landed (docs/playbot-lanes.md:219) — i.e. by the time a lane's worktree can legitimately disappear via the guarded path, its task record (and thus fm-merge-local.sh's reason to run at all) is already gone. Concretely: build a kind=lane .meta exactly as ensureTerminalLaneIdentity produces it (kind=lane, spawn_gen, playbot_*, project=, worktree=<path>, landing_branch=, mode=local-only) for a worktree that has been removed, and run fm-merge-local.sh against it — it falls through the dead `if` to the pre-existing `git -C "$WORKTREE" symbolic-ref` line, which fails because the directory is gone, and the task is refused with 'has no checked-out branch' exactly as it would have been without this commit. The 'land retired lanes' capability this change claims to add is not actually delivered for any task produced by the system's real writers or its guarded retirement path.

User intent states: "Playbot has updated to 0.128.0 ... Confirm whether 0.128.0 can be trusted the same way, and if so, extend the check so engine-dependent validation can proceed again."
