The diff instead adds 0.129.0 to every verified-version list/string (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:49-50, 3792, 3800, 3808; docs/playbot-lanes.md:276), and the new tests explicitly assert the opposite of what was requested: tests/fm-playbot-lanes.test.sh:8724-8735 feeds version 0.128.0 and asserts the verdict is 'unconfirmed' and that engine IPC is NOT reached ('unverified 0.128.0 reached engine IPC' / 'fails closed'), with a comment stating 'the earlier reported version remains unverified because this fixture cannot establish its live contract'. So 0.128.0 — the version the Frogpile bug fixes are actually stuck on per the intent — is still rejected after this change; only 0.129.0 gained trust. There is no evidence in the repo (commit message, docs, or code comments) of an investigation establishing that Playbot has since moved to 0.129.0, superseding the 0.128.0 report, or that 0.128.0's IPC contract was checked and found untrustworthy. This is a direct contradiction of the stated required behavior and needs the author to confirm whether this is a deliberate version correction (Playbot actually shipped 0.129.0 by the time of the fix) or a transposition bug (128 typed as 129), since as written the change does not unblock the reported problem.

Under `set -eu`, `"${LANE_RETIRE_ARGS[@]}"` expands an empty array, which is an unbound-variable error on bash < 4.4 (including macOS /bin/bash 3.2). The same file guards this elsewhere with `"${LANE_BACKLOG_FLAGS[@]+"${LANE_BACKLOG_FLAGS[@]}"}"` (line 1247). Every ordinary lane teardown without --landed-via would abort at this line on such a shell, which regresses the existing lane retirement path. Use the `+` guard form.

The proof is weak: any commit that is an ancestor of the landing branch (e.g. an old base commit) satisfies --landed-via. This fits the 'operator's word' intent, but nothing ties the named commits to the lane's work.

The 'already owns duplicates' guard reads only the backlink in `.duplicates`. dedupe writes the duplicate record first and the canonical backlink second. If a run is interrupted between those writes, A is a duplicate of B but B.duplicates is still empty. A later `dedupe B --into C` then passes the guard and creates the A→B→C chain this change is meant to prevent. The window is narrow. The existing interruption test suggests it is a known failure mode, and none of the new tests cover it. Consider also refusing when any record has a duplicate disposition whose reference is this candidate, or repair the missing backlink before the check.

The new green-final-head gate is not skipped for `--relaunch`, so a green-final-head ship task can no longer be relaunched. `BASE_HEALTH_REQUIRED` is computed from the brief for every ship task, including a relaunch (the brief still has `Final-head health: green`), and exits with 'supply --base-health-receipt' when `BASE_HEALTH_SET` is 0. A few lines earlier, the relaunch branch rejects `--base-health-receipt` outright ('applies only to fresh dispatch'). So `fm-spawn.sh <id> --relaunch` fails whether or not the flag is passed, which contradicts the header comment ('Relaunches preserve work and do not repeat the initial dispatch check'). Fix: gate the requirement on `[ "$RELAUNCH" -eq 0 ]`, and add a relaunch test case.

The fast-forward merge runs before the incoming receipt is recorded. If `fm_health_store` then fails (disk full, symlinked landing-health dir), the script exits 1 after the tip has already moved, so the caller sees a failed landing. The tip then has no recorded receipt. The next red candidate is refused with 'no current full-suite baseline', until someone supplies `--base-receipt`. Storing the receipt immediately before the merge would not fix this either. A better fix is to exit with a distinct status or message that says the landing succeeded and only recording failed. The merge-then-record ordering is itself reasonable.

The refusal is opt-in per brief. fm-spawn.sh only runs the open-question check when the brief already contains an `Open-question register:` line, and that line only exists if firstmate passed `--open-questions` to fm-brief.sh. The intent requires that a ship brief for a project with a register must name every dependent question and be refused while any is open. Nothing ties the register to the project, so a brief scaffolded without the flag, or with the section deleted, dispatches unchecked. That is the original incident path: a brief that never mentioned the register. AGENTS.md says to pass the flag 'when the project keeps a register', which leaves detection to firstmate's memory. Consider a project-level register declaration, for example in project metadata, that makes fm-spawn require the section. Otherwise confirm that firstmate-discipline enforcement is the intended scope.

`fm_oq_brief_check` scans every line of the whole brief, not just the `# Open-question dependencies` section. A line in the task text or captain's intent that begins with `Open question X: ...` or `Open questions: none` is counted as a dependency line. It can trigger a false refusal, a duplicate-id error, or a `none`/deps conflict. Restricting the scan to the section would remove that ambiguity.

In `--declared-registers`, a candidate whose `--path` lookup fails (duplicate or ambiguous entry) skips the clone-path comparison and is still counted as declaring for the target. If that entry's register is valid, it is attributed to every project. If it is invalid, `exit 1` makes every ship dispatch and brief scaffold fail repo-wide, not just that project's. Fix: when `--path` fails, `continue` for non-matching targets or fall back to the `FM_HOME/projects/<name>` path, and report the invalid entry only when it maps to the target.

The declaration clause ` open-questions <word>` is matched anywhere in a registry description. Ordinary prose such as "no open-questions yet" is parsed as a declaration of register `yet`. That makes dispatch fail on a missing register file, or makes fm-brief emit the section. Anchoring the clause more tightly, for example requiring a path-like token or backticks, would remove the ambiguity.

The new missing-workspace verification block is inserted between the existing sentence that ends "...first measured 2026-08-02 on Herdr 0.7.5 with identical results:" and the `tests/fm-control-herdr-smoke.test.sh` code block that sentence introduces. That separates the existing lifecycle-smoke evidence from its lead-in. The block also hardcodes a personal absolute path (`HERDR_LAB_HELPER=/var/home/sanchith/LILA/firstmate/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`), but the test already defaults to the repo's `bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh`. Move the block after the smoke-test evidence and drop the env override.

Rollback on a missing-endpoint relaunch reuses the stop-path wording. If the fresh-endpoint launch fails before the new record is published, the operator sees "$ID's agent was stopped but the replacement did not launch", but no agent was stopped (exit_result=endpoint-missing). The state left behind is correct: the prior record is restored and the unused endpoint is closed. Only the message misdescribes what happened. Consider branching on exit_result=endpoint-missing.

Still open from round 1 (review-2): the rollback message is wrong for a missing-endpoint relaunch. If fm-spawn fails before publishing the new record, relaunch_rollback takes the `exited|launching` → `prior-record-kept` branch and prints "$ID's agent was stopped but the replacement did not launch". In this path nothing was stopped (exit_result=endpoint-missing). The state left behind is correct: the prior record is kept, the progress note is kept, and fm-spawn's abort cleanup closes the unused endpoint. Only the operator-facing wording is misleading. Fix: branch on `exit_result=endpoint-missing` (or on a saved prior_state) and say that the recorded endpoint was already gone and the fresh endpoint did not come up.

This was flagged in rounds 1 and 2 and is still open. When a relaunch starts from a missing endpoint (exit_result=endpoint-missing) and fm-spawn fails before publishing the new record, relaunch_rollback goes down the `exited|launching` → `prior-record-kept` branch and prints "$ID's agent was stopped but the replacement did not launch". No agent was stopped in this path. The state left behind is still correct: the prior record and progress note are kept, and fm-spawn's abort cleanup closes the unused endpoint. Only the operator-facing message is wrong. Fix: record prior_state in a global, or check exit_result, and in this case say that the recorded endpoint was already gone and the fresh endpoint did not come up.

status_current_phase puts `working:`/`resolved:` back on the last reported phase. That phase never resets after a `done:` line. Example: a ship worker writes `phase: ready-to-merge - <PR>`, then `done: PR ready`, then gets review feedback and writes `working: addressing review comments` without a new `phase:` line. The board keeps showing "Ready to merge" (ready group) while the worker is back to fixing. Possible fixes: clear the remembered phase on `done`, or let a `working` line after `done` show as plain `working`. This is a product-semantics choice for the author.

Race on the keeper lock: the lock directory is created first and the pid file is written afterwards. A second `open`/`keep` that runs reclaim_keeper_lock in that gap finds no live pid and removes the empty directory with rmdir. It then claims the lock itself, so two keepers run and `stop` only kills the one whose pid ended up in the file. Fix: write the pid into a staged directory and rename it into place, or make reclaim leave alone a lock directory that has no pid file yet.

The keeper exits for good the first time `lavish-axi`'s session listing does not show the board open, including when the listing command itself fails (lavish_session_listed_open returns 1 on a non-zero exit). One transient listing error stops the live updates even though the captain still has the page open, and nothing reports it until someone runs `open` again. Consider exiting only after several consecutive not-open reads, or only when the listing succeeds and shows the session ended.

status_current_phase runs its own full status_open_decisions fold plus a per-line bash parse of the whole log, right before the snapshot runs status_open_decisions on the same log again. That doubles the open-decision fold cost per task in every fleet snapshot (/bearings, and every crew board refresh, which can happen every 2s). Passing the already-computed open set into status_current_phase would remove the duplicate fold.

A second `done:` line after `phase: ready-to-merge` + `done: PR ready` keeps the row on "Ready to merge". The done branch only switches to `done` when phase != ready-to-merge, and phase still holds ready-to-merge after the first done. Example: `phase: ready-to-merge`, then `done: PR ready`, then `done: merged` still shows Ready to merge. Only the first done right after a ready-to-merge phase should confirm it; set a flag, or compare against `worker` before clearing it.

status_snapshot_latest_event skips any line that starts with `phase:`, including a phase word outside the vocabulary. The watcher (status_span_phase_only) handles such a line as an ordinary no-verb append, and status_line_verb would also see `phase[corr=..]:` as the phase verb, which the perl regex does not skip. The two definitions of a phase line can drift apart. Low impact today, but `\Q$phase\E\s*:` could be made to match status_line_phase.

Row selection is stored as an index (m.selected[panel]), and focusedItem() is only resolved when Enter is pressed. A 2s refresh can reorder the rows while the captain is typing a note. Rows are sorted by id, and a worker that is torn down drops out of liveWorkers. The feed shifts once it reaches its 100-event cap. Example: the captain selects worker index 2 ('c') and starts typing; worker 'a' leaves; on Enter, focusedItem() returns 'd', so the note goes out as 'Crew board item: d', about the wrong worker. The refreshedMsg handler (lines 307-313) only drops selections that are now out of range, not ones that point at a different item. The same index drift affects m.expanded (peek follows a different worker). Fix: track the selection and expansion by item ID, or at least capture the selected item when note input opens.

readFeed stamps every line of a status file with that file's mtime (info.ModTime()) and shows it as the event time (Status = timestamp.Format). As a result, every past event of a worker shows the time of its latest append, e.g. a 'phase: building' line from hours ago shows as 12:30:05. The feed is also ordered by file rather than by event time: one new line moves that worker's entire 8KB tail to the bottom. The FEED panel therefore shows wrong times and a wrong chronology without any error. Fix: use per-line timestamps if the status format has them; otherwise, show no per-line time and order only by the file's append position.

Command mode quits only on the exact text ':q'. Under the nvim-compatibility requirement ('the TUI should be nvim compatible'), habitual :q!, :qa, :wq or :x are not treated as quit: the prefix is stripped and the text ('q!', 'wq', ...) is sent through fm-inbox.sh as a note, which wakes firstmate. ':' followed by Enter with a row selected sends an item-only note. Fix: treat the common quit forms as quit, and do not send a note for an empty or unrecognised ':' command.

In normal mode, any unbound lowercase letter (a, b, c, d, e, n, p, w, x, ...) switches into note input with that letter pre-filled. For a vim user, a mistyped key (e.g. 'x', 'w', 'n', or 'd' meant as Ctrl-d) followed by Enter sends that text, plus the selected item, to firstmate's inbox and wakes it. This conflicts with keeping the board a safe vim-style navigator. Please confirm that type-to-note is intended; if not, keep note entry behind i/: only.

watcher_alert raises a red 'Monitoring down' alert once state/.last-watcher-beat is older than a hardcoded 45s. Elsewhere the repo treats the watcher as down only after the derived grace (fm_poll_derived_grace: at least 300s; FM_GUARD_GRACE defaults to 300). In normal operation the beacon goes stale while firstmate handles a wake before re-arming, or when FM_POLL is raised above ~45s. The NOW page then shows a false red alert and a '!N' badge. Fix: use the same derived grace, honouring FM_GUARD_GRACE and FM_POLL.

The viewport Y offset is computed from the selected row index (selected - innerHeight/2). The content also includes the multi-line expanded detail, which contains a fm-peek tail of about 32 lines, plus soft-wrapped lines. Example: expand worker 0, then move to worker 5 in a 10-worker list; worker 5 sits at line ~40, but the offset is 0, so the selected row is off-screen. Similarly, a mouse click (app.go:338) maps msg.Y - rect.y - 2 straight to a row index, ignoring both the scroll offset and the expanded lines. It can therefore select, and attach to a note, a different item than the one clicked. Fix: compute line offsets from the rendered lines.

tasks_axi_full parses tasks-axi TOON output with csv.reader, but TOON escapes with backslashes (" , 
), not CSV-style doubled quotes. I reproduced it: the row `  alpha,in_flight,ship,widget,"Build "widget", fast","Finish it.
Second line, too.",-,-` parses into 9 fields, so `len(fields) != 8` silently drops that task from the BACKLOG page. Any title or body that contains a double quote is affected. A multi-line note body that survives parsing shows a literal `
` instead of a line break. The row lines also keep their 2-space TOON indent, so ids come out as `  alpha` and that padded id is attached to notes sent to firstmate. Fix: strip each row and decode TOON quoting properly (backslash escapes), or ask tasks-axi for JSON output if it supports it.

moveSelection now moves focus to the neighbouring panel when it reaches a row edge. Ctrl-d and Ctrl-u call moveSelection 5 times in a loop, so a page jump that starts within 5 rows of a panel edge leaves the panel. Example: in a 5-row panel at row 2, Ctrl-d reaches row 4, then moves focus to the panel below, then keeps moving rows inside that panel. Ctrl-d/u are documented as 'jump within a panel'. The loop also returns nil instead of motionTick, so the focus animation started by beginMotion never gets a tick. Fix: clamp inside the panel for the Ctrl-d/u paths, e.g. an edge-crossing flag on moveSelection or a separate clamped step.

question_entries builds detail from "\n".join(entry), and entry[0] is the bullet text itself. Both the new full page and the existing NOW-page questions panel now repeat the question title as the first detail line when expanded. A question with no continuation lines expands to its own title instead of 'No further detail'. Before this change, detail held only the indented continuation text. Fix: use entry[1:] for detail.

Ctrl-f adds height/3 to scrollOffset with no upper bound. The viewport clamps what is drawn, but the stored offset keeps growing, so after extra Ctrl-f presses the user must press Ctrl-b the same number of times before the view moves back up. Fix: clamp the offset to the content height.

full_backlog shows held tasks only when hold_kind == captain. Tasks held for any other reason (dependency or external waits) appear nowhere on the QUESTIONS page. The user asked for the TUI to show the backlog, so confirm that hiding non-captain holds is intended.

The new EXIT trap in `command_tui` replaces the `trap "rm -rf -- '$work'" EXIT` that `command_refresh` installed earlier in the same shell (`command_refresh >/dev/null` runs in-process at line 185; the base version had no second trap). On the default `tui`/`open`/`firstmate` path the staging directory `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-crew-board.XXXXXX` created at line 119 is therefore never removed and leaks on every board launch, holding snapshot.json, previous.json, mtimes.json, panels.json (phone serials, captain questions, quota detail) and the previous board payload. The leak is invisible to the test suite because the PTY harness sets `FM_CREW_BOARD_ALLOWANCE_DISABLE=1`, and it does not reproduce on the standalone `refresh` path where the original trap survives. Keep both cleanups: either `rm -rf -- "$work"` at the end of `command_refresh` (or chain the previous trap text into the new one) instead of overwriting it.

`quota_entries() + entries(cache, "allowance")` concatenates the live quota rows with the cache overlay and performs no merge, unlike `phone_entries()` which matches cache rows by id/title. `data/crew-board-cache.json` was the only allowance source before this change (docs/configuration.md:626 lists `allowance` among the firstmate-maintained arrays, and the previous fixture used `{"title":"Claude","status":"45% remaining"}`), so any home that already has those entries shows each provider twice once the default-on sampler produces a live row (e.g. `claude  70% left · 0m ago` beside `Claude  45% remaining`), and `panelSummary` counts the duplicate in the card header, reporting "4 providers" for two providers. Decide the merge before this is relied on: prefer the live quota row and drop or label the matching cache row (case-insensitive provider match, the way `phone_entries` overlays), or document the cache `allowance` array as legacy/supplementary.

This default-on sampler makes the board's terminal path issue a network request (quota-axi at fm-crew-board-panels.py:266), and the change also alters documented layout, but `docs/configuration.md` - declared the single owner of this behavior - was not touched. Line 627 still promises "the board refresh and terminal UI make no network request"; line 628 still says an absent cache leaves those panels empty (phones now come from adb); line 623 still describes the QUESTIONS page as showing questions "beside" the backlog panel; line 631 still says `h`/`l` move "to the visible panel in that direction" (they now step sub-tabs); line 617 still lists Harmonica as part of the interface. `AGENTS.md:149`'s state inventory also omits the new `state/crew-board-quota.json` and `state/.crew-board-quota-error`. AGENTS.md:376 keeps keeping documentation accurate inside the current task, and the script header itself was updated, so only the docs lag.

`github.com/charmbracelet/harmonica v0.2.0` is still a direct requirement, but the spring animation was the only importer and nothing in the module (including the tests) references it any more, so `go mod tidy` should drop it from `require` and `go.sum`.

`abs()` is now dead code: after the spring motion was replaced by the frame counter, no caller remains in the package (`absInt` was already deleted in this change). Remove it. Same rewrite left `collapsedHeight(count int)` at view.go:58 ignoring its argument at every call site, since all summary cards are now a fixed 4 rows - a constant would state that instead of implying the count matters.

The QUESTIONS page now renders only the focused panel at full width (`focusWidth = m.width`, summary loop breaks) with CAPTAIN QUESTIONS / BACKLOG demoted to the sub-tab strip, so the two lists are no longer visible at once. That does satisfy the reported bug - focus is now distinguishable at a glance, and `TestQuestionsPageFocusCueFollowsPanel`/`TestSubTabsStayAboveFixedLargePanel` lock the cue and the fixed large panel in place - but the report described the two panels as sitting side by side and only asked to tell them apart, not to hide the inactive one. Confirm you are happy seeing one list at a time here (and then the docs line in the previous finding is simply refreshed), rather than wanting the side-by-side layout kept with a distinguishing border/cursor cue.

The sentence added by the fix round says each page shows "the page's other sub-tabs as summary cards beside or below it", but `view.go` renders a compact card for *every* sub-tab on the page, including the focused one: wide layout at view.go:429-430 (`summaries = append(summaries, summary)` with no skip for `focus.id`), narrow layout at view.go:462, and the narrow height arithmetic at view.go:443-447 counts `summaryCardHeight` once per spec and exactly fills `bodyHeight` only because the focused spec's card is drawn. So the code is deliberate and the sentence is what is wrong: a page shows the focused sub-tab twice (large panel plus its own card). Reword (e.g. "every sub-tab as a summary card beside or below the focused panel") rather than changing the layout.

Clicking a panel that is not focused is now silently discarded: `if rect.id != m.focus { return m, nil }` fires for every summary card recorded in `m.lastRects` (view.go:432, view.go:464), so on the default page the right-hand cards and the stacked cards on a narrow terminal ignore the click. The base code focused the clicked panel (`m.focus = rect.id` plus a selection re-anchor), and mouse reporting is still enabled (view.go:490), while the only mouse test added here (app_test.go:585) covers the sub-tab strip and row clicks, so it cannot tell inert cards apart from working ones. Confirm that inert cards are intended (the sub-tab strip is then the only click target) rather than an accidental loss of click-to-focus.

The new EXIT trap signals `$FM_CREW_BOARD_ALLOWANCE_PID` without checking that the pid still belongs to the sampler. The sampler can end on its own during a session: `refresh_allowance`'s handler calls `QUOTA_ERROR.touch()` outside any guard (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:282), so an OSError there (state directory removed by teardown, unwritable state) escapes `refresh_allowance`, ends the `--allowance-loop` process, and is invisible because the sampler's stderr is redirected to /dev/null (bin/fm-crew-board.sh:190). Once bash has reaped that child its pid is free for reuse, so a board left open for hours can SIGTERM an unrelated process on quit. The Go side already guards this exact class by checking `ps -p <pid> -o command=` before signalling (bin/fm-crew-board-tui/main.go:41); do the same here (or make the loop survive that OSError and exit when its parent does).

The new phones overlay matches a cache row to a live device only by exact id or exact title, while `local_phones()` derives its id from the adb serial and its title from the adb `model:` field with underscores turned into spaces. Concrete case: cache `{"title":"S22","status":"locked"}` (the shape documented at docs/configuration.md:627 and used by tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh) plus an attached phone whose adb line is `... model:Galaxy_S22 ...` -> live row title `Galaxy S22`, no match, so `rows + cached` keeps both rows for one device. `panelSummary` then labels the card `2 connected` (the `phones` noun is `connected`) although one row is a cache row, and `project()` adds a stale `Phone S22 locked` alert beside a device adb just reported as connected. The allowance path was just changed to a case-insensitive provider match for exactly this class of duplicate; decide whether phones should merge on a normalized title (case-insensitive, ignoring spaces/underscores) or whether the cache contract should require the adb serial as `id` and stop matching on title.

Two lines in the crew-board section still describe behavior this change replaced. Line 634 says `j`/`k` 'move above or below at a row edge', but at a row edge `moveSelection` now calls `moveFocusSpatial(0, step)` -> `changeFocus(step)` (bin/fm-crew-board-tui/app.go:314,326), i.e. it steps to the next/previous sub-tab; in the wide layout that panel is beside the focused one, and on QUESTIONS it switches to BACKLOG. Lines 632-633 also omit the new reply path: on the questions panels the note line no longer 'always shows the `i` shortcut' (view.go:477 renders `REPLY [<label>] r/i: answer`) and text typed there is wrapped as `Reply [X]: ... Answer: ...` (app.go:496), neither of which appears anywhere in docs/configuration.md. Reword the j/k sentence to 'step to the next or previous sub-tab at a row edge' and add the `r` reply and its framing to the note-line sentence.

The reply target is resolved from the live selection at Enter time (`m.focusedItem()` / `m.selectedQuestion()`), but the mouse branch at app.go:426 has no `m.inputActive` guard and `m.lastRects` stays populated while the note input is open, so row clicks still write `m.selected` (app.go:445). Concrete sequence: select question A, press `r`, type `use the prototype`, click question B's row, press Enter -> the note that reaches `fm-inbox.sh` reads `Reply [B] ... Answer: use the prototype` and is sent against question B, which firstmate will answer and delete. Freeze the reply target (label + title) when the input opens, or ignore row clicks while `m.inputActive`.

Wide-layout summary cards record a hit rect for every non-focused sub-tab without checking that the card fits in the body, while the body is clipped to `bodyHeight` at view.go:482 and the note line (3 rows) and footer (1 row) are drawn *below* it. Each card is `summaryCardHeight`=4 tall starting at y=4 (view.go:441-446), so on NOW/TESTING (5 sub-tabs) 20 card rows are laid out against a body of `height-8` rows. Concrete: a 120x24 terminal -> focusWidth=81, bodyHeight=16 (body y=4..19), note y=20..22, footer y=23; the FEED card is laid out at y=20..23, is entirely clipped by `Height(bodyHeight).MaxHeight(bodyHeight)` so it is invisible, yet its rect is still recorded, so a click anywhere at x>=81 on the note input line or the footer matches that invisible rect and `focusSubTab` switches the panel to FEED (app.go:429-431). Same overlap at 120x18 (questions rect y=12..15, ready rect y=16..19 over the note/footer) and 120x20 (ready rect). This is a regression from the previous 4-card, 3-row column, which fit inside the body down to height 20. Fix by skipping cards (and their rects) whose bottom exceeds 4+bodyHeight, the way the narrow layout already drops them via `minimal` — that is also what docs/configuration.md:621 already claims ("a terminal too short for both drops the cards").

`phone_entries` resolves each attached device against the cache in one first-match pass whose predicate ORs the serial and the normalized title, so cache order wins rather than the requested "match ... first by id equal to the adb serial, then by normalized title equality". Concrete: cache `[{"title":"Pixel 8","status":"locked"},{"id":"serial-one","title":"Old name","status":"locked"}]` with a live device serial `serial-one` / model `Pixel 8` — the title-only entry is popped, the serial-keyed entry is never considered, and `rows + cached` keeps two rows for one device (card reads "1 connected (1 cached)" and `project()` adds a stale `Phone Old name locked` alert beside a device adb just reported as connected). The prior review round asked for exactly this ordering; two passes over the cache (all serial matches first, then normalized-title matches) implements it and is equivalent in the normal one-entry-per-device case.

`TestNarrowTabStripKeepsFocusedTabVisible` asserts on strings that the focused panel's own title always renders, not on the sub-tab strip it names. At 55x18 with `m.focus = "feed"` the focus panel title "FEED" is drawn by `renderFocused` regardless of what `subTabs`/`subTabStart` produce, and on page 3 `strings.Contains(view, "BACKLOG")` is satisfied by the focused panel title (plus the header's "4 QUESTIONS"). If `subTabStart` regressed to always returning 0 — the exact failure this test claims to cover — both assertions still pass. Assert the strip itself instead (e.g. the active-tab rendering inside `m.subTabs(width)`, as TestSubTabsStayAboveFixedLargePanel does).

Every board refresh now forks `adb devices -l` (panels.py:217, 2s timeout) and a full node process running `fm-playbot-lanes.mjs board-lanes` (1.5s timeout), and the TUI triggers `fm-crew-board.sh refresh` every 2 seconds while it is open (app.go:370), recomposing the payload even when nothing changed. Both calls are bounded and their failures degrade to empty panels, so this is not a correctness problem, but a board left open all day pays a node start plus an adb call per tick for freshness that only the PHONES/lane panels use; gating the subprocess-backed panels to a slower cadence would keep the useful freshness without the per-tick cost. Noted as a tradeoff, no action required.

The row hit test accepts every Y from rect.y+3 through rect.y+rect.height-1, but the focused panel only draws `innerHeight = height-5` view rows (view.go:335), and its box ends one row above the rect bottom: `Height(max(1, height-2))` (view.go:387) cannot pad the height-3-line content (strip + title + viewport) up to lipgloss' height-4 target, so the panel is height-1 rows tall while the rect claims height. Concrete: focus WORKERS at 120x24 (rect.y=4, rect.height=16 -> 11 visible lines, indices offset..offset+10). Clicking the panel's bottom border (Y=rect.y+14) computes line = offset+11, one past the last visible line, and clicking the blank row below the panel (Y=rect.y+15) computes offset+12, so a click on dead space silently moves the selection to a row that was never on screen and re-scrolls the panel. Bound the accepted range to the rendered rows (rect.y+3 .. rect.y+3+innerHeight-1) or reuse the viewport's visible window when computing `line`.

The unfocused-panel cue is unreachable in production: renderFocused is only ever called with the page's focused spec (view.go:434 and view.go:467), and panelLines/rowLine are reached only for m.focus (view.go:336, plus app.go:444 which is behind `if rect.id != m.focus { ... return }`). So rowLine's `id != m.focus` muted branch (view.go:244-247) and renderFocused's `accent := muted` default (view.go:356-358) can never run, and the cue that actually works is the sub-tab strip. app_test.go:184-188 (TestQuestionsPageFocusCueFollowsPanel) asserts the focused and 'unfocused' calls differ, so it pins those dead branches: deleting them fails a test that claims to cover the focus cue. Drop the branches and re-point that assertion at the sub-tab strip, as TestSubTabsStayAboveFixedLargePanel already does, so the cue has one owner.

`local_phones` reports adb's `unauthorized` and `offline` states as row status with alert=True, and phone_entries marks every such row `live` (line 251), while the PHONES card counts `Live` rows as `N connected` (view.go:84-93) and the connected noun is what the card prints. Concrete: `adb devices -l` lists `serial-two device` and `serial-three unauthorized` -> the panel row reads `serial-three unauthorized` in red, but the card reads `2 connected`, so a device the captain cannot dispatch to is reported as connected capacity. The same new states are also absent from ALERTS: project() (line 424) promotes only `locked`/`unavailable` phone rows, so `unauthorized`/`offline` never reach the ALERTS list even though their rows carry alert=True and therefore already drive the page and sub-tab badges. Decide whether the card should count only adb state `device` (or be renamed `attached`) and whether the two new states belong in ALERTS.

`local_phones` collapses every failure of the adb query (binary missing from PATH, non-zero exit, 2s timeout) into `[]`, the same value as 'no devices attached', so the panel still asserts `No phones connected` (view.go:341) when the board could not ask adb at all - the same misleading shape as the reported bug, with a different cause. Not raised as a defect: the query is best-effort by design, the refresh retries every 2 seconds, and a transient adb-server startup self-heals. If the panel is ever reported empty again, the cheap discriminator is to have `local_phones` return a distinguishable marker row (or a flag on the phones panel) so the panel can say the query failed instead of asserting that no phones are connected.

The new phone-alert block keys both the promotion predicate (line 425) and the reason line (429) off the *merged* status, while `phone_entries` overlays a matched cache entry onto the device row and keeps the adb fact only in `row["adb"]` (`row.update(status=entry["status"] or row["status"], ...)`), so a cache match can mask or mislabel the state this fix round was asked to surface. Concrete 1 (wrong label, reproduced by running the projection with a stub adb): cache `{"id":"serial-two","title":"Galaxy S22","status":"locked","detail":"held by worker"}` + `adb devices -l` -> `serial-two unauthorized` yields a row with `status` "locked" and `adb` "unauthorized", and the alert reads `Phone serial-two locked` / detail `adb reports locked, so the phone cannot take tests` - contradicting the `adb` value stored in the very same row. A locked phone whose cable/daemon drops is exactly this case. Concrete 2 (missing alert, also reproduced): the same cache entry with `status` "busy" + `serial-two offline` fails the tuple check at line 425, so the offline device adds no ALERTS row at all (only the watcher row was emitted) even though the row carries `alert=true` and therefore already badges the page and the PHONES sub-tab; docs/configuration.md:630 states the intended contract ("unauthorized, offline, locked, and unavailable phones each add an ALERTS row"). The earliest shared boundary that makes the invariant hold is the adb state itself: append the adb-driven alert from `phone.get("adb")` (title/status/reason all from the adb state) alongside the existing status-driven branch, so a cache overlay can neither relabel nor suppress it. One case in `test_phone_connection_states` with a cache entry that also matches the unauthorized serial would pin both paths.

`local_phones` keeps only lines whose second field is exactly `device`, `unauthorized`, or `offline`, so a real attached phone that adb reports in any other state is dropped and the panel falls back to `No phones connected` (view.go:341) — the exact symptom of the reported bug, from a different cause. Concrete: on a Linux host without udev rules `adb devices -l` prints `R58M12345            no permissions (user in plugdev group; are your udev rules wrong?); see [http://developer.android.com/tools/device.html]`; `fields[1]` is `no`, so the row is skipped and a phone the captain has plugged in is invisible again. `recovery`, `sideload`, and `bootloader` states are dropped the same way. Since the durable fix for this bug is exactly "show what `adb devices -l` lists", dropping unknown states keeps the authorized failure reachable. Earliest shared boundary: treat every device line as a row — recognise the two-word `no permissions` state, and for any other second field report it with `alert=true` (e.g. `item(model, serial, state, alert=True)` with `row["adb"] = state`), instead of filtering by an allowlist.

The new adb-keyed alert branch narrows which phones reach ALERTS: promotion now requires either `phone.get("adb")` to be `unauthorized`/`offline` (only attached rows have an `adb` key) or a merged status of `locked`/`unavailable`. A cache-supplied phone row that no attached device matches (`phone_entries` returns `rows + cached`, and `cached` rows have no `adb`) with `"status":"offline"` or `"status":"unauthorized"` therefore produces no ALERTS row at all, where the previous round's projection promoted all four statuses regardless of attachment. docs/configuration.md:630 still states "unauthorized, offline, locked, and unavailable phones each add their own ALERTS row", so the code and the documented contract diverge for that row shape. Naively re-adding `unauthorized`/`offline` to the status check would double-alert attached phones (their merged status is adb-derived), so the safe form is `if phone.get("adb") is None and phone["status"] in ("unauthorized", "offline"): alerts.append(item(f"Phone {phone['title']} {phone['status']}", phone["detail"], phone["status"], alert=True))`. Whether a cache-only row in those states should alert at all is a contract decision: if not, drop them from the doc line instead.

The alert title is built from the device's model name (`Phone {phone['title']} {adb}`) and the detail is the fixed reason string, so the adb serial — the only thing that distinguishes two identical handsets — never reaches ALERTS; alert rows also carry no item id. Concrete: two Galaxy S22s attached, one showing `unauthorized`, produce a single ALERTS row reading `Phone Galaxy S22 unauthorized`, which the captain cannot map to a specific handset from the board (the PHONES panel has the serial in `detail`, but the alert drops it). Putting the serial in the detail (`f"adb reports {adb} for {phone['id']}, so the phone cannot take tests"`, or `phone['detail']` which already holds the serial for adb rows) would keep the state and the identity together. Noted as a small captain-facing gap, no action required for this change.

`section = None` + `if section is None: continue` makes question_entries() ignore the whole register until the first `## ` heading, and both question panels read through it (lines 451-452), so a register whose questions are bullets without an H2 now reports zero questions where the base commit reported them. Concrete trace: for `# Open questions

- Which release should ship?
  Blocks the Android build.` every line is skipped by the guard (H1 is not `## `, bullets are not `## `/`---`) and `flush()` finds `entry` empty, so `panels.questions` and `panels.full_questions` are `[]`; the QUESTIONS page renders `No captain questions` and the WAITING ON YOU card reports `none`, while at 534b7a6 the same file yielded the one question that `test_panel_projection_and_launcher` asserted. The same commit edited exactly that fixture to add `## Decisions` (tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:132) to keep `assert_equals 1 .panels.questions|length` green, so no test pins the pre-heading shape any more, and the new `test_bold_question_paragraphs` does not need the guard: its preamble paragraph is already ignored because an entry can only be opened by a bullet or bold line, so the guard only suppresses pre-heading bullets/bold lines. This is the same "panel is empty although content exists" symptom the captain reported for phones, moved onto the question surface. The heading requirement is not documented anywhere (AGENTS.md section 9 and docs/configuration.md state no format for data/captain-questions.md), and the file is home-local so its real shape is not verifiable from the repo. Please confirm which registers must still be recognized: the narrow fix keeps the pre-heading shape working (default `section` to `Questions` as before and require a heading only for the `**bold**` opener, or only for prose after a `## ` section), and either way a test should pin the chosen outcome for a heading-less register rather than the fixture being adjusted around it.

`if scopes: continue` is evaluated on the provider's input scope list rather than on whether any row was appended, and the loop above skips every scope without a numeric `percent`, so a provider whose `effectiveAvailability` entries are all `status: "unknown"` produces no AI ALLOWANCE row, no PLANNING badge (line 348) and no `N providers unavailable` line — it vanishes silently. This shape is schema-valid and produced by the real producer: bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:84-88 explicitly accepts a scope with `status: "unknown"`, no `effectivePercentRemaining`, and `runway.status: "exhausted_now"`, which is what bin/fm-quota-choose.sh builds from a quota-axi `attention[]` row whose kind is `headroom_unknown` and detail says `exhausted_now`. Concrete input: `{"provider":"codex","state":{"status":"fresh"},"quotaSemantics":{"status":"unknown","effectiveAvailability":[{"scope":"all_models","status":"unknown","runway":{"status":"exhausted_now"}}]}}` traces to zero rows for codex, so the one provider state that most needs the captain's eye is the one the panel omits. The existing fallback path (credits, else `state.status` into the `providers unavailable` row) already exists for providers with no scope data and is the obvious boundary to widen, but what an unknown-headroom-and-exhausted provider should read on the board is your call, so this needs your decision rather than a mechanical patch.

`alert=runway == "projected_exhaustion"` raises the flag for the forecast state but not for `exhausted_now`, the strictly worse state carried by the same field (bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:79-81 lists `through_reset`, `projected_exhaustion`, `exhausted_now`, `unknown` for a known scope), so the severity signal is inverted: concrete input `{"provider":"claude","quotaSemantics":{"status":"known","effectiveAvailability":[{"scope":"all_models","status":"known","effectivePercentRemaining":0,"runway":{"status":"exhausted_now"}}]}}` yields the row `0% left · <age> ago` with `alert=false`, leaving the AI ALLOWANCE sub-tab badge, its red border and the PLANNING tab count off, while a provider at 17% left with `projected_exhaustion` lights all three. The one-line fix is `alert=runway in ("projected_exhaustion", "exhausted_now")`; test_quota_allowance_snapshot only covers `projected_exhaustion`, so an added case for an exhausted scope would pin it.

An `exhausted_now` scope is still silently dropped whenever the same provider has another scope with a numeric percent, so the requirement this round was written to satisfy ("treat exhausted_now as an alert") holds only for the two shapes it enumerated. `exhausted` (line 337) is consulted only under `if not scoped:` (line 350), so the flag is discarded as soon as one sibling scope appended a row. The mixed shape is produced by the real path, not just by hand-written fixtures: bin/fm-quota-choose.sh's TOON→JSON branch (`group_by(.provider)` over `$rows + $attention_entries`) merges a provider's `quota[]` rows with its `attention[]` rows, and `attention_availability` maps kind=headroom_unknown + detail `exhausted_now limited by …` to `{status:"unknown", runway:{status:"exhausted_now"}}`; bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:61-88 accepts that under `quotaSemantics.status` known (all scopes known or unknown) and partial. Concrete input: `{"provider":"claude","quotaSemantics":{"status":"known","effectiveAvailability":[{"scope":"all_models","status":"known","effectivePercentRemaining":70,"runway":{"status":"through_reset"}},{"scope":"model:fable","status":"unknown","runway":{"status":"exhausted_now"}}]}}` traces to: scope 1 appends `claude` / `70% left` with alert=false and scoped=1; scope 2 sets exhausted=True and `continue`s; `if not scoped:` is false, so scope 2 yields no row and no alert on any surface (the AI ALLOWANCE sub-tab badge, its red border, and the PLANNING tab count all stay off) while a scope reads exhausted_now — the same severity inversion the prior finding reported, in its remaining reachable form. Make the invariant hold at the earliest shared boundary, the per-scope loop, rather than at the provider-level fallback: for a scope without a numeric percent whose runway is `exhausted_now`, append the exhausted row there (title `name` for `all_models`, else `name / <scope>`, status `exhausted now`, alert=True) so no scope can vanish because a sibling is scoped. Pin it with a test in tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh using the mixed input above.

`str(window.get("label") or window.get("id"))` renders the literal `None` into the captain-facing detail when a `limitingWindowIds` entry has no matching entry in the provider's `windows` (`windows.get(key, {})` defaults to an empty dict), unlike the neighbouring `reset` join on line 342 and the credits path on line 362, which both fall back to `"unknown"`. Concrete input: `{"provider":"claude","windows":[{"id":"weekly","label":"week","resetsAt":"Friday"}],"quotaSemantics":{"effectiveAvailability":[{"scope":"all_models","effectivePercentRemaining":40,"limitingWindowIds":["weekly","model:fable:7d"],"runway":{"status":"through_reset"}}]}}` yields the AI ALLOWANCE detail `limit: week, None; reset: Friday, unknown; runway: through_reset; …`. That input is schema-valid: fm_quota_json_valid never checks `limitingWindowIds` against `windows[]`, and tests/fm-quota-array-dispatch-live-e2e.test.sh:85-90 walks those ids defensively (taking the first that resolves to a `resetsAt`) for exactly this reason. Add `or "unknown"` per window so the three expressions in this family agree.

The PHONES panel's new source still only resolves `adb` by bare name, so in the environment the bug was reported from it returns no devices and the reported symptom survives the fix. Sequence: `local_phones()` (line 213) runs `subprocess.run(["adb", "devices", "-l"], ...)`; when adb is not resolvable that raises FileNotFoundError, which the handler on lines 215-216 (`except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired): return []`) converts into an empty list, never into an error. `phone_entries` then merges that empty list with `entries(cache, "phones")`, and this home has no `data/crew-board-cache.json` at all, so `panels.phones` is `[]` and bin/fm-crew-board-tui/view.go:340 renders the literal `No phones connected`; the TESTING summary card reads `0 connected`. Evidence that the precondition does not hold where the bug came from (this machine is the captain's home, /var/home/sanchith/LILA/firstmate): `command -v adb` fails, the binary exists only at `$HOME/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb`, no startup file (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .zshrc, /etc/profile.d, ~/.config/environment.d) adds platform-tools to PATH, the shell history only ever invokes it as `$HOME/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb -s <serial> ...`, firstmate's own `data/learnings.md:234` records "needs the Android SDK on PATH; plain adb exits 127", and the board payload this change replaces already has `panels.phones == []`. `tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:187` passes only because it installs a stub `adb` on a fabricated PATH (line 176: `PATH="$stub:/usr/bin:/bin"`), so the fix's precondition was never exercised against the real environment. The earliest shared boundary that makes the required invariant hold is one adb resolution behind the query, matching how this repo already handles a tool a non-login shell cannot find (`bin/fm-inbox.sh:68` prepends `$HOME/.toolbox/bin` for exactly this reason) and how the project's device harness accepts either (frogpile `scripts/device_test_lib/android.py` reports "adb not found on PATH — install Android platform-tools, or set ANDROID_HOME"): PATH first, then `$ANDROID_HOME`/`$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/platform-tools/adb`, then `$HOME/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb`. The same boundary should also stop rendering an unanswered query as `No phones connected` — a timeout (2 s on line 214) or a missing adb currently produce the identical empty panel a healthy `adb devices` produces when nothing is attached, so "adb could not be queried" is indistinguishable from "no phones attached"; that is the ambiguity that made this bug reportable in the first place. Which fallbacks this home should support, and what an unqueryable adb should read on the board, is the author's/captain's call.

`phone_entries` returns the single `Phone check` row before reading the cache, so whenever adb cannot be resolved, exits non-zero, or times out, every captain-maintained `phones` cache row (locks, "held by worker" notes) is dropped from the panel, together with the `(N cached)` count on the TESTING card. That is a documented-behaviour change: `docs/configuration.md` still states "a cache row no attached device matches stays listed without counting as connected", and nothing in the same file records the new exception beyond the generic "the panel shows one `Phone check` alert row". Concrete trace: cache `{"schema":"fm-crew-board-cache.v1","phones":[{"id":"serial-two","title":"Galaxy S22","status":"locked","detail":"held by worker"}]}` with adb absent yields `panels.phones == [{title:"Phone check", …}]` and no `locked` row or lock alert on any surface. This is contained, not a merge blocker: the fix round's instruction explicitly asked for exactly one alert row in that case (implemented at bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:271-274, surfaced at :457-459 and bin/fm-crew-board-tui/view.go:100-102), and the reported home has no `data/crew-board-cache.json`, so no cache data is lost there today. Recorded only so the tradeoff is visible if a cache is ever introduced; merging the cache rows into the failure path would be a product decision, not a defect fix.

`quota_entries()` returns `[]` the moment `state/crew-board-quota.json` is missing or unreadable (line 338) and `allowance_entries()` (line 407-411) then falls back to cache rows only, so the failure marker the sampler writes on every failed attempt (`QUOTA_ERROR.touch()`, line 275-281) is never read in exactly the state a permanently broken sampler lives in. Concrete trace: on this home `quota-axi` resolves only from `/var/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin` (npm global under the Linuxbrew prefix; `command -v quota-axi` fails in any shell that did not source brew's shellenv), so `refresh_allowance()` raises OSError on `subprocess.run(["quota-axi", ...])`, touches `state/.crew-board-quota-error`, and never writes `crew-board-quota.json`; `quota_entries()` then hits the `except OSError` at line 337 and returns `[]`, this home has no `data/crew-board-cache.json`, so `panels.allowance == []`. Surfaces: the PLANNING page's `renderFocused` shows the generic `No items to show` (bin/fm-crew-board-tui/view.go:298-299), the AI ALLOWANCE summary card reads `AI ALLOWANCE  none` (view.go:56-57), `alertCount(2)` and `subTab` see no row with `alert`, and the ALERTS panel gets nothing - a home with a broken sampler looks identical to a home with no providers, and the doc sentence this behaviour was written against only covers the pre-first-snapshot case ("shows only its cached rows until the sampler records its first good snapshot"), not a sampler that has failed every time. The earliest shared boundary that makes the invariant hold is the same one this file already uses for the two sibling failure paths: `tasks_axi_list` returns None so `backlog.source` reads `unavailable` on the board, and `local_phones()` returns a single `Phone check` alert row carrying the reason (line 269-274). One row on the `allowance_entries`/`quota_entries` boundary when `QUOTA` is absent and `QUOTA_ERROR` is present (mirroring `Phone check`) would make a failed sampler visible without touching the sampler itself; what that row should say, and whether the card should read `unavailable` as the phones card does, is the captain's call, so this is recorded rather than assumed. Not a merge blocker: no wrong value is printed, only an ambiguity.

The adb parse loop treats any stdout line with two whitespace-separated fields as a device, so adb's own client/server version-mismatch banner becomes a phantom phone row. Sequence: `local_phones()` runs `[binary, "devices", "-l"]` (line 248) with `check=False`; when the resolved client and the running server differ in version, adb prints e.g. `adb server version (41) doesn't match this client (39); killing...` to stdout, restarts the server, and still exits 0, so the `if run.returncode` guard at line 255 does not fire. The loop guard at line 260 skips only lines starting with `*` or `List of devices`, so the banner yields `serial="adb"`, `state="server"`, and a row `{id: "adb", title: "adb", status: "server", alert: true, adb: "server"}` via lines 262-267. The PHONES panel then lists a non-device row named `adb` with a red alert badge on its sub-tab, and no ALERTS row (the alert loop at line 491-497 matches only `unauthorized`/`offline` plus cache statuses), and the TESTING card counts it in no bucket (view.go:93-108 switches on `device`/`unavailable`/empty only), so the row is unexplained. This is reachable in the reported home: `adb_binary()` resolves to `/home/sanchith/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb` here (PATH has no adb), while a different platform-tools build is installed at `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/adb` (Caskroom 37.0.1), and both clients address the single server on tcp:5037 that is running now, so whichever client starts the server first, the next refresh from the other one takes this path once. The earliest shared boundary that makes the invariant (one row per attached device, and only device output parsed) hold is the query itself: parse only lines after adb's own `List of devices attached` header, which line 260 already recognises, so any other stdout line is treated as non-device output.

`allowance_failure()` unconditionally states `no quota snapshot is recorded`, but its caller reaches it on any empty `quota_entries()` result, which is not the same as the snapshot being absent. Sequence: sampler run 1 succeeds with `{"providers": []}` (refresh_allowance only requires `isinstance(payload.get("providers"), list)`, line 341-343, so an empty list is a good snapshot) and unlinks `.crew-board-quota-error`; run 2 fails (network outage, or quota-axi removed from all five resolution locations) and touches the marker; `quota_entries()` now iterates zero providers and returns `[]` (line 353-420), so `allowance_entries` (line 433-439) emits `Allowance check: no quota snapshot is recorded; the last quota-axi attempt failed 0m ago` while `state/crew-board-quota.json` exists, and any captain-maintained cache allowance rows disappear behind that false reason. The same wording is produced if the snapshot file exists but is unreadable/invalid (`observed_at` missing), which also returns `[]` at line 354. The panel and the card are otherwise right (unavailable + alert), so this is a wrong reason string, not a wrong state; deriving the message from whether the snapshot file is present (or dropping the first clause, since the failure age is the actionable part) makes it accurate without changing the prescribed behavior.

The new sentence is inserted between the `commands.test` pair (line 233's guidelines-skill sentence and line 235's `commands.test`-is-trusted-only sentence), so it breaks that coherent pair and its subject "It" no longer has a nearby antecedent — the immediately preceding sentence's subject is the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill, not the tracked `.no-mistakes.yaml`. Read as written, "It also sets `review.chunk_threshold_lines: 800`" can be attributed to the skill. Name the subject ("The tracked `.no-mistakes.yaml` also sets ...") or move the sentence next to the other gate-default statements (after line 235) so the trusted-only fact stays with the gate-defaults context it belongs to.

Intent requires the crew board fix to be validated under chunking ('add all the follow-up items ... And chunk it', context: 'the setting has to land on main before the crew board fix is validated'; backlog: 'run the board fix through no-mistakes chunked'), but this threshold only gates ENTRY into chunked mode; the split itself is bounded by the fixed per-chunk budget (128 KiB of patch while the patch is <=1 MiB, 96 paths), not by the line count. Measured on the branch the intent names (fm/fm-board-focus-highlight @907c386 vs main 534b7a6): 2008 changed lines, 15 paths, 113163-byte `git diff --no-renames --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --unified=0` patch, so `chunked` is true (review.go:170) yet planReviewChunks yields exactly 1 chunk - the board fix is still reviewed in one agent turn (only the prompt and the fail-closed structured-output requirement differ), and no value of chunk_threshold_lines can split it because the patch fits one chunk budget. For contrast, only a patch above 128 KiB splits: commit b20ec58 (3252 lines, 142414 bytes) plans as 2 chunks. Confirm whether enabling chunked mode is the intended outcome for the board fix, or whether that change must be split (or the fork's per-chunk budget used) so its review actually runs as bounded independent turns. docs/configuration.md:234 ('splits the review of a diff larger than that many changed lines into bounded chunks') overstates the guarantee in the same way.

This new value is validated fail-closed on the trusted default-branch copy: validateReviewRaw rejects anything that is not 0 or >500, and the daemon's trusted-copy read (assertGateTrustedConfigReadable) aborts EVERY run in this repo when the default branch's .no-mistakes.yaml fails to parse or validate. A later edit on main to e.g. 500 or 400 therefore bricks the repo's gate, including the run that would fix it, and recovery needs an out-of-band push. The tracked file is already treated as a versioned contract elsewhere (tests/fm-nm-test-contract.test.sh parses it with a YAML parser for the `commands.test` invariant, and a .no-mistakes.yaml change selects the pure-contract-unit family, so such a check would run pre-merge). Extend that existing contract test (do not add a source-text/regex assertion) to parse the document into its semantic model and assert review.chunk_threshold_lines is absent, 0, or greater than 500.

The guard's Ruby model does `review.is_a?(Hash) ? review["chunk_threshold_lines"] : nil`, so a future edit that writes `review: 800` (or any non-mapping `review:` value) parses to `val == nil` and the contract reports success even though no-mistakes' unmarshal into the review struct would fail and `assertGateTrustedConfigReadable` would abort every run on main - exactly the brick-out this test exists to prevent. The intended value check itself is correct (absent/0/>500 matches the `review.chunk_threshold_lines must be 0 (disabled) or greater than 500` validator, and string/float/negative values are correctly rejected). Non-blocking: this is an unrealistic edit shape and the test was only prescribed to cover the one key, so treat it as an optional hardening (treat a present-but-non-mapping `review` as a failure rather than as absent).

`pipeline_step` bails unless one of the first eight stdout lines is exactly `status: running`, but `running` is only one of the live statuses this repo's own run reader accepts: bin/fm-crew-state.sh:788 enumerates the non-terminal set as `pending|running|fixing|ci|awaiting_approval|fix_review`, and tests/fm-crew-state.test.sh:367-379 pins a live run that prints `status: fixing` together with an `active_steps` row. Concrete: a worker in a fix round prints `  status: fixing` plus `  active_steps[1]{step,status,...}: test,fixing,...`; the gate returns "" and `worker_tags` (line 660) falls through to `short_note(phase.note)`, so that row shows VALIDATING - the exact complaint the tag exists to fix - instead of the documented `FIXING TESTS` (docs/configuration.md:629). The same gate also discards `ci`, `awaiting_approval`, and `fix_review` runs, so the `{NAME} GATE` branch at line 622 is unreachable from a real run. The only test covering this (tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:695) stubs a run that prints `status: running` while its step row says `fixing`, so it cannot catch the mismatch. Accept any non-terminal status at the gate and derive FIXING/GATE from whichever of the run status or the step row reports it.

The PLANNING BACKLOG panel only falls back to `back.Next` when `Panels.FullBacklog` is empty, but `full_backlog()` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:172-196) always returns at least its four group headings, and on a read failure returns one error row (`Backlog unavailable`), so the fallback can never run in production - the nil case exercised by `TestPlanningBacklogCarriesTheFullBacklog` cannot occur. Concrete reachable case: `backlog.next`/counts come from `tasks_axi_list` (`fm-tasks-axi.sh list --limit 8`, which succeeds), while `full_backlog` needs `tasks_axi_full` (`--fields body,hold_reason,hold_kind,hold_until`, 9 CSV fields, exact header) to succeed; when that form is unavailable - an older/failing tasks-axi - the panel shows only `Backlog unavailable` and drops the queued rows the board did read, although docs/configuration.md:637 promises it "falls back to the next queued tasks when the full list cannot be read". Treat a full list with no task rows (headings only, or the error row) as unusable and append `back.Next`, so the documented fallback is actually reachable.

The background sampler is stopped only by `trap stop_allowance_sampler EXIT` (line 202), so it is cleaned up when the wrapper exits normally. If the wrapper dies without running that trap - `kill -9`, an OOM kill, or a crash inside the trap chain - `python3 fm-crew-board-panels.py --allowance-loop` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:965-968) keeps looping forever: `while True: refresh_allowance(); time.sleep(300)` has no parent-death or board-liveness check, so a closed board leaves a process that spawns quota-axi (a network call) every five minutes and keeps rewriting state/crew-board-quota.json and state/.crew-board-quota-error in the home, forever, invisible because its stderr went to /dev/null. A terminal close is covered (SIGHUP reaches the process group), so this is not a merge blocker, but the sampler is the one part of the board whose cost is unbounded in time. Exiting the loop when its parent changes (`os.getppid()`) or when state/.crew-board-tui.pid no longer names a live board would bound it.

`assert_equals 1 "$(jq '[.panels.phones[] | select(.title == "S22")] | length' ...)" "phone cache"` is the suite's only check of the documented cache contract (docs/configuration.md:644: "a cache row no attached device matches stays listed without counting as connected"), but it drives the real board with the ambient environment and no adb stub. bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:311-316 returns the single `Phone check` row and drops *every* cache phone row whenever the bounded adb query fails to resolve a binary (no `adb` on PATH, no `ANDROID_HOME`, no `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, no `~/Android/Sdk`, no Linuxbrew). Concrete: on a host with none of those five locations (a macOS or minimal-container checkout) `run_board "$home" refresh` yields `panels.phones == [{"title":"Phone check", ...}]`, so this assertion reads 0 and fails against a correctly behaving implementation; the mirror assumption is at line 297, where `PATH="/usr/bin:/bin"` is expected to contain no `adb`, so a host that installs the distro package (Debian/Ubuntu `android-tools-adb` puts `/usr/bin/adb` on that PATH) makes the "adb was not found" case fail instead. Both are new in this change: every other new phone test (e.g. lines 176-190) builds a stub `adb` on a fabricated PATH, and this assertion's predecessor (`.panels.phones[0].title == 'S22'`) only became ambient-dependent once the panel started querying adb before reading the cache. Stub `adb` here with the same no-device stub the neighbouring tests use (or assert the cache contract through `run_panels` with a stub PATH) so the assertion is deterministic.

`readableBacklog()` (line 125) discards the only failure signal a full-backlog read produces, and the substitute it falls back to is empty in this home. Trace with real data: `full_backlog()` fails to read tasks-axi -> returns exactly one row `{title: "Backlog unavailable", detail: "Could not read bin/fm-tasks-axi.sh", status: "error"}`; `readableBacklog` returns nil for it, so `rawItems("backlog")` returns just the counts heading plus `back.Next`. `back.Next` comes from `tasks_axi_list("queued")` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:974), which returns None in this home: tasks-axi truncates the queued list and prints `count: 8 of 67 total`, and bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:115 does `int(line.split(':', 1)[1].strip())` -> ValueError -> `return None` (line 117). Verified against the live home: `jq .backlog state/crew-board.json` reads `{"queued": null, "in_flight": 7, "next": [], "source": "unavailable"}` even though the full list reads fine (full_backlog has 70 rows, so tasks-axi itself resolves). Two consequences: (a) docs/configuration.md:638 promises the panel "falls back to the next queued tasks when the full list cannot be read", but that fallback yields no rows in this home, so a failed read now renders as a bare `In flight ?  /  Queued ?` heading with no rows and no reason - strictly less diagnosable than the base commit, which showed the `Backlog unavailable` error row in the same case; (b) the same parse failure prints `Queued ?` in the heading while 67 tasks are queued, and forces `backlog.source` to `unavailable` although the in-flight list was read (7). Earliest shared boundary that makes both hold is the count parse at bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:115 (accept the `N of M total` form, e.g. take the leading integer), which restores the queued count, `source`, and a non-empty fallback; if the fallback can still be empty, add a one-line reason row at app.go:167-170 rather than dropping the error row silently. Reachable input: any environment where tasks-axi is not resolvable (the same Linuxbrew-PATH class the adb and quota-axi fixes already cover) gives full_backlog = [{title: "Backlog unavailable", status: "error"}] with back.Next = [].

The `if [ -n "$suite_waiter" ]` guard is set at line 630 the moment the background `exec flock` subshell is launched, not when that process is actually blocked on the suite lock, so the guarded assertion at line 646 compares `.panels.test_queue[2]` against `NEXT: Make the widget spin|next` on a premise it never verified. Concrete failing sequence on a loaded runner: the blocker at line 627 (`flock ... sleep 60 &`) has 0.3s to grab the lock; if it has not, or if the waiter wins the race, the waiter runs `true` and exits, `suite_waiters()` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:545-563 reads FLOCK rows from /proc/locks) finds nothing, `suite_waiter` is still non-empty so the guard passes, and index 2 of `test_queue` is the first phone group heading rather than the suite waiter row — the assertion fails against a correctly behaving implementation. Poll /proc/locks (or probe with `flock -n`) for the waiter's pid before asserting instead of keying the guard on the variable being set.

The aggregate allowance row hard-codes the plural `providers`, so with exactly one provider that reports neither a scope nor a credit balance the AI ALLOWANCE panel shows the captain the literal title `1 providers unavailable`. The shape is reachable and is exercised by this change's own fixture: `tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:483-490` feeds one such provider (`cursor`, `state.status` `auth_required`) and asserts only its `.status`/`.detail`, so nothing pins the title and the singular case is untested. Pluralize on `len(unavailable)` (e.g. `provider` when the count is 1).

`daily_routines()` derives a routine's hourly gate by regexing the routine's own check script and passes the captured number straight into `dt.time(hour)`, which raises `ValueError` for any hour outside 0..23, and no caller catches it. Concrete path: a hand-written `state/<name>-daily.check.sh` containing `[ "$hour" -lt 24 ]` (or such a line inside a comment, since the regex matches anywhere in the file) makes `project()` raise, so `bin/fm-crew-board.sh refresh` aborts with `cannot compose local crew board panels`; the TUI then keeps its last payload and shows the error in the notice bar — every panel stops updating, not just DAILY ROUTINES. Not triggered today (this home's three scripts gate on 18 and 10), but one authored bound fixes the blast radius cheaply: clamp or ignore out-of-range matches, e.g. `hour = min(23, int(hour.group(1))) if hour else 0`, or keep the whole routine row inside a try/except and emit the row with `hour = 0`.

`boardLanes` keeps a lane only while `thread.agent_status === "working"` or its `deliveryState` is still undelivered (`queued`/`sending`/`recall-pending`/`unconfirmed`), so a dispatched lane that parks on a card is dropped exactly while it waits on the captain: this check exists for the park transition (`# Prints one line when the worker parks on a card` in the same check template), a parked chat's row is `agent_status` `pending_input` — verified as a real status in this home's Playbot DB (`chat-2-1786446261365`, `pending_input`, workspace `active`) — and by then `deliveryState` is `delivered`. The row therefore appears while working, vanishes while parked, and returns when answered, although the stated requirement is that work assigned to Playbot is not skipped. Reachable for any lane whose workspace is `active` and whose thread is parked. Either include a live non-working lane (with its own phase, e.g. `parked`) or have the docs say parked lanes are reported only through the supervision poll — please confirm which is intended.

The aggregate allowance row is built from every provider that has neither scope rows nor numeric credits, keeping only `provider.state.status`, and is then titled `N providers unavailable`. On this home's live `quota-axi --json` payload (schemaVersion 5, run with the sampler's own flags) that bucket mixes unlike states: `copilot` has `state.status` `fresh` with `quotaSemantics.status` `unknown` and an empty `effectiveAvailability`, so it is listed as `copilot: fresh` inside a row whose title says it is unavailable, next to genuinely broken providers (`cursor: error`, `grok: auth_required`, `agy: unavailable`) and is counted in the `13` — a captain reading `13 providers unavailable` is told a working provider is down. The detail line is honest but the title and the bucket are not: carry the state into the wording (or split `fresh`/`unknown` from `auth_required`/`error`/`unavailable`), which also makes the single line less misleading on a home where most providers are unconfigured.

`command -v node` proves only that *a* node exists, but this test then hard-asserts a Playbot row, which needs a node that can run bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs: that module does `import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"` at the top (line 82, and its header at line 74 states "Requires Node.js 22.5 or newer for node:sqlite"), and `board-lanes` is reached only through `playbot_workers()` in bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py, which returns [] on any non-zero exit. Concrete host: an old ambient node (e.g. /usr/bin/node 20) with a usable node under ~/.nvm or Linuxbrew, the exact roots tests/lib.sh:139 `fm_test_find_node` searches. `command -v node` succeeds, `node ... board-lanes` fails on the node:sqlite import, `playbot_workers()` yields [], and `assert_equals 1 ... "live Playbot lane count"` at line 508 fails with "0" against a correctly behaving implementation - a false failure, not a skip. The suite already owns the fix: `fm_test_require_node` (tests/lib.sh:182) refuses a runtime older than FM_TEST_NODE_MIN=22.5 and prepends the resolved runtime's directory to PATH so the bare `node` this file invokes resolves to it; gate the skip on that resolver (or on `fm_test_node_usable "$(command -v node)"`) instead of a bare `command -v`.

The label reads "fast refresh called quota", but `quota-calls` already holds one line from the explicit `--refresh-allowance` invocation at line 384; asserting the file still has exactly one line is what proves the fast refresh did *not* call quota-axi (the documented "fast projection never queries a network service" contract). The assertion is correct and meaningful; only the message inverts it, so a future reader trying to make the message true would call quota-axi from the fast path. Relabel it e.g. "fast refresh did not spend a quota-axi call".

`assert_equals 0 ... 'idle phone heading shown'` asserts that an idle phone with an empty queue contributes *no* TEST QUEUE rows (group() in bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py returns early when there is no holder and no waiter), which is the intended behavior and matches the contradiction already pinned just above at line 660 ('dead holder kept the phone busy'). The label says the opposite, so someone reading only the message would "fix" the board to emit an empty heading. Reword it to state the invariant, e.g. 'idle phone with an empty queue adds no test queue rows'.

`local_phones()` records every adb state other than `device` as the row's status with `alert=True` (line 302-303, including the `no permissions` form it explicitly re-assembles from the two-field token at line 297), but `alert_entries()` only raises an ALERTS row for `unauthorized` and `offline` (line 786) and then only for `locked`/`unavailable` statuses (line 790), so every other state falls through with no explanation anywhere. Concrete reachable input: a Linux host missing plugdev udev rules makes adb print `R5CT32HRVNM  no permissions (user in plugdev group; are your udev rules wrong?); see [.../udev.html]`, so `local_phones()` yields `{id:"R5CT32HRVNM", title:"R5CT32HRVNM", status:"no permissions", adb:"no permissions", alert:true}`; the PHONES panel lists the row, `alertCount(TESTING)` counts its `alert` flage so the TESTING page tab and the PHONES sub-tab carry a red count badge, `subTab()` marks PHONES with the badge, and `renderCompact()` draws the card with a red border, yet ALERTS — which docs/configuration.md:625 says collects the phone reasons — stays empty, so the captain sees an unexplained alert exactly when the phone is unusable. The same holds for any further adb state (`bootloader`, `recovery`, `sideload`, `authorizing`). Widen the guard to any adb state that is not `device` (for example `if adb not in (None, "device", "unavailable")`), which is where the row's own `alert` flag is already set, so ALERTS and the flagged row agree.

`rows: (($live | sort_by(.id)) + $lanes + ($gone | sort_by(.id)))` sorts the live and gone blocks but leaves `$lanes` in the order `boardLanes` produced, which is `fs.readdirSync(state)` order (bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs:5156 `for (const name of names.filter(...))`). That order is not stable across state-directory changes (a lane registering its `*.lane-poll` file can reshuffle the hash order of the whole lane block), and the TUI consumes payload order directly: `rawItems("workers")` keeps payload order inside each project group (`sort.SliceStable` in bin/fm-crew-board-tui/app.go:191-198), the cursor is a positional index (`m.selected["workers"]`), and `command_refresh`'s `changed` test compares `.rows` arrays element by element — so a reordered lane block silently re-points the highlighted worker and reports a spurious `changed` rewrite on a board whose contents are identical. `$lanes | sort_by(.id)` matches both neighbouring blocks and is idempotent for the lane set.

This change removed the last consumer of `panels.questions` — `rawItems` no longer has a `case "questions"` and the NOW page's sub-tab list no longer contains it (bin/fm-crew-board-tui/app.go:18-21), leaving `panels.Questions` (bin/fm-crew-board-tui/data.go:52) referenced nowhere in the TUI — yet `project()` still emits `"questions": questions(DATA / "captain-questions.md")` beside `"full_questions": question_entries(...)`, so every 2-second board refresh reads and parses the same markdown file a second time just to discard the section rows. Dropping the field and the now-unused `questions()` helper (line 95) removes the duplicate read/parse; the only dependent assertion is `.panels.questions | length` in `test_questions_without_headings` (tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh), which would move to `.panels.full_questions` minus its section rows.

`lock_holds()` never matches a held FLOCK, so the guard that is supposed to prove the suite-lock blocker actually holds the lock before the waiter is launched is a no-op. The awk predicate requires `$3 == "FLOCK"`, but /proc/locks prints `<id>: <pid?>` as `"<id>: FLOCK  ADVISORY  WRITE <pid> <dev> 0 EOF"` for a held lock: field 2 is `FLOCK`, field 3 is `ADVISORY`, field 5 is the pid. Only a *blocked* request gets the extra leading arrow (`"296: -> FLOCK  ADVISORY  WRITE <pid> <dev> 0 EOF"`, fields 2/3 = `->`/`FLOCK`, pid in field 6), which is why the sibling `lock_waits()` at line 65 is correct and `lock_holds()` is not (verified directly against /proc/locks on this host: with `flock <file> sleep 2` holding the lock, `awk -v pid=<holder> '$2 != "->" && $3 == "FLOCK" && $5 == pid'` exits 1). Concrete effect at lines 663-668: `for _ in 1..10; do lock_holds "$blocker" && break; sleep 0.1; done` always burns its full 1s and returns without the blocker holding the lock, so on a loaded runner the waiter can win the race, run `true`, and exit; `lock_waits` then finds nothing and `suite_waiter=''` silently skips the `test_queue[2] == 'NEXT: Make the widget spin|next'` assertion at lines 668-671 - i.e. the exact contention case the round-2 guard was added to make provable degrades back to "sometimes checked". Fix the predicate to the held-lock shape (`$2 == "FLOCK" && $5 == pid`) or probe contention with `flock -n` instead, so the waiter's expectation is asserted rather than skipped.

`playbot_workers()` spawns bare `node` and returns `[]` for every failure (non-zero exit, the 1.5s timeout, OSError) with nothing recorded anywhere, so all Playbot lanes disappear from WORKERS with no row, badge, or ALERTS entry explaining it. Concrete path: `bin/fm-playbot-lanes.mjs` imports `node:sqlite` at its top (line 82) and its header states it requires Node 22.5+ (line 74), so on a PATH whose `node` is older than 22.5 the module dies at import, `run.returncode` is 1, and no lane is ever listed for that whole session; the same empty result comes from node being absent, or from the 1.5s bound being exceeded on a loaded machine. This repo already treats ambient `node` as untrustworthy — `tests/lib.sh`'s `fm_test_find_node`/`fm_test_require_node` (lines 139/182, FM_TEST_NODE_MIN=22.5) search PATH then the known install roots for that reason, and this change hardened the lane test to gate on that resolver — but the production read kept the bare `node`, while docs/configuration.md:628 promises unconditionally that a live Playbot lane appears. The captain's stated requirement is that Playbot work is never skipped. Earliest shared boundary that would make that hold: resolve the runtime the way the suite already does (at least FM_TEST_NODE_MIN, else the fm_test_find_node roots) and/or emit the read's own reason as a row when the bounded read cannot answer.
