The claimed invariant - the sampler stops when its own board exits - holds only while no other board is open. `board_pid_state()` reads the home-wide `state/.crew-board-tui.pid`, and main.go:88-92 removes that file only when it still names its own pid, so with two boards open (A then B) closing A leaves the record naming B's live pid: sampler A's next tick reads `state == "live"`, and `if state == "gone" or (os.getppid() != parent and state != "live")` is false on both counts, so it keeps asking quota-axi every five minutes and rewriting state/crew-board-quota.json until B exits. Reachable and bounded by B's lifetime, and harmless to the payload (both samplers write the same snapshot), so this is a note rather than a defect; exiting on the parent change regardless of the shared record would make the earlier fix hold unconditionally.

test_phone_adb_fallbacks (lines 295, 298, 301, 304) and test_phone_check_unavailable (line 316) run the board with PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" and rely on that PATH holding no `adb`. bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:239-249 shows why PATH wins: `adb_binary()` calls `shutil.which("adb")` first and only then tries ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, ~/Android/Sdk and Linuxbrew, so any ambient adb on that PATH pre-empts the probe. Concrete: on a host with the distro package (Debian/Ubuntu `android-tools-adb` installs /usr/bin/adb), the first block of test_phone_check_unavailable resolves that binary, `local_phones()` returns its output or the "no device list" failure instead of the intended "adb was not found", and the assertions 'Phone check'/'adb was not found' fail against a correct implementation; the four fallback blocks likewise read the host binary (or jq yields null ids) instead of serial-android-home/serial-android-sdk-root/serial-home-sdk/serial-brew. The round-1 fix neutralized ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, HOME and HOMEBREW_PREFIX in these blocks but left PATH, which is the one path the resolver consults first. Run these blocks with a PATH that provably has the tools the board needs (sh, python3, jq, perl, mktemp, date) and no adb - a fixture directory of symlinks, or the neighbouring tests' stub-PATH pattern - so binary resolution is controlled rather than ambient.

run_board hands the board `${FM_CREW_BOARD_PHONE_QUEUE_ROOT:-$home/locks}`, `${FROGPILE_SUITE_LOCK:-$home/locks/frogpile-suite.lock}` and `${FROGPILE_SUITE_LOCK_HOLDER:-$home/locks/suite.holder}`, so an already-exported value silently replaces the fixture the test just built; the sibling helper run_panels (lines 48-49) assigns the same three variables unconditionally to $home/locks, so the two helpers address the same fixtures two different ways. Nothing else in the repo or the TUI harness sets these names (only bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:351-357 consumes them, with /tmp and ~/.frogpile-suite.lock.holder as production defaults, and docs/configuration.md documents them as operator-settable), so the `:-` has no producer to preserve and only defeats the fixtures. Concrete reachable failure: with FM_CREW_BOARD_PHONE_QUEUE_ROOT=/tmp exported, test_phone_testing_and_test_queue's refresh reads the host's real /tmp phone queues instead of $home/locks, and 'held phone is testing' plus 'phone group lists holder then waiters' fail; with FROGPILE_SUITE_LOCK(_HOLDER) exported, the $home/locks/suite.holder fixture is ignored and the FULL TEST SUITE heading/rows come from the host's live suite. Assign the three names unconditionally in run_board, as run_panels already does.

`panelSummary` derives every collapsed card's number from `len(rows)` plus a fixed noun, but for two panels the rows are not one per named item. (a) AI ALLOWANCE: `quota_entries()` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:957-966) appends aggregate bucket rows (`2 providers unavailable`, `1 provider unmeasured`) alongside the per-provider rows, so with four providers of which two report a broken state the card renders `AI ALLOWANCE  3 providers` (the aggregate row counts as a provider). This is the captain's own requested surface (`Also where is the cost thing you promised to show me`) and the exact complaint the labelled card was added for (`The bare number has no label`), so a number that does not match what it names reproduces the reported problem. Reachable input: the repo's own fixture in tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:483-490 feeds a `cursor` provider with `state.status` `auth_required`, which produces one bucket row next to every healthy provider. (b) TEST QUEUE: `nouns["test_queue"] = "queued"` while `test_queue()` rows are one per resource group member, including each group's `RUNNING: <task>` row (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:713-719), so a suite that is running with two waiters reads `TEST QUEUE  3 queued`. Fix by counting what the noun names (per-provider rows for allowance, running+waiting split for test_queue) rather than `len(rows)`.

`allowance_failure()` reports only the failure's age, and `refresh_allowance()` (line 909-933) throws the cause away: a non-zero exit, an unparseable payload, and a missing binary all collapse into the literal `quota-axi failed` / `quota-axi was not found...`, and the marker is written with `QUOTA_ERROR.touch()` so `state/.crew-board-quota-error` carries no content. A captain whose AI ALLOWANCE panel reads `Allowance check: no quota snapshot is recorded; the last quota-axi attempt failed 0m ago` therefore cannot tell an unauthenticated provider from a network outage from a missing quota-axi, while the two sibling checks rendered by the same panel do surface their concrete reason (`Phone check: adb was not found on PATH, under ANDROID_HOME...`, and `Playbot check unavailable: <binary> board-lanes exited N`). The marker is only tested for existence (tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:451) and read by nothing else, so writing the cause into it (e.g. the `run.stderr` tail or the exception text) and including it in the message is safe; otherwise state the actionable half only, since the age alone is not actionable.

The doc (and the module docstring at bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:16) promises READY FOR YOU lists "a finished scout report not yet relayed", but the scout branch at bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:833 keys on `hints.scout_report_present` alone. That flag is plain file presence (bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:835, `[ -f "$report_path" ]`), and nothing in the snapshot carries a completion or relay signal (`scout_reports[]` is only `{id, path, kind}`), while the two sibling branches in the same function require `done` (line 829 for the PR, line 831 for local-only). Reachable wrong label: a scout that has written its report and is then sent back for a review/fix round keeps the previous round's `data/<id>/report.md`, so READY FOR YOU shows "Investigation finished; read the report" while WORKERS shows the same task validating; the same row also stays listed after the report has been read and answered. Earliest supported boundary is the guard its siblings already use (require `current_state.state == "done"`), or drop "finished ... not yet relayed" from docs/configuration.md:628 and the module docstring if listing any scout that has a report is the intent.

After a refresh, `refreshedMsg` only drops a selection whose index is now out of range, and `selectReadable()` returns early whenever an in-range index exists. It never checks whether the row at that index is now a section heading. Concrete path: the captain replies to the last question under 'Your decisions'. Firstmate deletes that entry (AGENTS.md:514), so on the next 2s refresh the same index points at the 'For Tarun' heading. `selectedQuestion()` then returns nil, `readingQuestion` is never true because headings take the `continue` branch in panelLines, and no row is highlighted. The full-text view and the REPLY label disappear until the captain presses j. Moving a stale index onto the nearest selectable row (`selectableFrom(index, 1)`, falling back to `selectableFrom(index, -1)`) in the refresh path, or in selectReadable itself, would keep the invariant 'a selection never sits on a heading' that the keyboard paths already enforce.

`question_entries` now opens a new entry for every bold line, but it still flushes and starts a new question at every column-0 `- `/`* ` bullet, even when the current entry began with a bold title. AGENTS.md asks escalations to list options when applicable, so a likely entry is `**UIX. Pick the UI: four calls.**` followed by `- Prototype ...` and `- Claude Design ...` bullets. Each option becomes its own CAPTAIN QUESTIONS row (and its own reply target with a meaningless label), and the bold question's highlighted full text loses its options. That is the opposite of the requested 'show full questions when highlighting'. Keep column-0 bullets inside an entry that started with a bold title, closing it only at the next bold line, `##` heading or `---` (the bullet-before-bold fixture in test_questions_without_headings would still pass).

`phaseChip` draws the selected row's tag as dark text on the tag's phase colour, but the selection bar is itself yellow. For every yellow phase (`testing`, `validating`, `parked`, `due now`) the chip matches the bar exactly, so the tag reads as plain row text. The captain asked for the tag to 'stand out even if it's highlighted', and the VALIDATING/TESTING tags are the ones they called out. Cyan, red and green phases do stand out. Consider a contrasting chip (for example inverted or bordered) when the phase colour equals the highlight colour.

The empty READY FOR YOU message says it lists 'unread investigation reports'. Following the round-4 decision, the scout branch lists a scout whose state is done and whose report exists, and the docs and docstring were reworded to drop any read or relay claim. The board's own explanation text still makes that claim. Reword it to 'finished investigation reports' to match.

`resolve_node()` runs on every panel projection, and the TUI refreshes about every 2s. Each refresh therefore spawns one `node -p` probe per candidate (each with a 2s timeout) before the 1.5s lanes read. When PATH has an older node and the suitable one is under nvm or Linuxbrew, that means at least three node processes per refresh. Together with adb (2s), the worker-tag axi reads (2s budget) and the two tasks_axi reads (2s each), the worst-case serial budget exceeds the TUI's 8s refresh timeout. Caching the resolved binary (for example keyed on PATH and the override) would bound this.

test_playbot_lane_projection runs `PATH="$(dirname "$node"):$PATH"; export PATH` at script scope, not in a subshell or as a per-command prefix. Every test that runs after it (test_playbot_check_unavailable, test_full_questions_and_backlog, test_phone_testing_and_test_queue, and so on) therefore inherits the node install directory at the front of PATH. Most later tests pin PATH explicitly, so this is not a failure today. But a node install root such as Linuxbrew's bin can also hold adb or quota-axi, and those would then pre-empt the fixtures in the tests that use the ambient PATH (for example test_full_questions_and_backlog, and test_quota_check_unavailable's run_board). Scope the change to the two run_board calls, as in `PATH="$(dirname "$node"):$PATH" PLAYBOT_DESKTOP_DIR=... run_board ...`.

The docs say the lane read adds the unavailable alert when the runtime 'does not answer within 1.5 seconds'. The code applies that 1.5s bound only to `board-lanes` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:427). The runtime is first version-probed by node_probe with its own 2s timeout (line 348), and the new test asserts 'did not answer within 2s' for a hanging runtime. So a hanging node is reported after 2s with a 2s reason, and the worst case is about 3.5s per refresh. Reword the doc to describe both bounds.

The fix round's new guard `if entry and re.match(r"^\*\*(.+?)\*\*", entry[0])` checks the entry's stored first line, and a bullet entry stores `line[2:]`. So a bullet question whose text starts with a bold label (`- **UIX. Pick the UI.** Prototype or design.`) leaves `entry[0] == "**UIX. ..."`, which matches. Every following column-0 bullet is then appended to that entry instead of starting a new question. I checked this against the current code: with `## Your decisions` followed by `- **UIX. Pick the UI.** Prototype or design.` and `- **OPS. Release timing.** Choose the window.`, question_entries returns one question, 'UIX. Pick the UI.', whose detail also contains the OPS bullet. The OPS question disappears from CAPTAIN QUESTIONS, cannot be selected or replied to, and the QUESTIONS badge undercounts. Before this round each bullet was its own question. Fix: record whether the current entry was opened by a column-0 bold line (a flag set in the bold branch and cleared in flush), and keep bullets inside only those entries. Add a fixture with bold-led bullet questions to test_bold_question_keeps_its_options.

Following the round-1 prescription, `question_entries` now keeps every column-0 `- `/`* ` bullet inside an entry that began with a bold title, and closes that entry only at the next bold line, `##` heading or `---`. Blank lines do not close it (`elif entry: entry.append(...)`). So a section that mixes styles without a separator, such as `**OPS. Release timing.** ...`, a blank line, then `- Can we use the staging phone?`, folds the plain bullet question into the bold one. It gets no row or reply target of its own. AGENTS.md does not fix the register's format, so this can happen. The new test only covers the case where a `---` separates the two styles. This is noted as the accepted tradeoff of the prescribed rule, not as a defect.

`state_tag` decides whether a worker is waiting on the captain by checking only the raw `backlog.hold_kind == "captain"`. The snapshot's own contract says tasks-axi keeps `hold_kind` when a task is closed (see fm-captain-hold.sh:1035), and that `hold_bucket` is the single classification for captain holds; `hold_bucket` is null for Done rows. Concrete case: the captain answers "WA: as recommended", fm-captain-hold closes the task with `tasks_axi done`, and the worker's meta is still in `snapshot.tasks` while it wraps up. The row then still reads "WAITING ON YOU · WA" even though nothing is waiting on the captain any more. That is a wrong label with no error raised. Fix: use the snapshot's classification, either `backlog.hold_bucket is not None` or at least `backlog.state != "done"` (or `captain_actionable` if dated, aged and blocked holds should not count).

`question_label` treats any hold reason that starts with a 1–4 character uppercase token followed by '.', ':' or ')' as a captain-questions label. A reason such as "PR: waiting on review" or "CI: flaky" would therefore show "WAITING ON YOU · PR", which names no question. Lowercase-suffixed labels already used in captain-questions.md (e.g. "T4b.") never match either regex, so those rows lose their label. Consider checking the hold-reason label against the labels actually present in `questions` before using it.

The fallback match uses a bare substring test (`name in detail`) on the task id and decision keys. A short id or key, or one that is a prefix of another id (e.g. `art` vs `art-requirements`), can match an unrelated captain-questions entry; the first entry in file order wins and its label is shown. The real ids today are long and unique, so this is low risk, but a word-boundary match would make it robust.

`state_tag` sets `held` whenever `hold_bucket is not None`. That includes the `dated`, `aged` and `blocked` buckets (see fm-fleet-snapshot.sh:554-561), but docs/configuration.md says `WAITING ON YOU` appears only for "an open decision or a live captain hold". BEARINGS also treats non-live buckets as parked rather than captain-actionable (fm-bearings-snapshot.sh:380-382). Concrete case: a captain hold with `hold_until` set to a future date, or one still waiting on an unresolved blocker task, gets `hold_bucket` "dated" or "blocked". The row then reads "WAITING ON YOU · XX" even though the captain has nothing to act on yet. That is a wrong label with no error. Fix: use `hold_bucket == "live"` (equivalently `captain_actionable`) so the code matches the documented behavior.

The pause cause is found by matching words in `current_state.detail`, `hints.last_event_text` and the phase note. Those fields can hold text that has nothing to do with the pause. Concrete case: a worker paused for an upstream release whose last event was "review round 2 done" reads `WAITING FOR REVIEW`. Consider checking `current_state.detail` first and only falling back to the other fields when it is empty.

open_bugs drops any cached bug whose free-form status contains the word "QA" anywhere (case-insensitive `\bQA\b`). The intent is narrower: hide bugs that are *with* QA. Firstmate writes the status as free text, so a card QA has bounced back (for example status "QA failed", "failed QA" or "back from QA - reopened") would also disappear from ROCKETBOARD BUGS, even though it needs work again. Nothing errors when this happens. Consider matching the ownership phrase (for example `^\s*(with|in) QA\b`) or a structured owner field, rather than any mention of QA.

The held-backlog grouping logic did not change. At the base commit it already split on hold_kind: tasks_axi_full maps the hold_kind column into task["kind"], and the live crew-board.json already shows the UI comparison and the paused Tarun update under "Held for the captain". This change only renames "Held (other)" to "Waiting on others", adds a comment, and adds a regression test (kind: captain with hold-kind: external lands in the other group). That satisfies the intent, but the reported symptom was not caused by this code at the base commit, so the commit message's "group held backlog by hold kind" describes behavior that already existed.

docs/configuration.md:646-648 describes the cached `bugs` array as passed through as-is. It does not say that entries whose status mentions QA are now hidden from the panel. A one-line note there would stop cache authors being surprised when rows vanish.

crew_cwd_reconcile runs each relaunch one after another, in the foreground, inside the bootstrap child. fm-session-start.sh collects that child's output in BOOT_OUT=$(...) and runs it under the whole-digest bound (FM_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT, default 120s). Each `fm-control.sh relaunch` can wait up to EXIT_WAIT (30s) for the old agent to stop, plus settle time, plus LAUNCH_WAIT (90s) for the replacement to come up. That makes one worker's worst case longer than the whole budget. With the reported scenario of three misplaced workers, slow but normal launches (about 30-40s each) can also use up the budget. When the bound is hit, the process group is killed and two things go wrong. First, the buffered BOOT_OUT is lost, so the CREW_CWD lines already produced never reach firstmate and the digest only shows STARTUP TRUNCATED. Second, an fm-control transaction can be killed partway, after the old agent was stopped but before the replacement is confirmed; its EXIT-trap rollback does not run on SIGKILL. Suggested fix: move the relaunches out of the bounded local digest, either into a detached or deferred stage with its own deadline (as the network sweeps do) or with a per-relaunch time limit, and keep only the detection and reporting in the digest.

The slot holder checks that the agent is still alive only with `kill -0 <agent-pid>` once every 60s. If the agent exits and the kernel gives its pid to an unrelated long-lived process within that window, the holder stays in the copy indefinitely. Treehouse then keeps reading the slot as in-use until teardown reaps the holder. This is rare and teardown already reaps processes in the copy, so it is informational. To close it, also compare the process start time, or check that the pid's cwd is still inside the slot.

The detached relaunch worker only gets its own session when `setsid` exists. On macOS, which this repo supports and which has no `setsid` by default, it falls back to `nohup`, and nohup does not change the process group. fm-session-start runs the whole digest under fm_run_timed (timeout, gtimeout, or perl setpgrp), and when the bound expires it kills the entire process group (`kill -KILL -- -$runner_pid`). The nohup'd worker is still in that group. So if any later stage (wake-drain, fleet-state, network harvest) pushes the digest past FM_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT while a relaunch is running (the relaunch can take 30-120s), the worker is SIGKILLed partway through `fm-control.sh relaunch`. That skips fm-control's EXIT-trap rollback and queues no outcome wake, which is exactly the failure this fix round was meant to remove. Fix: in the fallback, also give the worker a new process group or session, for example `perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV'` (perl is already a fallback in fm-timeout-lib.sh) or a `set -m` background job, so the bound's group kill cannot reach it.

Detection does not know about relaunches that are already running in the background. If the digest truncates, the banner tells firstmate to rerun bin/fm-session-start.sh. The rerun's bootstrap can then see the same worker still in the primary checkout while the first background relaunch is still in progress, and it starts a second detached worker for the same task. fm-control's per-task CONTROL_LOCK try-acquire refuses that second relaunch, so it queues a 'check: crew-cwd: ... the automatic relaunch failed: ...; relaunch it into that copy with ...' wake. Meanwhile the first relaunch succeeds. Firstmate receives contradictory wakes, and the failure wake tells it to run a manual relaunch on a worker that was just moved. A small marker such as state/.crew-cwd-relaunch-<id> (written by the sweep, removed by the worker), or skipping ids whose control lock is held, would prevent this.

The detached worker never checks where the agent is before it relaunches. It re-reads the location only after a failure. The busy check in bootstrap protects only the one task whose fm-control lock is held at that moment; tasks still waiting in an earlier worker's list are not protected. Example: three workers A, B and C are found in the primary checkout. Run 1 starts worker W1, which is relaunching A while B and C wait in its list. The digest truncates and firstmate reruns session start. Run 2 sees A as busy, but B and C hold no lock, so it starts a second worker W2 for B and C. There are two bad outcomes. (a) W2 relaunches B successfully, and later W1 reaches B, takes the now-free lock, and relaunches B again. That throws away the replacement that just started, with a note that wrongly says the worker was found in the primary checkout, and it queues a second success wake. (b) W1 is in the middle of B's relaunch when W2 hits the lock refusal. The re-read finds the old agent stopped or the replacement not yet visible, so the read fails and W2 queues a false 'automatic relaunch failed' wake that tells firstmate to relaunch by hand. Fix: before each relaunch, have the worker re-read the location with fm_backend_agent_process and skip the task if the agent is already inside its copy. Treat fm-control's 'another lifecycle action is already running' refusal (or a held control lock or an active relaunch journal) as 'under way', not as a failure.

The round-3 fix the user chose (crew-cwd-worker-no-precheck-before-relaunch) is not in the code. The last commit, 3bb9f62, only covers the round-2 items. crew_cwd_relaunch_worker still calls `fm-control.sh <id> relaunch` without first re-reading the agent's location, and it takes no per-home lock to serialize crew-cwd workers. It re-reads the location only after a failure. The reported race is still reachable. Example: A, B and C are all in the primary checkout. Run 1 starts worker W1, which is relaunching A. The digest truncates and firstmate reruns session start. crew_cwd_relaunch_busy skips only A, whose control lock is held, so run 2 starts worker W2 for B and C. W2 relaunches B successfully. When W1 reaches B, B's lock is free again, so W1 relaunches B a second time. That discards the fresh replacement, sends a note that wrongly says it was found in the primary checkout, and queues a duplicate success wake. A second outcome: W2 hits the lock refusal while W1 is mid-relaunch, the re-read cannot see a live agent, and W2 queues a false 'automatic relaunch failed' wake. Fix as instructed: (1) right before each relaunch, re-read the location with fm_backend_agent_process and skip the task, reporting nothing, if the agent is inside its copy or can no longer be read as being in the primary checkout; (2) serialize workers per home with a lock from bin/fm-lock-lib.sh or fm-wake-lib.sh under $STATE, with a bounded wait, and exit with no relaunch and no failure wake on timeout; (3) add a test in which the agent is already back in its copy before the relaunch and the fm-control stub is never called.

The round-3 fix the user chose (crew-cwd-worker-no-precheck-before-relaunch) is still not in the code at 3bb9f62. crew_cwd_relaunch_worker calls `fm-control.sh <id> relaunch` without first re-reading where the agent is. It re-reads the location only after a failure, and no per-home lock serializes crew-cwd workers. The race is still reachable. Example: A, B and C are all in the primary checkout. Run 1 starts worker W1, which begins relaunching A. The digest truncates and firstmate reruns session start. crew_cwd_relaunch_busy skips only A, whose control lock is held, so run 2 starts worker W2 for B and C. W2 relaunches B. When W1 later reaches B, B's control lock is free, so W1 relaunches B again. That throws away the fresh replacement, sends it a note that wrongly says it was found in the primary checkout, and queues a duplicate success wake. A second outcome: W2's relaunch is refused while W1 is partway through B's relaunch. The re-read cannot see a live agent at that moment, so W2 queues a false 'automatic relaunch failed' wake. Fix as instructed: (1) right before each relaunch, call fm_backend_agent_process and skip the task, reporting nothing, if the agent is inside its copy or can no longer be read as being in the primary checkout; (2) serialize workers per home with a lock from bin/fm-lock-lib.sh under $STATE, using a bounded fm_lock_acquire_wait, and on timeout exit with no relaunch and no failure wake; (3) add a test in which the agent is already back in its copy before the relaunch and the fm-control stub is never called.

To check whether a task is busy, crew_cwd_relaunch_busy briefly takes the task's fm-control lock (fm_lock_try_acquire, then release). If a real `fm-control.sh <id> ...` starts during that short window, its own fm_lock_try_acquire is refused with 'another lifecycle action is already running', even though nothing else was running. The window is tiny and the refusal can be retried, so this is informational. A probe that does not take the lock would avoid it, for example checking the lock's holder or the relaunch journal phase.

The new header-tab click path ignores the help overlay and filter modes. View() leaves lastRects nil in those modes, so panel clicks are already ignored there, but a click on the tab row (Y==2) still calls setPage. Concrete failure: press `/` on the WORKERS panel, type a filter, click the PLANNING tab, then press Enter. setPage has already changed m.focus to pages[1][0].id, so `m.filters[m.focus] = m.filterInput.Value()` applies the filter to the wrong panel, and the panel the user meant to filter gets nothing. With help open, the page also switches silently behind the overlay. Fix: return early from the Y==2 branch (or skip it) when m.help or m.filterActive is set, which matches how keyboard page switching is blocked in those modes.

The commit adds a compiled Go binary of about 7.6 MB (bin/fm-crew-board-tui/fm-crew-board-tui), most likely left behind by a local `go build`. bin/fm-crew-board.sh:180 builds the TUI into state/.crew-board-tui-bin, so nothing reads this file. It bloats git history for good and goes stale as soon as the sources change. Fix: remove it with `git rm --cached` and add it to .gitignore.

The tag assertion is written as `!Contains(coloured) && !Contains(plain)`, so it passes whenever the plain text is present. It never checks that the row is drawn in the magenta pr-ready colour. A separate check compares phaseColor values directly, so this is only a weak assertion.

A worker waiting on a merge now gets Status "pr-ready" instead of its real phase. The `/` filter matches on Title, Detail and Status, so filtering by the real phase name (for example "ready-to-merge") no longer finds these rows. This is a minor behaviour side effect.

The 'stopped' alert depends only on the existence of `.dead-reported-<key>`. fm-watch.sh deletes that marker in one place: `wedge_dead_record` (bin/fm-watch.sh:1080), which runs only when an idle pane goes stale again. Nothing in clear_stale_hash_tracking or clear_pause_tracking removes it. Concrete case: a worker's agent dies, the marker is written, and firstmate respawns the agent in the same window. The worker is now busy and never goes stale, so the marker stays. The board keeps showing '<task>: stopped' as a NEW notification ('Its work is not progressing … Ask firstmate to recover the worker') for a worker that is actually running. The dead check also wins over the wedge check, so a recovered worker cannot show as anything else. Suggested fix: only alert when the dead marker is newer than the task's `.status` mtime, or when the task's current_state is not active.

`watcher_verdict()` returns {} on OSError, on the 5 s timeout, or when the script prints no `state=` line. `watcher_alert()` treats an empty state the same as 'unavailable' and raises 'Monitoring status unavailable — No watcher heartbeat was found'. A slow or failing verdict probe therefore produces a false major notification with nid `monitoring:status`, claiming no heartbeat exists when one may be fresh. Before this change, that message appeared only when the beat file was missing. The intent's core complaint was spurious monitoring alerts. Suggested fix: on probe failure, return None or a distinct 'monitoring check failed' row. Keep the 'unavailable' wording for an explicit `state=unavailable`.

The API_ERROR pattern is matched against the free-form worker status detail and last_event_text, and it includes broad terms such as `rate.?limit`, `connection (?:reset|refused|error|lost)` and `network error`. A worker whose task is about these topics trips it. Example: a current_state detail of 'Adding rate-limit middleware' or 'Handle connection error retries' raises a NEW '<task>: API or network error' notification while nothing is wrong. That is a wrong result with no error raised. The intent asks for 'a worker whose pane shows an API or network error'. Suggested fix: anchor the match to agent or harness error shapes (e.g. a leading 'API Error:', HTTP 5xx/429 codes, or error event kinds) rather than topic words.

`suite_wait_alerts` measures the wait with `process_age(pid)`, which is the age of the blocked process since it started, not how long it has waited on the lock. If the process that requests the flock is a long-lived runner that did other work first (e.g. 25 minutes of setup before taking the suite lock), the 30-minute alert fires after a few minutes of real waiting, and its 'Since N ago' text overstates the wait. This is accurate only when the waiter is a dedicated `flock` process started at queue time.

`markViewed` runs after every key press or click while the ALERTS panel is focused, and it marks the row at the remembered `selected["alerts"]` index. That index carries over across refreshes and focus changes. A newly arrived alert that lands at the old cursor index is drawn with the selection style, and rowLine hides the NEW tag for selected rows. The next unrelated key press (or tabbing back into ALERTS) then marks it seen without the product owner having picked it. Separately, the loop guard in `markViewed` that checks `index == m.selected["alerts"] && !selected` is hard to follow. Checking `m.focusedItem()` plus the expanded index directly would be clearer.

With the probe-failure fix, a failed or timed-out `fm-monitoring-verdict.sh` (an empty verdict) now produces no monitoring row at all. A real 'Monitoring down' is therefore hidden, with no sign on the board, while the probe itself is broken. This is the tradeoff the prior finding offered ('return None or a distinct row'). It is noted only so the choice is deliberate.

`decisions_summary` builds its 'Since N ago' text from the oldest `hold_set` among all captain holds in the backlog. It never checks whether those holds belong to the open questions in data/captain-questions.md. A captain hold can be for a preview or a landing approval, both of which READY FOR YOU lists. Example: a preview hold set 3 days ago plus one question added 5 minutes ago gives '1 open question is waiting for your answer. Since 72 hours ago.' The number is wrong and nothing errors. Suggested fix: count only holds whose task is tied to a listed question, or leave out the 'since' clause when that link can't be made.

`pruneSeen` removes the seen record of any alert missing from one refresh. Since the round-2 fix, a failed or timed-out `fm-monitoring-verdict.sh` probe drops the monitoring row for that refresh. So a 'Monitoring down' alert the product owner already viewed loses its seen record when one probe fails. On the next successful refresh it comes back highlighted as NEW, though the issue never cleared or changed. Any alert whose source read fails for one refresh behaves the same way. Optional follow-up: only prune after the row has been absent for a few refreshes, or keep the seen record when the verdict probe failed.

`decisions_summary` counts every row that `question_entries()` returns, and that includes the `## ` heading rows it emits with status "section". The other callers and tests filter those out with `select(.status != "section")`. Two examples of the wrong result: (1) the register layout in `test_full_questions_and_backlog`, with 4 `## For …` headings over 4 bullet questions, produces "8 decisions waiting on you". (2) A register left with only `## Your decisions` after every question was answered produces a NEW "1 decision waiting on you" alert when nothing is waiting, which breaks the required empty case. The decisions test hides this because its fixture `## A. Which release?\nPick one.` writes the questions as headings, so the 2 "questions" it counts are really section rows. Fix: filter `questions` to `status != "section"` before the empty check, the count, `labels`, `details`, and the sig. Then change the fixture to real entries (for example `**A. Which release?** Pick one.`) under a heading, and add a heading-only register case that expects no alert.

The new `asks()` repeats the hold-reason label regex and the question-title label regex from `question_label()` (line 811). It also adds a looser id match: `str(record["id"]) in details` matches any substring across all question details, so a short backlog id such as `rel` matches 'release'. Sharing one label-extraction helper with `question_label` keeps the decisions alert and the WAITING ON YOU tag consistent.

The intent gives the example format "Claude/Codex/Playbot/Pi(Model-Name)", which suggests the model sits next to the harness on the WORKERS row. The change puts only the short runtime on the row (`status = rt.Runtime + "  " + status`). The model appears only in the expanded detail ("Runtime: Pi (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash), effort …"), and the Go test explicitly asserts the row does NOT contain the model. Please confirm that keeping the model in the detail view is acceptable rather than showing `Pi(Model)` inline.

The Playbot lane entries in worker_runtimes skip runtime_entry's normalization. The lane effort is passed through raw (`str(lane.get("effort") or "")`), so a lane whose execution_reasoning_level is "default" or "-" shows ", effort default" in the detail. Task-meta entries drop those values. Running the lane effort through the same filter would make the two consistent.

The runtime label is put in front of the status before `ansi.Truncate(status, max(8, width/2), "…")`, which cuts from the right. On narrow terminals, or with long tags like "WAITING ON YOU · <question label>", the runtime now pushes more of the state/PR tag off the row, and that tag carries the actionable signal. This is acceptable if intended. Otherwise, the runtime could go after the tag, or be dropped first when space is tight.

`phone_locks` runs after `phone_activity` and sets status to `unavailable` (and so raises a `Phone X unavailable` alert) whenever `adb -s <serial> shell dumpsys window` takes longer than 1s, exits non-zero, or contains none of the four keyguard field names. This overrides a phone that was just marked `busy`. `dumpsys window` output is large and slow on a phone that is running tests, and recent Android builds may not print these fields in `dumpsys window` at all. In either case a healthy, busy registered phone shows `Unavailable` in the test queue and raises a spurious alert. The probe also runs up to three sequential blocking adb shells on every refresh. Suggestion: when the keyguard state is unknown (None), keep the existing busy/idle status, or record it only in the detail, instead of downgrading the phone to `unavailable`. Probing only idle phones would also help.

The test queue maps every phone status outside idle/busy/locked/unavailable to `disconnected`. Two cases get the wrong label. (1) When adb itself fails (not found, timed out, non-zero exit), `phones` holds only the id-less `Phone check` row, so all three PHONE_ORDER sections read `Disconnected` even though the board could not check. The alert path guards against exactly this with `not any(adb == 'unavailable')`. (2) An attached phone that adb reports as `unauthorized` or `offline` keeps that adb state as its status, and the queue also shows it as `Disconnected`. Suggestion: map an adb failure to `unavailable` and pass unauthorized/offline through, or show them as unavailable.

With ALERTS moved into the rail, the only way to open a rail row's detail or mark a notification seen is a mouse click (`railHit`). Previously `j`/`k` or opening a row on the ALERTS tab did both, through `markViewed`. A keyboard-only user can now scroll the rail with Ctrl-n/p but cannot acknowledge notifications, so the header's new-alert count never clears for them. Please confirm that mouse-only acknowledgement is intended, or add a key to step through and open rail rows.

`markViewed` returns early unless `m.focus == "alerts"`, and `alerts` is no longer a sub-tab on any page, so it can never be focused. Its call on every key press and click in `Update` (app.go:447) is now dead code and can be removed.

`alertCount(0)` now adds `len(m.newAlerts())` to the NOW page tab badge, even though notifications live in the rail on every page and the header already shows a counted new-alert highlight. The `1 NOW` tab therefore advertises alerts that page 1 does not contain, which duplicates the header signal.

`suite_queue_root()` falls back to `FROGPILE_SUITE_LOCK + ".queue"`, but its only caller, `queued_suite_waiters`, switches to the legacy `/proc/locks` reader whenever `FROGPILE_SUITE_LOCK` is set without `FROGPILE_SUITE_QUEUE`. That fallback branch is unreachable, and the two functions disagree about what setting `FROGPILE_SUITE_LOCK` means. Remove the branch or make the two functions agree.

A used provider (claude, codex, openrouter) whose quota state is `auth_required`, `expired`, or `error` is folded into the quiet `N hidden` count, and no alert is raised. The intent asked to hide providers that are not set up or not used. A provider the user relies on that has lost its auth is arguably a real issue rather than noise, but it is now indistinguishable from copilot or cursor.

Every backlog record with state `in_flight` is labelled `in progress`, including ones the fleet snapshot marks as held. A held record is an in_flight record with hold_reason and hold_kind set, which fm-fleet-snapshot.sh gives current_role "held". Example: an owner bug parked for the captain's preview shows `in progress · <id>` in BUGS even though nobody is working on it. Fix: check record.get("current_role") == "held" (or hold_reason/hold_kind) and show `held` or the hold reason instead.

The intent says Rocketboard bugs "needs to be prioritized first before mine are taken up". The change only lists Rocketboard rows above owner bugs in the BUGS panel. Nothing in the repo (docs, AGENTS/skills, dispatch scripts) makes firstmate start Rocketboard bugs before owner `Bug: ` backlog items. If "taken up" means dispatch order and not just display order, that requirement isn't implemented yet.

reset_time takes `resetsAt or resetText` and returns `unknown` for any string that isn't ISO 8601. A human-readable resetText, or an unparseable resetsAt next to a usable resetText, used to be shown as-is and now reads `unknown`. Cached allowance rows (used before the sampler's first good snapshot) also keep their raw detail and don't get the IST format. Current quota-axi output gives ISO resetsAt, so live rows are fine.

Focused Godot runs are counted as full suites. FrogPile's tests/run_tests.gd (_focus_filter) only takes `--focused` / `--focused=<name>`. The exclusion list checks exact `--focus` and the prefix `--focus=`, and neither matches `--focused=foo` or `--focused`. So `godot --headless -s tests/run_tests.gd -- --focused=SomeTest` shows up as a RUNNING full suite and raises the `EDITOR: N running` count. `--lock-check-only` probes are counted the same way. Fix: add `--focused` (exact and `--focused=` prefix) and `--lock-check-only` to the exclusions, and update the fixture test to use the real flag.

service_suite_rows only half-validates the test service's status.json. It checks the schema, and that each request is a dict with an options dict, but a few malformed fields still raise outside the try: `request.get("steps", [])` set to null or a non-list (TypeError); a non-dict step before the suite step in the `next(...)` scan (AttributeError, because any() filters with isinstance but next() does not); and `duration(request.get("wait_seconds"))` with a non-numeric string (ValueError). Any of these crashes the whole fm-crew-board-panels.py run, so every panel on the board goes blank, not just the Editor section. fm-test-service is still being written, so its output may not be stable. Fix: coerce `steps` to a list of dicts and guard wait_seconds, or skip any request that fails to parse.

A service-run Godot process is matched to its status.json request only when its realpath equals `runs/<id>` exactly. If the service launches Godot from a subdirectory (e.g. `runs/<id>/prototype-game`, the way run_suite.sh is laid out), the process and the service entry are both shown and one run counts as two. A prefix match (like process_owner uses) would hold up better once the service's launch cwd is settled.

suite_progress takes the last log line matching `N/M` or `N of M`, and the word `tests` is optional. Lines like `Loaded 3 of 12 scenes` or a `10/23` date in a Godot log would show up as `Progress: 3/12 tests`. Requiring the runner's actual progress format would avoid wrong progress labels.

The old loop over queued_suite_waiters still applies `WAITING FOR FULL SUITE #n` tags, and the new rendering loop applies the same tags again over suite_queue. Only the first assignment sticks (resource_tag keeps the first tag at equal priority). They agree today, but the old loop could become a plain list() so the tag logic lives in one place.

Sharded suite runs are counted as several full suites. Current FrogPile (tests/run_suite.sh with SUITE_SHARDS=2|4, through tests/run_sharded_suite.py) starts 2 or 4 `godot ... -s tests/run_tests.gd -- --selection-file res://tests/.suite-selection.json` processes, one per `<run_dir>/project-N` copy. The exclusion list does not include `--selection-file`, so each shard becomes its own RUNNING row. Their cwd is outside any task worktree, so process_owner falls back to labels like `project-0`. One sharded suite then shows as `EDITOR: 4 running`, and none of the rows names the owning task. The same happens to a service request that shards: every shard is matched and shown as its own row. Fix: treat `--selection-file` processes as shards and group them under their parent process (the run_sharded_suite.py PID, resolved to its worktree), counting them as one run. Simply excluding them would drop the run entirely whenever the holder fallback does not apply.

The tightened progress regex no longer gives false positives, but the real runner never prints an `N/M tests` or `N of M tests` progress line. It prints `TEST <path> ...` and `TEST <path> done in Xms`, and its only `N of M ... tests` line is `FOCUSED x: N of M tests` for focused runs, which are excluded. So the `Progress:` label documented in docs/configuration.md as 'log progress when available' will in practice never show for full suites. If progress matters, count `TEST ... done` lines against the registered test total.

Service waiters are de-duplicated by source worktree path (`waiting_cwds.add`). If the test service has two queued or preparing requests from the same source worktree (for example two SHAs from one task), only the first is listed, so the waiting count comes out one short without any error.

A shard can show the wrong test total for a few seconds. For a `--selection-file` shard, suite_counts falls back to registered_suite_tests(project) whenever its log has no `SHARD SELECTION:` line yet. That is the case while Godot is still starting, because run_sharded_suite.py opens a fresh shard-N.log. Each shard's --path copy contains the full run_tests.gd (232 tests), so a 4-shard run briefly reads `0/928 tests` instead of `0/232`. If some shards have printed their selection and others have not, the total is mixed. Fix: skip the registry fallback for selection-file shards (return None until SHARD SELECTION appears), so the group shows no progress until every shard knows its total.

The serve loop stops at the first 'preparing' row (`if row["state"] == "preparing": break`), and only `recover_preparing` at service startup ever moves such a row on. A row is 'preparing' while the submitting worker's own `submit` process runs `git clone --no-local` and the fetch. If that worker is killed or interrupted partway (SIGKILL, SIGTERM, or Ctrl-C/KeyboardInterrupt, which `except Exception` does not catch), the row stays 'preparing' forever. Every request queued after it, for any project, then waits until someone restarts the daemon. This breaks the required behaviour that the service 'survives ... the worker AI going quiet'. Fix: have the daemon take over stale 'preparing' rows, for example by recording the submitter's pid or a heartbeat and running `recover_preparing` for dead submitters on every loop pass. Alternatively, do the clone in the daemon and leave `submit` to insert the row only.

On startup, requests that were running are put back in the queue with `queued_at=now`. The scheduler orders by `queued_at,seq`, so these requests now sort behind every request that was waiting when the daemon stopped. Example: FrogPile has 4 requests running and a 5th queued, and the daemon restarts. The 5th takes a slot first and one of the 4 earlier requests now waits. This breaks the required arrival order ('runs requests in arrival order') across restarts. Fix: keep the original `queued_at` (or order by `seq`) when requeueing interrupted requests.

`config(row["project"])` is called in the main serve loop with no exception handling. If a queued request's project config file is deleted, made invalid, or edited to a bad `max_concurrent`, the loop raises a ValueError, OSError or JSONDecodeError and the daemon exits. systemd restarts it (`Restart=always`), the same queued row raises again, and the service crash-loops; no project's requests run. Fix: catch config errors for that row and complete it as `failed` with the config error, as `retest_moved` already does.

`first_error` returns the first log line that matches `(?i)(FAIL|ERROR|Assertion|Exception|not ok)` anywhere in the line, case-insensitively. Harmless earlier lines therefore match: a test named `test_error_handling`, a progress line like `0 errors`, or `Failures: 0`. In those cases the failure record and the `error` shown in status name the wrong test and message, and nothing signals it. The intent requires recording the 'first failing test and message'. Fix: anchor the pattern to the suite's real failure markers (for example `^(FAIL|not ok|SCRIPT ERROR)` or word boundaries), or let the project config supply a failure pattern.

If the snapshot clone in `submit` fails after the request was cancelled while 'preparing', the unguarded `UPDATE ... SET state='failed'` overwrites the terminal 'cancelled' state. The success path guards with `AND state='preparing'`; add the same guard here.

With `--retest-on-move` and `--receipt`, a passing retest writes the receipt for the rebased SHA into the worker's receipt path. That replaces the valid receipt for the worker's own HEAD with one for a commit the worker does not have, so `fm-merge-local --receipt` will reject it. The FrogPile brief does not pass `--retest-on-move`, so the default path is unaffected. Confirm whether retests should keep their receipts only under `results/`.

The approved plan calls for 'a general service with a small per-project configuration'. Two FrogPile-specific behaviours are hardcoded in Firstmate code instead: the service defaults `max_concurrent` to 4 when the project is named 'frogpile', and `fm-brief.sh` matches `frogpile|FrogPile|ProjectWhite`. The example config already sets `max_concurrent: 4`. Confirm whether these should come from the per-project config.

"a Playbot-executed run must never be reported as the suite's verdict" is wider than the problem it describes. The problem is the engine bridge (`execute_engine_code`) pausing on an expected `push_error`. But line 286 of the same doc says a direct `!` shell command from the controller goes through Playbot's `thread/shellCommand` route and can run the project's native automation. That route is shell-launched and returns the runner's own verdict, so it is also "Playbot-executed". As worded, the sentence forbids a valid Playbot-run full-suite entry point, which is the first option the F9 intent offers. Suggested fix: say "a bridge-driven (`execute_engine_code`) run" instead of "a Playbot-executed run". Optionally, mention the controller `!` shellCommand route as a way to run the pinned suite runner when a lane must stay in Playbot.

The green-final-head brief now tells every worker to run `$FM_ROOT/bin/fm-test-service.py submit … ` and `… wait`, and AGENTS.md names `bin/fm-test-service.py` as the receipt producer. That file is not on this branch or its base (e2d3bbb/main). It exists only in commit 784494e on the unmerged branch `fm/fm-test-service`. If this change lands first, every `--green-final-head` worker gets a command that fails with "No such file or directory" and cannot produce `data/<task-id>/suite.receipt`. `fm-merge-local.sh --receipt` then has nothing to consume. The intent asks to coordinate with the producer owned by fm-test-service, so either land this after (or together with) fm/fm-test-service or gate the guidance on the producer existing. Needs an owner decision on merge order.

The scaffolded command passes `--task <id>` to `fm-test-service.py submit`, but the producer's argparse (784494e, bin/fm-test-service.py:494-501) only accepts project, worktree, sha, --suite, --device-gate, --scenario, --harness, --receipt and --retest-on-move. A worker running the brief verbatim hits `error: unrecognized arguments: --task green-receipt` (exit 2), so no request is queued and no receipt is written. The test at tests/fm-brief.test.sh:562 locks this wrong argument in place. Either drop `--task` (the task is already identified by `--receipt data/<id>/suite.receipt`) or add `--task` to the producer in the same coordinated change.

The unmerged producer branch (784494e) also edits fm-brief.sh in the same region, around HEALTH_MARKER. It adds a FrogPile `TEST_SERVICE_GUIDANCE` block telling workers to write the receipt to `"$PWD/full-suite.receipt"`. When the two branches merge, they will conflict textually, and a FrogPile green-final-head brief could carry two different receipt locations. The intent requires a single task-specific `data/<task-id>/suite.receipt`. Reconcile the two blocks when the branches are combined.
HEADROOM_REPORT=1 duplicates MODE=headroom: both are set together and the dispatch could just check `[ "${MODE:-}" = headroom ]`, the same way aggregate mode does. This is optional cleanup.

The report adds every successful script row to the drift list, including ones that finished faster than their hint. When fewer than five scripts outgrew their hints, the 'largest drifts' output can include negative deltas. The output stays correct because it prints delta_ms, but readers should know these are signed drifts, not only overruns.

The new diagnostics (structured error, completed read count, offending IPC calls, one message per condition) only cover the vanished-workspace refusal block. The receipt check and the new audited-inventory check in the concurrency test still exit with a bare `process.exit(1)`, so a failure there doesn't print the observed receipt sha or the recomputed hash. Each check does have its own `fail` message, so the condition can still be told apart. This is optional hardening, not a contradiction of the intent.

Every request permanently leaves three copies on disk. `submit` makes a full `git clone --no-local` under `repos/<id>`. `execute` makes a working checkout under `runs/<id>`, which the FrogPile `prepare` step fills with a Godot import cache. `retest_moved` makes a scratch copy under `rebase/<id>`. None of these is deleted after the request finishes; the only `rmtree` calls run before a re-run of the same id or on a failed submit. On this PC (four parallel FrogPile requests, each ship task submitting, plus retests) the state directory grows by roughly one full repository plus one imported checkout per request until the disk fills. Then every later clone fails and the service can no longer test anything. Fix: delete `runs/<id>` (and the `rebase/<id>` scratch copy) once the request finishes, keeping logs and results. Delete `repos/<id>` once a request is finished and not set to retest on move, or has been cancelled.

`retest_moved` has no stopping point once the submitted commit has landed. After the worker's commit is merged, `original_sha` is an ancestor of the new landing tip. `merge-base` then returns `original_sha`, the rebase produces the landing tip itself, and the service queues a full suite and phone run of that tip. This repeats on every later landing-branch move, for every `--retest-on-move` request that was ever submitted and not cancelled. With N such landed requests, each push to `proto/godot/frog-pile` queues N identical runs of the same tip, filling FrogPile's four slots and the shared suite and phone queues ahead of real worker requests. Fix: when `git merge-base --is-ancestor original_sha tip` succeeds, stop retesting that request (mark it settled, or clear `retest_on_move`) instead of requeueing it.

Every 5 seconds, `reclaim_finished` loads every terminal request the service has ever handled. For each one it parses its options and runs two or three `shutil.rmtree` calls, even when those copies were deleted long ago. The cost grows with history without limit, although it is small at current volumes. A later fix could record that a request's copies were reclaimed, or select only rows finished since the last pass, so the loop touches only new work.

The macos-stock-bash job timeout went from 10 to 25 minutes (.github/workflows/ci.yml:477), but tests/fm-ci-workflow.test.sh:150 still pins `macos-stock-bash 10` in test_measured_lanes_keep_their_existing_bounds. That test reads the workflow YAML and fails with "macos-stock-bash timeout must stay 10 minutes, got 25". Change the pinned expectation to 25 and note that the new cap comes from the eight per-consumer bounds (17.5 minutes) plus setup headroom.

In fast board mode the cache key covers meta and status checksums, so any new status line from a worker throws away that worker's last live observation. Until the background observer finishes a full cycle (about 12 s+ with 19 workers), the worker shows `{state:"unknown",source:"none"}`. Two board behaviours depend on that live state. First, fm-crew-board-panels.py:1422 lists a PR as ready to merge only when `current.state == "done"`, so a merge-ready PR drops out of the ready list whenever its worker appends a status line. Second, task_json_one clears lifecycle-superseded open decisions only for a working run-step or pane source; with source `none`, stale decisions come back. Because notify.go drops the seen record when a cause clears, a returning decision can show up as a new alert. This can briefly reproduce the symptoms in the intent: the merge call is missing and an old question is shown. Options: keep the previous observation with a 'stale' marker, or observe changed and uncached tasks synchronously, which is cheap when only a few changed.

board_cached_observation captures status and report before checking the task generation, and keeps those captures when the generation no longer matches. prefetch_task_observations does the opposite: it removes `$id.status`/`$id.report` and reports 'task generation changed during snapshot'. In fast mode, a task relaunched mid-snapshot can therefore pair new-generation status with old captured metadata. Fix: on generation mismatch, remove the captures and write the same 'generation changed' observation as the slow path.

board_observe_one returns early when cp or mv fails and never removes `$tmp` or the `*.tmp.$$` files. Each failed observation leaves a temp dir in TMPDIR and partial files in state/crew-board-observations. Run cleanup on every exit path.

Nothing ever prunes state/crew-board-observations, so .json/.endpoint/.stamp files for closed tasks build up forever. A reused task id whose legacy metadata has no spawn_gen, with identical meta and status contents, would also match the old stamp and inherit the previous run's observation. Fix: in board_observe_all, delete cache entries that have no matching `$STATE/<id>.meta`.

start_board_observer has a lock race. A refresh can see the lock directory after the observer's mkdir but before it writes its pid; it then treats the lock as stale, removes it, and starts a second observer, whose lock the first observer's EXIT trap later deletes. The results are harmless because cache writes are per-id and atomic, but two observers can overlap and repeat the expensive probes.

The new regression test asserts that a 30-worker refresh finishes in under 7 seconds of wall-clock time. That checks the right behaviour, but the result depends on machine speed and may flake on slow or shared CI runners, such as the macOS compat runner.

The stale-observation fix covers status-line changes only. The cache is reused only when `${stored%%|*}` equals the current meta checksum, so any metadata write drops the task back to `{state:"unknown",source:"none",detail:"live observation pending"}` until the observer runs again. At least two common writers change metadata at the moments that matter here. First, bin/fm-pr-check.sh:122-123 rewrites `pr=`/`pr_head=` when the PR is checked, which is exactly when a PR becomes merge-ready, so the PR drops out of the ready list, which needs `current.state == "done"`. Second, bin/fm-captain-hold.sh:1666 appends `decisions_reviewed=1`/`decision_keys=`; with source `none` the lifecycle clearing in task_json_one is skipped, so decisions that were already cleared reappear. Both are the symptoms named in the intent, and they break the instruction 'do not fall back to unknown'. Task identity is already checked separately by snapshot_task_generation_is_current, both before and after the read. Fix: when the stored meta checksum differs but the generation is still current (spawn_gen matches, or legacy metadata is identical), serve the record as `stale`, the same way a changed status is handled. Add a test that appends `pr=` to the metadata.

When the board clears a decision that the live state has moved past, it sets the phase to the bare live state (`phase_name=$current_state`, usually `working`). This drops the worker's last reported phase. Example: the log has `phase: testing - suite`, then `needs-decision: [key=q] ...`, and the observation is working/run-step. status_current_phase tracks `worker=testing`, and a normal `working` line would give `testing`. Here the row shows plain `working` with no TESTING tag, because phase_tag only shows names in PHASE_WORDS. This only affects how the row looks: the decision and alert are cleared correctly. Fix: have the override fall back to the worker's last reported phase (for example, status_current_phase could also report it), and use current_state only when there is none.

The intent offers 'a bounded coordinated landing window' as one snapshot-policy option. The rendered contract says only 'the landing tip is held still from the first capture through the final suite', with no time limit or coordination owner. The other option (a moved tip invalidates the evidence, with a re-capture budget of one) is fully stated, so the intent's either/or is met. Still, a worker or firstmate reading the 'hold still' branch has no limit on how long other landings can be frozen behind a long suite.

The duplicate check calls json.loads on every existing ledger line with no error handling. If one line is malformed (for example a partial write after a crash or a full disk), every later `record` raises JSONDecodeError. All three teardown call sites (bin/fm-teardown.sh:1102, 1256, 4033) treat that as fatal (`|| exit 1` / `status=1`), and they run after irreversible cleanup such as removing the worktree, the home and TASK_TMP. One bad line therefore blocks every future teardown until someone repairs the file by hand. `summary` (line 305) crashes on the same input. Fix: skip lines that fail to parse in both the duplicate check and summary.

blocked_count only matches lines that start with `blocked:`. The repo also writes keyed and correlated blocked lines such as `blocked [key=...]: ...` (bin/fm-pending-reply-lib.sh:1262, bin/fm-procevent-remote-reply.sh:529), and status_line_verb in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh strips `[key=..]` and `corr=` tokens before reading the verb. Those blocked events are recorded as 0, so the stall evidence the intent asks for is undercounted without any error. Fix: parse the verb the same way status_line_verb does (first word before `:` or `[`).

captain_rejected and captain_corrected are true only when a status line contains the literal text 'captain rejected' or 'captain correction'. Nothing in bin/ writes those phrases to a task status file, so both fields are false for essentially every task. The ledger reads that as 'not rejected or corrected', which is a wrong value rather than an unknown. The intent says to judge each route by whether it was 'rejected or corrected afterwards'. Also, a correction that happens after landing cannot be seen at teardown time. Decide whether to define a real producer (for example captured learning candidates or a status verb), or record these as null/unknown until one exists. The validation_rounds and failed_rounds substring heuristics are similarly fragile, because worker prose has no fixed vocabulary.

fm-spawn now runs `quota-axi --json` on every non-relaunch spawn, only to take a metadata snapshot, with no timeout. If quota-axi hangs, spawn hangs while holding the spawn meta lock. bin/fm-procevent-quota.sh bounds the same call with fm_run_timed, and fm-timeout-lib.sh is already sourced in spawn. Fix: wrap the call the same way, and treat a timeout as snapshot-unreadable.

`claude-sonnet-5` appears twice in the price table (lines 11 and 14). The values are identical, so the result is the same today, but the JSON parser silently keeps the last one, so editing only the first entry later would have no effect. Remove the duplicate.

Claude session discovery walks every project directory under ~/.claude/projects and opens every .jsonl modified since dispatch, then compares its cwd exactly against the meta worktree string. On busy hosts this is a large scan at teardown time, and any difference in path form (a symlink, /private/var versus /var) silently gives a null cost. Consider limiting the scan to Claude's encoded project directory for the worktree and resolving both paths before comparing.

Learning candidates are matched on origin_task alone. Task ids can be reused: the ledger deliberately keeps a separate row per incarnation (instance_id/started_at), and the test records `missing-task` twice. Nothing filters candidates by time, so a captain-correction or review-rejection captured against the first incarnation is recorded as `captain_corrected: true` (and listed in `learning_candidates`) on every later incarnation's teardown row. The `--state` join in `summary` (line ~372) also flags every row with that task id, including earlier incarnations, so a rejection on the second run counts against the first run's rule too. The result is a wrong outcome value with no error, while pipeline_rounds already scopes by `created_at >= started`. Fix: keep `captured_at` per candidate, and count a candidate for a row only when captured_at >= that row's started_at (in summary, also before the next incarnation's started_at for the same task id).

The summary's `--state` join builds each row's upper bound (`until`) only from `started_at` values already in the ledger. A task incarnation that is still running has no ledger row yet, so it sets no bound. Concrete case: task X lands and gets row 1 (rule A). X is dispatched again under rule B and is still running. A captain-correction or review-rejection candidate is then captured for the running X. The weekly summary binds that candidate to row 1, because its until is None and captured_at >= its start, and counts rule A as rejected or corrected. Nothing errors. When the second incarnation is later torn down, the same candidate counts for both rows. Fix: `summary` already reads `--state`, so also take `routing_started_at` from `state/<task_id>.meta`, when present, as an extra incarnation start when computing `until`.

A red receipt on the bottom car can stall the queue with no wake to firstmate. This happens when the receipt names a failure that is not in the landing tip's landing-health baseline, or when the tip is red and no baseline has been recorded yet. In both cases the car is quietly set back to `needs-final` while its receipt stays recorded, and no ready or failed wake is emitted. The brief tells workers to rerun the full suite on `needs-final`, so the worker reruns, gets the same red result, resubmits, and gets `needs-final` again, forever. Firstmate never learns that it needs `fm-merge-local.sh --base-receipt` or that the car has a new regression. Concrete case: tip T is red with failure X and has no landing-health receipt; car A submits a receipt with failures=1 and failure=X; status returns needs-final, the wake count stays 0, and the loop repeats. Suggested fix: report a distinct status such as `red-receipt` / `needs-baseline`, or treat the car as failed, and emit a deduplicated wake so firstmate can record the baseline or the worker can report `failed:`.

`refresh` checks whether a car's branch still exists before it checks whether the car has landed. If firstmate fast-forwards car A with fm-merge-local and then tears it down (fm-teardown.sh deletes the branch with `branch -D`) before any queue call runs, the next `status` from any worker marks A as `failed`. That emits a spurious 'landing-queue failed ... reason=local branch missing' wake, and A's own status reports `failed` instead of `landed`, which can lead A's worker to report `failed:`. Suggested fix: when the branch no longer resolves, check whether the recorded head is an ancestor of TIP (`git merge-base --is-ancestor "${heads[i]}" "$TIP"`) and mark the car `landed` if so, `failed` otherwise.

Firstmate's operating instructions say nothing about the new `landing-queue ready-to-land` and `landing-queue failed` check wakes. AGENTS.md routes other check wakes (contributions, procevent, x-mention, and so on) to a skill or procedure, and only docs/architecture.md describes what firstmate should do here: recheck status, apply merge authority, run fm-merge-local with the receipt, push when authorized. The payload also lacks the `check:` prefix that other check wakes use. The intent says 'the firstmate tool should be handling' the train, so the firstmate side should have explicit routing. Without it, firstmate may fall back to asking the worker or coordinating by hand. Suggested fix: add a one-line routing entry in AGENTS.md for landing-queue wakes and use the `check:` payload prefix.

`event_reason` is taken from this invocation's `--reason` for every newly failed car in the queue, not only the car being failed. If car A runs `fail --reason 'suite failed'` in the same call that first notices car B's branch is missing, B's failure wake says 'suite failed' instead of 'local branch missing'. Suggested fix: use REASON only when i == found.

A failed car's reason is kept only in memory for the invocation that failed it. The queue snapshot has no reason column, and every loaded row resets `reasons[i]=-` (line 150). Both the brief and the landing-queue skill depend on that reason reaching the worker, so this breaks the handoff. In the needs-baseline flow, the skill has firstmate run `fm-landing-queue.sh fail <id> --reason <those failures>` and says the worker reports `failed:` from its own status. The worker's brief says "At `failed`, report `failed:` with the status `reason`". The worker's next `status` call loads the row fresh and prints `reason=-`, so the failures firstmate identified never reach the worker or its `failed:` line. The same loss happens for 'local branch missing' on any call after the one that detected it. Concrete case: firstmate runs `fail a --reason 'new-red'`, then worker a runs `status a`, which prints status=failed and reason=-. Fix: persist the failure reason in the queue row (add a sanitized column to the format, which is not yet released) and print it for failed cars. Add a test asserting that a later `status` call by a different invocation still returns the recorded reason.

A car whose receipt has failures beyond the tip's baseline is handled two different ways depending on whether a baseline happens to be recorded. If one is recorded, the queue reports `red-receipt`, and the worker can fix the failures on a new head and finalize again under the same task id. If none is recorded, the queue reports `needs-baseline`. Firstmate then gets a tip receipt, finds the extra failures, and the skill tells it to run `fm-landing-queue.sh fail <id>`. That makes the car terminal: it cannot rejoin, and the work has to restart under a new task id. The cause is that firstmate has no way to record the tip baseline without also landing, because only fm-merge-local calls fm_health_store, so it cannot turn this case into `red-receipt`. Please confirm that the stricter outcome is intended. If it is not, one option is to let firstmate record the tip baseline (for example via a queue or landing-health command), after which the queue would naturally report `red-receipt` and leave the fix with the worker.

`refresh` marks any active car as `landed` when its live head is an ancestor of the landing tip. A worker that runs `ready` with a head that adds no commits beyond the tip passes admission, because refresh runs before the join. On the next `status` call the car becomes `landed`, and the brief then tells the worker to append `done: landed {branch} at {head}`, even though firstmate never merged anything. Suggested fix: in `ready`, reject a head that is already an ancestor of TIP (for example, die with 'nothing to land').

`baseline` checks the receipt against `$TIP`, but `$TIP` was read during `refresh` before the landing-health lock was taken. The queue lock does not stop `fm-merge-local.sh`, so the tip can move in between. Concrete case: `fm-merge-local` holds the health lock, fast-forwards the landing branch to T2, and stores T2's receipt. `baseline` then gets the lock and validates the supplied receipt against the old tip T1. The recorded receipt now names T2, so the conflict check is skipped, and `fm_health_store` replaces T2's baseline with T1's receipt. The next red landing then has no baseline for the current tip and needs `--base-receipt`, and the queue reports `needs-baseline` again. Both commands are normally run by firstmate one after the other, so this is unlikely in practice. Suggested fix: after acquiring HEALTH_LOCK, run `resolve "$LANDING"` again and stop with 'landing tip moved; recheck status' if it no longer equals `$TIP`, which is what fm-merge-local.sh already does before it merges.

The new empty-car check in `ready` only refuses a head that is already in the landing tip. A stacked car whose head adds nothing beyond its assigned target is still admitted. Concrete case: car a is queued, and worker b branches from fm/a and runs `ready` before committing, so b's head equals fm/a's head and is not in the tip. When firstmate lands a, `refresh` sees b's head as an ancestor of the tip and marks b `landed`. The brief then tells b's worker to append `done: landed`, although nothing of b's was merged. Suggested fix: when `joined=1`, after `assign`, refuse if HEAD is an ancestor of `target_shas[found]`. That extends the round-4 fix to the same invariant for stacked cars.

`baseline` checks the receipt against `$TIP`, but `$TIP` was read in `refresh` before HEALTH_LOCK was taken. The queue lock does not exclude fm-merge-local.sh. Race: fm-merge-local holds the health lock, fast-forwards the landing branch to T2, and stores T2's receipt. `baseline` then takes the lock and accepts a receipt for the old tip T1. The stored receipt names T2, so the conflict check is skipped, and fm_health_store replaces T2's baseline with T1's receipt. The current tip then has no baseline, and the queue goes back to needs-baseline. Fix: after taking HEALTH_LOCK, run `resolve "$LANDING"` again and die with 'landing tip moved; recheck status' if it no longer equals $TIP. fm-merge-local.sh already does this check.

`ready` refuses an empty car only when its head is already in the landing tip. A stacked car whose head adds nothing beyond its assigned target is still admitted. Example: worker b branches from fm/a and runs `ready` before it commits, so b's head equals a's head. After firstmate lands a, `refresh` sees b's head as an ancestor of TIP and marks b `landed`. The brief then tells b's worker to append `done: landed` even though none of b's work merged. Fix: when joined=1, after `assign`, refuse admission if HEAD is an ancestor of target_shas[found]. This applies the round-4 invariant to stacked cars.

The new ownership check in the skill compares the raw directory from `fm_backend_agent_process` with the raw `worktree=` value from the record, and it never says to resolve symlinks first. `fm_agent_process_cwd` reads `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, which is always the fully resolved path. The recorded worktree can be written through a symlink. This host has exactly that case: `/home -> var/home`, and paths show up in both spellings. So an agent that follows the skill literally would see `/var/home/.../wt` against `worktree=/home/.../wt`, call a correctly owned pane foreign, refuse the steer, report the task blocked or failed, and relaunch it, losing its conversation. `crew_cwd_reconcile` already avoids this by passing both sides through `fm_slot_canonical_dir` (`pwd -P`) before comparing. Fix: have the snippet print the resolved worktree too, e.g. `cd "$(fm_meta_get <meta> worktree)" && pwd -P`, or tell the reader to compare the `pwd -P` forms of both paths.

The intent asks to suppress the Codex startup update prompt "at launch and resume". The override only exists in fm-spawn's launch template, so it covers fresh spawns and `fm-control relaunch`. The incident the new comment describes is a different path: a host restart where Herdr restores the pane and resumes the agent itself (see bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1662, "Herdr restores the pane and resumes the agent"). Nothing in this change shows that Herdr's own resume replays firstmate's `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false`. A per-launch override is deliberately never written to ~/.codex/config.toml, so a Herdr-resumed codex pane after an upgrade may still stop on the prompt. The comment at fm-spawn.sh:1901-1904 says a resumed worker is the case this protects, but that only holds for `fm-control relaunch`. Please confirm whether Herdr-native resume is in scope. If it is, it needs a separate mechanism, or the skill should note that restored panes still need a check for the prompt.

The intent requires the rendered brief to name "the three-line fm-full-suite.v1 form (schema=, sha= of the full head, failures=0)" and "the sanctioned pass-record producer owned by fm-test-service". When `--green-final-head` is used on a repo with no test-service project, the brief only gets the receipt path and the line "No test-service project is configured for this repository; ask firstmate to configure one". That brief never names `bin/fm-test-service.py` or the three-line form, because both only appear in TEST_SERVICE_GUIDANCE, which is gated on `-n "$TEST_SERVICE_PROJECT"`. Please confirm that dropping the producer and the form from unconfigured green briefs is intended. If it isn't, render the producer path and the schema/sha/failures form in this branch as well.

The new `# Evidence and access` section is rendered in every ship brief no matter the project or delivery mode. Local-only and direct-PR briefs, which forbid /no-mistakes, still get the no-mistakes gate guidance, and non-FrogPile projects get the FrogPile `tests/task_evidence/*.log` instruction. Each line is conditionally worded, so this is only prompt noise, but it could be gated by mode or project if brief size becomes a concern.

The new `[ ! -s "$publish_two_out" ]` check only shows that the second listing hadn't finished within about 3s. It doesn't show that the second listing actually reached `withRoutesLock` while the first publisher was paused, so on a slow host it can pass without exercising the interleaving. The later receipt and audited-inventory checks still catch the real invariant, so no change is needed. A stronger version could have the shim record the second process's lock attempt.

The post-creation `requireEngineReadiness` call (dispatch, after `createChat`) now also raises the graphical-capture refusal, but that refusal doesn't name the chat that was just created. The not-ready branch builds the `created` suffix ("Chat X remains in workspace Y; inspect this pair before retrying so no second pair is created"), but the `Graphical capture is unavailable` error leaves it out. Concrete path: the preflight read sees a non-headless or no-session instance, so capture is `unproven` and the preflight passes. The chat is created. The second read then sees the routed session as headless and ready. Dispatch throws with no mention of the created chat, so a caller who retries creates a second chat. Fix: add the same `created` suffix to the capture refusal, or compute `created` before both checks.
