Readiness can only be `ready` when the routed instance is `type === "headless"`, because the `session-unconfirmed` check requires that. So every project in a ready report has `graphicalCapture.status === "unavailable"`, which means `requiresGraphicalCapture: true` can never pass an engine-dependent dispatch. It works purely as a pre-dispatch refusal that points to an ordinary worker. This matches the intent's 'precise verdict' option, but the schema description ("Require the routed engine session to be able to supply rendered editor screenshots") reads as if it could succeed.

In a multi-root workspace the first root to finish decides `ipc.contract.status` (`classifyEngineContract` ignores later results). If root 1 returns the readable contract and root 2 throws 'No handler registered' or returns a changed shape, the report says `version-verified`/`capability-verified` while `errors` holds the later root's channel fault. The verdict still fails closed as `unconfirmed`, but the contract label for that workspace is misleading.

Intent conformance: the intent requires "2. Resolve the lost TERM. A watcher that survives SIGTERM must be reproduced and fixed: bin/fm-watch.sh's stop path must terminate while a poll is in flight". The commit message says the opposite: "The watcher's lost TERM in the wild is NOT claimed fixed. It was not reproduced here." The fm-watch.sh hunk (one `trap watcher_stop HUP INT TERM` plus a deferral flag, replacing `trap 'FM_CHECK_SIGNAL_PENDING=1'` and then `trap 'exit 1'`) behaves the same as before in every window it touches. On the base commit the disposition during `wait "$FM_ACTIVE_CHECK_PID"` was already `exit 1`, so test_stop_terminates_a_poll_in_flight (tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh:280) would pass without this change. It is not a failing-first reproduction of a watcher that survives TERM. The likely cause the commit itself names (a TERM lost shortly after a background fork, 2/150) is left for a follow-up. The user needs to decide whether to accept this as containment plus diagnostics, or to require the reproduction and fix that the intent marks as required.

A stop recorded during the deferred window is silently dropped on the pgid-mismatch path. If TERM arrives while FM_WATCH_STOP_DEFERRED=1 (FM_WATCH_STOP_PENDING=1) and `ps` then reports a pgid different from FM_ACTIVE_CHECK_PGID, the branch stops the check and does `return 1` without checking watcher_stop_pending. The next run_check_capture resets PENDING=0, so the watcher keeps polling after a stop it received. That is exactly the lost-TERM class this change targets. Fix: honor the pending stop in that branch too (e.g. `watcher_stop_pending && exit 1` after cleanup), or check it before the branch, since fm_active_check_stop has already run.

The fix-round commit does not meet requirement 3 of the user's narrowing. Commit 7ab4ef8 has only a subject line ("Revert fm-watch.sh; defer lost TERM to lesson-f16b") and no body. It never states that the change pins only the fixture reap bound and its regression, that bin/fm-watch.sh is unchanged, or that the TERM lost shortly after a background fork (measured 2 of 150 runs) is not reproduced or fixed here. Meanwhile the earlier commit 3f1e26d still says "bin/fm-watch.sh installs its ONE stop handler once and never swaps it ... now defers through the same handler", which is now false. If the branch is squashed or read commit by commit, the history says a stop-path change shipped when none did. Fix: reword the fix commit (or the combined message) so it states those points plainly and drops the stale fm-watch.sh paragraph.

Intent half 2 ("Resolve the lost TERM ... must be reproduced and fixed") is still not implemented. bin/fm-watch.sh is byte-identical to base. The user explicitly chose this narrowing in round 1 and deferred the work to lesson-f16b, so it is recorded here only for traceability. test_stop_terminates_a_poll_in_flight passes on base too, so it pins an existing contract and is not a fail-first regression; its comment now says that honestly.

The user's round-2 decision (review-r2-1) has still not been carried out in the branch history, and the intent requires the commit message to state the narrowing plainly. Fix commit 232b628 has only a subject line ("Revert fm-watch.sh; defer lost TERM to lesson-f16b") and no body. The earlier commit 708c332 still says "To hold up under that last assertion, bin/fm-watch.sh installs its ONE stop handler once and never swaps it ... now defers through the same handler and honors the recorded request at its next safe point". That is false: `git diff 442ee30 232b628 -- bin/fm-watch.sh` is empty. No commit states that bin/fm-watch.sh is byte-identical to base, that test_stop_terminates_a_poll_in_flight pins existing behavior rather than a fix, or that the TERM lost after a background fork (2 of 150 runs) is filed as follow-up lesson-f16b. The name lesson-f16b appears only in the bodiless subject. Fix as already decided: fold 232b628 into 708c332 under one corrected message that drops the stale fm-watch.sh paragraph and states those points. If rewriting history is not supported, give the fix commit a full body that states them and explicitly supersedes the stale paragraph, and put the same statements in the PR description.

The capability probe checks only the top-level list items (`engineKind` and an absolute `projectPath`). The snapshot fields that readiness actually depends on (`instances`, `routedInstanceId`, `connectionBlocked`, `lifecycleStatus`, `pluginStatus`, `type`) are not part of the classification. Concrete case: a future Playbot keeps the list shape but renames `routedInstanceId`. The report then says `ipc.contract.status: capability-verified`, while every project fails as `connection-unconfirmed`/`session-unconfirmed` instead of `shape-changed`. The dispatch still fails closed, but the contract label points the operator at the wrong repair. A follow-up could fold the per-project snapshot shape check into `classifyEngineContract`.

The new `get_engine_readiness` tool description says it reports "whether rendered editor capture is available or merely unproven". `graphicalCaptureCapability` never returns `available`: it returns only `unavailable` (headless) or `unproven`, and the docs say so. Callers reading the tool description will expect an `available` status that can never occur. Reword it to "unavailable or merely unproven".

`bridge-not-connected` is added to the list of diagnostic verdicts ("distinguishes `addon-drift`, `missing-addon-files`, `startup-pending`, ..."). It is a reason code whose verdict is `unconfirmed`, not a verdict of its own, so a reader may expect `report.verdict === 'bridge-not-connected'`. Describe it as an `unconfirmed` reason code instead.

landing_gates_for_repo runs json.loads on every config/test-service/*.json file before it checks whether the file matches the repo. The sibling project_for_repo skips files that fail to parse or validate. bin/fm-landing-queue.sh:103 now runs this lookup for every action and dies on any non-zero exit. So one malformed or half-edited config for an unrelated project makes every queue command fail for every repository, including `status`, `fail`, and `baseline`. Workers then cannot record failures or see their place in the queue. Suggested fix: keep failing closed when a file's stem equals the repo, or when a file that parses lists the repo, but skip files that don't parse and can't match (the way project_for_repo does). That limits the failure to the affected project.

Gates are found by the basename of the primary checkout. If that name doesn't equal a config file's stem or appear in its `repos` list, the lookup returns no gates and a green suite becomes ready-to-land, as it did before this change. This matches how fm-brief resolves the test-service project, and the FrogPile example lists its repo-name variants, so no change is needed. It is still the one way the real-phone hold could be bypassed without any error, so the `repos` list is worth keeping complete.

A captain hold whose reason mentions a preview shows up twice in "Needs you". `full_backlog()` puts it under "Held for the captain" as "Title [repo] - reason", and `ready_entries()` also emits it as a `preview` row titled "Title". The held-for-captain loop only checks for duplicates against the decisions already in `needs`. The later `ready` loop (line 108) appends the preview row without any duplicate check, so the owner sees the same hold once as "Held for you" and again as "Approval needed". Fix: skip held rows whose task id matches a `preview` ready row, or dedupe the ready loop against existing needs. The `id` field is present in both panels, so matching on id is more reliable than the current title-prefix match.

Every URL in the page is relative (`api/board`, `details#…`). With the documented `tailscale serve --set-path /crew-board` mount, opening `https://host/crew-board` without a trailing slash makes the browser resolve `api/board` to `/api/board` and `details` to `/details`. Those requests go to the existing `/` proxy, not this server, so the page stays at "Stale · last update unavailable" and the detail links break. `/details/` is broken the same way: the server accepts it via rstrip, but the fetch then goes to `details/api/board`. The backend cannot tell these cases apart because Serve strips the prefix. Fix: at startup in the page script, if the overview path does not end in `/` (or the details path does), call `location.replace` to the normalized path.

The SECRET regex also accepts plain whitespace as the separator, so ordinary task titles get mangled without any error. For example, "Rotate token handling" becomes "Rotate [redacted]", "Fix password reset flow" becomes "Fix [redacted] flow", and "Pin the node version" becomes "[redacted] node version". The keyword and the following word are both replaced, so worker, decision and needs titles show wrong text. Fix: require `[:=]`, or a whitespace-separated value that looks like a secret (for example one containing a digit), so the "PIN 1234" case is still caught.

Intent item 5 says the page must be "Reachable only by the product owner over the private Tailscale network". The server itself does not enforce that. It trusts any request arriving on loopback, and `tailscale serve` exposes the mount to every tailnet member the ACL allows. On a shared company tailnet, this criterion holds only if the operator has an owner-only ACL, which docs/configuration.md asks for but does not check. Ask the user whether a documented ACL is enough, or whether the server should also check Serve's `Tailscale-User-Login` header against a configured owner login.

The overview shows at most 5 "Needs you" rows and, unlike the workers and landing sections, has no "All" link. If the first five are merge rows (which link out to GitHub), the remaining decisions and blockers cannot be reached from the page. Fix: add a `details#decisions` "more" link, at least when the list is truncated.

The SECRET pattern only redacts the word right after the keyword. If a filler word sits between the keyword and the value, the value still shows, for example in hold-reason titles from "Held for the captain". "phone PIN is 1234" and "PIN - 1234" are both left unchanged, because the word after `PIN` ("is" or "-") contains no digit. The pre-fix regex had the same gap, so this is not a regression. If those phrasings matter, the redaction could also cover a digit-bearing word within one or two words of the keyword.

The intent says "Phone mode is an on/off switch; firstmate sends a push notification for new questions only while it is on." The diff only stores `state/crew-board-phone-mode` and adds a docs line saying "firstmate reads this state to decide whether to push when adding questions". Nothing reads that file and nothing sends a push. The only readers are the phone server and its test. The captain-questions contract in AGENTS.md section 9 ("Raising a question with the captain adds its entry in the same turn…") was not updated to tell firstmate to check phone mode and push. So turning the switch on changes nothing, and the docs describe behavior that does not exist.

The intent says "Every section, including Design, UI and Art, needs cards and a forward action." The diff adds Forward only when `/^For (UI|Design|Art)/.test(card.section)`. Cards under "Your decisions" or any other section get no forward action. Real registers can also name sections after people: tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh uses `## For Tarun`, `## For Arshnoor` and `## For Aleksandra`. In a home laid out that way, no card gets a Forward button at all. Please confirm whether every card should be forwardable. If only teammate sections should be, match any `For …` section instead of three fixed words.

`questions()` only recognizes lines that start with `**LABEL. Title**`. The crew board's own parser, `question_entries` in bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:64, also accepts bulleted entries (`- **A. …**`, `- Which release?`), checkbox prefixes, and `---` separators, and the existing tests use these forms. I ran the function on `- **A. Which release?** Pick one.`: no card is produced. A later `- Which phone?` line gets glued onto the previous card's body. So open questions can silently disappear from the Decisions tab, or show "No open questions.", while the terminal board still lists them. That breaks "Each open question is a card". Fix: share or mirror `question_entries`' entry splitting (bullets, checkboxes, `---` ending an entry). Also either show unlabeled questions as cards, or say clearly in the UI that they cannot be answered from the phone.

Decisions load only when the tab is tapped. The 5-second `refresh()` updates only the board, and a card stays tappable after "Sent to Firstmate". Answered cards therefore stay on screen after firstmate deletes the entry until the owner taps the tab again, and repeat taps queue duplicate inbox notes. Consider reloading decisions on the existing interval while the tab is visible, and disabling a card's controls after a successful send.

The fix round sets `options_open = bool(BOLD.match(...))` after a bulleted bold entry. The crew board's `question_entries` (bin/fm-crew-board-panels.py:100-104) does not do this. As a result, any plain bullet directly after a bulleted bold question gets folded into that question. I ran `questions('## Your decisions
- **A. Release?** Pick.
- Which phone?
- **B. X?** y
')` and got only cards A and B. "Which phone?" vanished into A's body, while the terminal board lists it as its own question. This is the same drop the earlier parser-drops-questions finding described, and it is still reachable. Fix: after a bulleted bold entry, absorb only following bullets that look like options (for example `^[-*]\s*\([a-z]\)`) and let any other bullet start a new entry. That keeps the new `- (a) Play` test passing and matches the board for other bullets. Add a test case with a plain bullet directly after a bulleted bold question.

Unlabeled cards under a `For …` section now get a Forward button. `forward()` always builds `${card.label}. ${card.title}`, so the shared text for these cards starts with a stray ". " (for example ". Which phone?"). Leave out the label prefix when `card.label` is empty.

The last round fixed the stray ". " prefix only in `forward()`. The card heading still renders `${card.label}. ${card.title}`, so an unlabeled card (for example `- Which phone?`, which the tests now produce) shows the heading ". Which phone?". Use the same conditional prefix here: `${card.label ? card.label + '. ' : ''}${card.title}`.

Answers are identified only by the label: the inbox note is `A: …`, and both the `sent` map and the server's `known` check key on the label. If two sections reuse a label (for example `A` under Your decisions and `A` under For Tarun), the inbox note doesn't say which question it answers. Answering one card also locks the other card and marks it "Sent to Firstmate". Consider including the section in the note and keying `sent` on section+label.

The intent says the `tests/fixtures/fm-brief/ship-no-mistakes.md` fixture "already pins the generated block", but no test compares against it any more (see the comment at tests/fm-brief.test.sh:1389-1396). This change leaves the fixture without the three new sentences (fixture line 85 still ends the paragraph at "Do not hand-edit..."). Nothing breaks because of this, and the new `assert_grep` checks on the generated brief cover the sentences. The fixture just drifts further from the real output until someone regenerates it.

The new routing-record check makes teardown refuse every task whose meta has no routing_* keys, and `--force` does not get past it. Per the cited routing review, 16 of 17 live tasks have no `routing_started_at`, so after this lands none of them can be cleaned up or retired (secondmate/scout/lane retire paths run after this check too). The relaunch fix doesn't help them, because `preserve_relaunch_routing_meta` only copies keys that already exist. The diff had to add routing keys to `write_legacy_meta` in the tests to keep the legacy-meta teardown tests passing, which shows the same break. The ledger writer already handles this case honestly (`fm-routing-ledger.py:132,373` reports 'start time absent from legacy metadata'). The intent asks that such tasks be 'reported rather than silently ledgered'; a permanent refusal with no bypass goes further than that. Options: let `--force` (or a dedicated flag) bypass the check, or warn loudly and write the ledger row with an explicit missing-routing reason instead of exiting.

`routing_rule=manual` still passes the check, because only empty or absent values are rejected. A task spawned without `--routing-rule` therefore still reaches the ledger as `rule: manual`. That behavior is documented and intentional at spawn time. Still, the intent's goal of not 'silently ledgered as manual/null' is only met for the missing-key case. Confirm that's the intended boundary.

On the first `serve()` start after this upgrade, the startup replay calls `queue_notification` for every historical passed, failed or cancelled request (`SELECT * FROM requests WHERE state IN (...)`), because the new `notifications` table starts empty. Each old row that carries a valid `--task` and whose task still has a `.meta` file then gets a fresh "Test service completion ... Resume this request's work" steer. Old rows have no `home`/`state_dir`, so they fall back to the service HOME. Live workers whose results were already consumed, or were already pinged by the session stopgap loop (different body, so idempotent dedupe will not collapse it), get woken for stale requests. Each wake costs a full-context turn, which is the cost this change exists to cut. Consider limiting the replay to requests with no outbox row that finished after the table was created (for example, record a migration marker/timestamp, or mark pre-existing terminal rows as already 'skipped' when the table is first created), so only true crash gaps are replayed.

Upper cars are now `waiting-for-front` for the whole time every lower car runs its full suite and phone gate, which the train now does one after another. The brief still tells them to "keep checking queue status every 30 seconds". Each check is a full-context worker turn, and nothing wakes a car when it reaches the front: queue wakes go to firstmate only for ready-to-land, needs-baseline and failed. A car three places back could poll for hours. That keeps the polling pattern the intent asked to remove ("Why is the worker waiting. Can we not use hooks?") and may cancel out much of the token saving from testing once at the front. Consider emitting a durable inbox steer (as the test service now does) when a car's place becomes 1, and telling `waiting-for-front` workers to pause and end their turn.

`queue_notification` freezes only the first terminal result (`INSERT OR IGNORE`). A `--retest-on-move` request that passed and later fails on its rebased retest, or goes to 'conflict', never notifies the task. Workers using the still-documented `--retest-on-move` flag would not learn about the regression. This is intentional per the docstring, and the brief no longer uses that flag, so it is noted only.

A notification whose task `.meta` still exists but whose `fm-send` keeps failing is retried every ~5 s forever, logging each time. Examples: a retired task that left its meta behind, or a remote endpoint where `fm-send`'s own 30 s remote budget races the 30 s subprocess timeout. On typed or remote planes `FM_SEND_IDEMPOTENT` does not dedupe, so a timeout after a successful send can duplicate the message. Consider a retry cap or backoff, and marking the row skipped after N failures.

The new retry cap marks a notification `failed` after 12 attempts, about 30 minutes with the backoff. The only signal is a stderr line in the service log. Under the new brief the requesting worker has already posted `paused:` and ended its turn, so after an fm-send outage of about 30 minutes that worker sleeps forever, and nothing wakes firstmate. That is the same stuck-worker failure (lesson-p22/p25 etc.) this change exists to remove. The cap stops the endless retry loop but turns a transient delivery failure into a silent permanent stall. Consider publishing a firstmate wake when a notification reaches the cap, through the shared durable wake queue as the landing queue does, so a person or firstmate can resume the task.

Queue reconcile runs only on the fully successful path. If `fm_health_store` fails after the ff-merge has already moved the branch, the script prints "landing SUCCEEDED" and exits 3 before `fm-landing-queue.sh reconcile`. The next car's worker is paused at `waiting-for-front`, so it is never steered until some other queue invocation happens. The same gap applies when a bottom car leaves the train only through `refresh()`, for example when its branch is deleted, because nothing invokes the queue. Running reconcile, which only warns on failure, before the exit-3 return would close the merge-local case.

A notification stuck in 'escalating' retries `escalate_notification` every ~5 s with no cap or backoff, and logs each attempt. This happens when the wake-queue append keeps failing, for example when the notice's `state_dir` is unwritable or was removed with its home. It is a smaller version of the earlier unbounded-retry issue. Consider reusing the delivery backoff (min(5·2^n, NOTIFY_MAX_DELAY)) for escalation retries. Separately, dedupe uses only the keys still in the queue (`fm_wake_queued_keys_locked`). A crash after the append but before `state='failed'` commits, followed by firstmate draining that row, would publish the wake a second time on replay. That window is narrow and acceptable.

The brief still tells workers at `ready-to-land` or `needs-baseline` to "keep checking queue status every 30 seconds". Each check is a full-context worker turn. Nothing steers the worker when its car becomes `landed`: the only steering message the queue sends is the front steer, and the merge-local reconcile steers only the next car. `needs-baseline` waits on a firstmate decision and can last a long time. This leaves a polling loop in place, against the intent ("Why is the worker waiting. Can we not use hooks?" … "with no polling"). Consider having reconcile send the landed car's worker one durable steer, using the same front-marker pattern, and changing the brief so these states post `paused:` and end the turn.

Still unaddressed from round 4. A notification stuck in 'escalating' calls `escalate_notification` every ~5 s, with no cap or backoff, and logs every attempt. This happens when the wake append keeps failing, for example when the notice's state_dir is unwritable or was removed. Reuse the delivery backoff (min(5·2^n, NOTIFY_MAX_DELAY)) for escalation retries. Also, dedupe checks only keys still in the queue. If the process crashes after the append but before `state='failed'` commits, and firstmate drains the queue in that window, the wake is published again. The window is narrow.

The `--consumer` allow-list is kept in two places (the usage string and the `case`), separately from the IDs passed to `run_consumer`. If they drift, for example a new consumer is added to the `case` but its `run_consumer` call uses a typo'd ID, or an ID is renamed in only one place, then `--consumer X` passes validation, every `run_consumer` returns early, `compatibility_failed` stays 0, and the script exits 0 without running anything. That is a false pass on exactly the local proof path the new guideline sends contributors to, and the guideline requires adding consumers, so this drift is likely. Fix: set a `ran_consumer=1` flag inside `run_consumer` after the selection check, and fail with an error at the end if `selected != all` and no consumer ran. That also lets the duplicated `case` list go away.

The documented example `/bin/bash bin/fm-stock-bash-compat.sh --consumer merge` defaults `STOCK_BASH` to `/bin/bash`. On Linux, or on macOS with a newer Bash at /bin/bash, the consumer then runs under Bash 4/5 and reports 'Stock Bash consumer passed' without proving Bash 3.2 compatibility. The prose above it says to use Bash 3.2 or set `FM_STOCK_BASH_BIN`, but the script never shows which runtime it used. Printing the child runtime version (e.g. `"$STOCK_BASH" -c 'echo "$BASH_VERSION"'`) next to the timeout-mechanism line would make a non-3.2 local run visible.

The new test unsets `RUNNER_TEMP`, so the script creates `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-stock-bash-compat.XXXXXX` outside the fixture root. That directory is not registered with `fm_test_cleanup` and has no `.fm-test-fixture` marker, so every test run leaves one behind in /tmp. Pass `TMPDIR="$tmp"` in the `env` call so the generated log root lands inside the cleaned fixture, and optionally assert that the printed 'stock Bash logs:' path exists.

The new floor check warns on most fresh dispatches, not just prepaid ones. Subscription providers like claude and codex have no `credits` object in the quota-axi snapshot (see the fixture in tests/fm-crew-board.test.sh:437), so every Claude or Codex dispatch prints 'warning: claude credit balance absent or unreadable; prepaid credit floor was not checked'. It also warns when quota-axi isn't installed. When no provider is resolved it prints 'warning:  credit balance unreadable (provider-unresolved)' with an empty provider name. These warnings make it look like a prepaid check was skipped on providers that aren't prepaid, which weakens the signal when an OpenRouter balance really can't be read. Suggested fix: only warn when the provider's snapshot row has a `credits` object that can't be read (wrong unit or a non-number `remaining`), or when the provider is known to be prepaid. Stay quiet for providers that report no credits at all. This changes the documented 'absent balance warns' behavior, so it needs the author's decision.

For `--secondmate` spawns, the credit-floor refusal runs after the secondmate branch has already synced the home, created `$PROJ_ABS/state`, and propagated inherited config. A refused secondmate dispatch leaves those changes behind. They are idempotent and the EXIT trap releases the inheritance lock, so this is harmless, but moving the check above the KIND-specific setup would make a refusal free of side effects for every kind.

The credit floor applies only when the caller passes `--routing-provider openrouter`. `--routing-provider` is optional, and `fm_quota_single_provider_for_harness` in bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:96 has no `pi` entry. So a Pi DeepSeek dispatch like `--harness pi --model deepseek/deepseek-chat --routing-reason '...'` with no `--routing-provider` gets an empty ROUTING_PROVIDER and takes the `provider-unresolved` path. The floor is never checked, and after this fix round no warning is printed either. Before, it at least printed a 'provider-unresolved' warning. The user intent says the hand-written routing-reason path is the gap to close: "DeepSeek dispatches that use a hand-written routing reason skip the profile-array quota gate entirely. The ask: make the dispatch path itself refuse a dispatch on a prepaid-credit provider whose remaining balance is below a floor". Every test passes `--routing-provider openrouter` explicitly, so this path is untested. The silence matches the user's round-1 instruction ('stay silent ... when no provider resolves'), but it leaves the original failure reachable whenever firstmate omits the provider flag. Options: map pi to openrouter when the model is a DeepSeek or OpenRouter model, require `--routing-provider` with `--routing-reason` on harnesses whose provider can't be inferred, or keep the warning for an unresolved provider on pi.

The intent requires cut (4): "review limits: at most 2 review rounds then escalate to firstmate, review only what changed after the first round, and a cheaper review model (Sonnet) for low-risk changes". The diff has none of this. It contains no round cap, no escalation, no review scoped to the delta and no switch to Sonnet. The only changes are the worker context block, a price row and a teardown reorder. The intent names review as the largest single cost: $18.42 of $37.04, from 20 Opus invocations over 5 rounds. Either implement cut (4) or confirm with the product owner that it is deferred.

Workers are told to append `working: phase handoff ready ...` and end the turn, on the promise that "Firstmate relaunches this task into a fresh session". Nothing on the firstmate side acts on that line. `working:` is not in FM_CLASSIFY_CAPTAIN_RE_DEFAULT (bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:78), so the line never wakes firstmate. AGENTS.md, docs/agent-control.md and the stuck-crewmate-recovery skill never mention phase handoffs. The only reference is a row in the harness-adapter tables. Failing sequence: the worker writes phase-handoff.md, appends the working line and goes idle. The watcher absorbs the nonterminal line until the stale-wedge threshold (~240s), then escalates it as a possible wedge. Firstmate, with no instruction, treats it as a stuck worker or nudges it to continue in the same conversation. The context is never reset, so cut (1) gives no saving. Each phase boundary also adds a spurious stale wake, which inflates the stale_wake_count this same change records in the routing ledger. Fix: have the classifier and firstmate's instructions own a phase-handoff signal that triggers `fm-control.sh relaunch --note-file`. Alternatively, have the worker use a verb that wakes firstmate.

phase-handoff.md is written to the worktree root and is not gitignored. A worker that runs `git add -A` or commits at the end of a phase (often the same moment it writes the handoff) can commit the note into the PR branch. 'Remove the note before final delivery' only helps if the worker remembers, and by then the note may already be in history. Write it under an ignored path such as .git/ or a gitignored scratch directory, or add it to the worktree's exclude file at spawn time.

The intent asks for a before-and-after token breakdown. Nothing in the change produces or records one, and the brief-only cuts (1)-(3) have no measurement hook beyond the existing ledger. Confirm whether the report is delivered outside this change. Also confirm the gpt-6-sol cached_input price of $0.20/M against the published price list; gpt-6.1-sol is $0.10/M.

Workers now append `blocked: phase handoff ready <path>` at every phase boundary. bin/fm-routing-ledger.py:59 computes `blocked_count` as every status line starting with `blocked:`, and this change makes teardown preserve that count for the routing review. As a result, each routine handoff on a Codex or Claude task adds 1 to blocked_count. Example: a task with 3 phase handoffs and no real blocker records blocked_count=3. Next week's before/after review uses these ledger counts, so it will read the rise as more blockers and will not match last week's baseline. Fix: exclude the `blocked: phase handoff ready` form from blocked_count in the ledger and record it as a separate phase_handoff_count. That keeps the blocker metric comparable and also gives a measurement hook for cut (1).

`record_note` appends every relaunch note to brief.md permanently. A task with N phase handoffs therefore starts session N+1 with all N earlier handoff notes in its brief, and each new fresh session re-reads them. The growth is small next to the conversation-growth cost that cut (1) removes, but it slightly works against the goal of a minimal fresh context. A possible follow-up is to keep only the latest phase-handoff note.

The new handoff guidance (bin/fm-dod-lib.sh:138-142) tells the worker to write `$DATA/<id>/phase-handoff.md`. That is firstmate's data directory, outside the task worktree. The same ship brief's rule 2 says "Stay inside this worktree; modify nothing outside it except a private learning candidate". The scout brief's rule 2 at bin/fm-brief.sh:652 likewise lists only the report, the status file and a learning candidate as allowed outside writes. A worker following rule 2 must either skip the handoff or write the note at another path. In both cases `fm-control.sh relaunch --note-file <path>` fails with 'is not a readable file', or firstmate never gets a usable note, so cut (1) does nothing. The authorized fix asked for an ignored scratch path *in the worktree*. The fix chose the data dir instead. That still avoids the commit risk, but nobody added the matching exception to rule 2. Fix: add the phase-handoff note path to both rule-2 exception lists, next to the status file.

The changed line says "except at a planned phase handoff below". The handoff guidance comes from fm_worker_context_block inside `$(phase_protocol ship)`, which renders *above* this line. A worker looking further down the brief for the handoff instructions won't find them. Change 'below' to 'above', or drop the direction word.

The re-raise heuristic treats a matching finding ID in a different round as the same issue, and it only exempts IDs shaped like `review-N`/`rN`. The local ledger shows no-mistakes reviewers also use per-round positional IDs such as `F1`..`F5` and `R1`. So an unrelated `F1` in round 2 gets flagged `re_raised_same_issue: true` just because round 1 also had an `F1`. This inflates the 'recurring review waste' signal the curator clusters on, and it does so without any error. Fix: treat any short alphanumeric positional ID (e.g. `^[A-Za-z]{1,8}-?\d+$`) as non-identifying, or require the file to match as well as the ID.

The INSTANCE regex alternative `(?:^|\s)[\w.-]+/[\w./-]+` rejects any whitespace-preceded slash token, so general prevention text like 'check read/write paths', 'and/or', or 'client/server boundary' fails validation as 'instance-specific'. The `\b[a-f0-9]{7,40}\b` alternative also matches ordinary hex-letter words (e.g. 'defaced', 'acceded'). The curator is required to pass validate before reporting, so legitimate reusable patterns would be blocked or reworded. Fix: narrow the path rule, e.g. require a file extension or at least two slashes, and require a digit in the hex SHA rule.

A single blank or malformed line in the `--bug-cards` JSONL raises ValueError and aborts the whole extract. Because `--output` is opened (and truncated) before extraction runs, the abort leaves an empty output file. Separately, a candidate whose `captured_at` is JSON null makes `candidate.get("captured_at", "")[:10]` raise an uncaught TypeError when `--since` is set. Fix: skip blank lines and use `(candidate.get("captured_at") or "")`.

The narrowed INSTANCE regex fixes the read/write and hex-word false positives, but it introduces two small tradeoffs. First, single-slash paths without one of the listed extensions (e.g. 'bin/fm-spawn', 'src/server') are no longer caught. Second, any plain 7+ digit number (e.g. '1000000 tokens') still matches the SHA rule, because a run of digits is valid hex. The skill already says the curator must reject semantic one-offs that slip past the syntax check, so this is acceptable as a heuristic. If needed, it could be tightened later by requiring at least one a-f letter in the SHA rule.
